"This time I think it's slightly different in that I don't think the others have changed anything from Q2 to Q3," Leclerc said. "Where we have lost is on ourselves and that is mostly the tyres.

"The out lap was extremely difficult. There was a bit more cloud in Q3. We lost one or two degrees of track temp and, for us, it was night and day different and already from the out lap I felt I was having lots of difficulties.

"It's a shame that it happened in Q3 because I strongly believe that we had the pace to be fighting in front but unfortunately not today again."

Sports.title: 'Not realistic' - Can Wolff's assessment of Antonelli's title chance be trusted?
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff believes it is "not realistic" for Kimi Antonelli to win the 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship on Sunday at the United States Grand Prix, despite the Italian starting on pole position.

Antonelli was not expected to claim top spot in qualifying but produced a superb lap in Q3 to beat Red Bull's Max Verstappen and take his first pole position since July's Belgian Grand Prix.

Should Antonelli win Sunday's race in Austin with Lewis Hamilton finishing fifth or lower and George Russell ninth or lower, he will seal the title with five rounds remaining.

Hamilton will start fifth and Russell sixth when the lights go out at the Circuit of the Americas at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event.

However, Wolff has warned Mercedes will not have the pace to win as they did not have the pace in Friday practice's long runs.

"We are not talking about that [the championship]. It's not realistic," he told Sky Sports F1.

"I don't think we are quickest in the race, so it's about scoring points and eventually, hopefully, winning."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli takes pole for the United States Grand Prix

Antonelli is also wary of Red Bull's race pace and the possibility Verstappen in second and Isack Hadjar in third can also work together.

He admits this week has been "a bit different", knowing it is the first opportunity to become the sport's youngest world champion at 20 years old.

"The goal stays the same. I just need to keep doing my job, and actually, I feel like I can enjoy the driving and everything more," said Antonelli.

"But of course, we still have to do the race, still have to try and win, and then, of course, we'll see what happens. But, I feel like I can enjoy it a bit more because obviously I'm in a very good position. But still, the mindset is always the same."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 United States Grand Prix.

Verstappen plans to 'keep it respectful' against Antonelli

The uphill run towards the wide Turn 1 at the start provides a good opportunity for the driver in second to steam up the inside of the pole-sitter, something Verstappen may look to do if he has a strong getaway.

Verstappen, who has won the last two races, effectively has nothing to lose but suggested he will not be excessively aggressive against championship leader Antonelli.

"Kimi wants to go for the win right? That helps his position in the championship," he told Sky Sports F1.

"We keep it respectful and try to win the race."

Tyre degradation was high in Friday's practice sessions in Austin but that has been the case at several races this season, only for the Grand Prix to turn into a one-stop race as the teams have changed the setup on their cars and the track has gripped up over the weekend.

Nevertheless, overtaking is possible and Verstappen cut a quietly confident figure to make it a hat-trick of wins and deny any chance Antonelli has of winning the title on Sunday.

"We have been happier in the long runs, and I hope that it will be the same tomorrow," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ahead of the United States Grand Prix, Max Verstappen discusses Red Bull's Championship title aims for next season

As for Russell, it has been another tricky weekend and he faces a big challenge to overtake Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in front of him, who have both been quick in practice, to get into the podium fight.

Russell has been unable to get to grips with Mercedes' new upgrade package but admits he simply just did "two bad laps in Q3".

"I think I could have been in the top three. My Q2 lap was two and a half tenths quicker than what I achieved in Q3 but that obviously isn't good enough from my side," he told Sky Sports F1.

Asked about his race prospects, he said: "I think it's a long race, a lot happens here in Austin. Strategy plays a role so still opportunities."

Sports.title: Littler powers past Aspinall to reach European Championship quarter-finals
Sports.content:
Luke Littler remains on course to win the one major title he's never won as he beat Nathan Aspinall 10-5 in the second round of the European Championship Darts on Saturday evening.

Littler produced the second-best average in the competition's history - his 114.47 has only ever been bettered by Phil Taylor's 118.14 - as he secured an impressive victory in Dortmund.

Aspinall produced ten 180s in the match - three more than his opponent - but it wasn't enough to survive the onslaught from the world No 1, who won the first four legs of the match in 12 darts or fewer.

Aspinall briefly rallied to reduce the score to 5-4, but Littler controlled the second half of the game and, despite one brief interruption to deal with a vocal fan in the crowd, he ultimately closed out the match on D10.

"I felt really good from the off," Littler told ITV.

"I knew the start was good. I was gutted at giving him a leg and going into the first break at 4-1 when I wanted 5-0.

"Nathan is always there and is always going to come back at you. I couldn't afford to drop off. I felt confident and had to get the job done."

European Championship: Saturday's results

Round Two

Gerwyn Price 10-4 Cameron Menzies Stephen Bunting 10-3 Kim Huybrechts Ross Smith 10-7 Damon Heta Luke Woodhouse 10-6 Gian van Veen Krzysztof Ratajski 10-8 Kevin Doets Martin Schindler 10-4 Jermaine Wattimena Luke Littler 10-5 Nathan Aspinall Jonny Clayton 10-8 Josh Rock

Littler arrived at this tournament following shock defeats at the World Series of Darts and the World Grand Prix which ended his dreams of a perfect season in the majors.

However, he remains on track to win the European Championship for the first time after exiting in the last 16 of his debut campaign last year.

"I'm playing well. I'm feeling really good. There was only one issue in there, but other than that the crowd have been really good," he added.

"I've had a long time off and past results haven't gone my way. I've seen on social media some memes that 'Luke's finished' and this and that.

"I've had long enough to look at them, get on the practice board and forget about it all. Hopefully if I do lift the trophy I can say I've not gone anywhere.

"I've definitely not gone anywhere here with that performance."

Littler will face Krzysztof Ratajski in the quarter-finals after the Pole fought from behind to beat Kevin Doets 10-8.

Ratajski lost the first four legs of the match and trailed 8-6 in the closing stages before clinching four legs in a row to seal a victory over the man who stunned Michael van Gerwen in round one.

Home favourite Martin Schindler kept alive his hopes of winning the title in Dortmund as he powered to a 10-4 win over Jermaine Wattimena.

The German averaged just 90, but relied on finishing stats of more than 52 per cent - including a brilliant 121 in the ninth leg - and the support of a raucous crowd to reach the last eight on home turf for the first time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Josh Rock and Jonny Clayton have a giggle after Rock loses his dart on stage

He will face Jonny Clayton on Sunday after the Welshman beat Josh Rock 10-8 in the final match of the day.

Clayton wasted a series of match darts in the closing stages, but clinched the win in brilliant fashion with a 121 checkout on the bullseye.

Afternoon session: Van Veen's reign ended by Woodhouse

Image: Defending champion Gian van Veen suffered an early exit

In the afternoon session, Luke Woodhouse ended Gian van Veen's reign as European champion, as he coasted into the quarter-finals with a 10-6 victory.

Woody will face top seed Ross Smith on Sunday in a bid to reach the semi-final after the 2022 European champion held off a Damon Heta fightback.

A scintillating start saw Smith average in excess of 112 to storm into a 5-0 lead before Heta rallied, only to succumb to a 10-7 loss. Smith finished with six 180s and an average of 96.19.

Gerwyn Price averaged 95.75 to reach the quarter-finals for the first time in three years with a dominant 10-4 victory over Cameron Menzies, which included three ton-plus finishes.

It was tight after seven legs which all went with throw, but 'The Iceman' shifted through the gears to pull clear, winning seven of the last eight legs.

Stephen Bunting produced a finishing clinic (56 per cent) to defeat Kim Huybrechts and reach the quarter-finals for the first time since 2014.

'The Bullet' hit 10/18 on the doubles and four ton-plus checkouts to set up a blockbuster showdown with Price on Sunday.

If Price wins the title this weekend, he will provisionally be ranked higher than Luke Humphries, who withdrew from this event through illness. That would open up the possibility of a Luke vs Luke semi-final at the World Darts Championship.

Sports.title: Smith beats Puello in thriller to retain WBC title and stay unbeaten
Sports.content:
Dalton Smith retained his WBC light-welterweight title with a thrilling, split-decision victory over Alberto Puello on Saturday night.

On his homecoming at Utilita Arena, the Sheffield man was taken the distance in his first title defence, but kept his unbeaten record in tact as judges Kieran McCann of England and Spain's Jon Llona both scored the bout 115-113 in his favour, while Filipino Ray Danseco had it 116-112 to Puello.

Puello - is a former WBA and WBC champion - suffered only his second defeat in 27 fights. Smith has won 20 from 20, including beating Subriel Matias in New York in January - who inflicted Puello's only previous loss - to become world champion.

The 29-year-old had been due to fight mandatory challenger Puello four months sooner in June, but an injury to the Dominican Republic fighter resulted in a postponenment.

Smith, speaking to DAZN after retaining his title, said: "We knew what we were coming in for, he's a two-time world champion [and] look at the names he's beat.

"We knew it wasn't going to be a show, he was going to be an awkward opponent, but a champion has to do what he has to do.

"These are the best in the world and I'm proving why I'm number one now."

He added: "I got his rhythm early on. I think he respected my power, but, look, he's experienced.

"He's a lot more experienced than me, and that's what I'm gaining now. I switched off a little bit in the early rounds, but I did what a true champion did and win the last couple, so I'm very proud."

Sports.title: Alonso urges Cole Palmer ‘to learn’ from red card in Chelsea’s defeat to Spurs
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso said that Cole Palmer must learn from his red card during Chelsea’s shock 2-0 defeat to Tottenham, who claimed their first win at Stamford Bridge since 2018 thanks to an own goal from Mike Penders and a late effort from Mathys Tel.

Spurs, who had won on one of their previous 34 trips to west London, were already 1-0 up when Palmer earned a second yellow card for catching Conor Gallagher with a late tackle. The playmaker could have been sent off earlier – his first booking came during a clash with Mateus Fernandes – and Alonso agreed that this could be an important lesson for the 24-year-old.

“Absolutely,” Chelsea’s manager said. “I haven’t seen them [back] on TV but as far as I have been told probably he [the referee] got it right. We need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments. When you have conceded for 1-0, still probably it was 15-20 minutes to go. I need to check the action to talk with Cole but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer clashes with Mateus Fernandes, earning his first yellow card. Photograph: Isabel Infantes/Reuters

Alonso said there are no wider concerns with Palmer’s character, even though Chelsea’s No 10 could have been sent off against Everton last weekend too. “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a concern,” Alonso said. “It is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature, for everyone.”

Chelsea struggled without João Pedro and do not know when the forward will return after picking up an unspecified injury in training on Friday. “He has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “He felt it yesterday and we need to wait to do the test and to know the whole seriousness of the injury.”

Alonso defended Penders after the goalkeeper punched a corner into his own net on his full Premier League debut. “We win, we lose together,” he said. “We support Mike and we support the rest of the team. He will learn from that.”

Roberto De Zerbi hopes that Spurs can use this victory as a springboard. “Why not?” the Spurs manager said. “There is no reason why not. I can’t understand why we have to ask this question. Because we won two games in a row. But we didn’t win nothing. We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough.”

Sports.title: Clinical Arsenal earn precious win against Everton thanks to Konsa and Gabriel
Sports.content:
The wait goes on for David Moyes. The 63-year-old Scot must have been hoping that on his 14th visit to this stadium as Everton’s manager, his luck would change. Yet from the moment Ezri Konsa slammed home his first goal for Arsenal as the Premier League champions rediscovered their knack of scoring from set pieces, the writing was on the wall.

While it took until midway through the second half for Gabriel Magalhães to make sure of the victory, Arsenal were never going to let slip the chance of moving level on points at the top with Manchester City after their defeat by Aston Villa earlier in the day.

Asked whether it was strange that his side are again going toe-to-toe with their great rivals but with the added uncertainty of what punishment City will receive after being found guilty of 115 charges by the Premier League, Mikel Arteta said: “[We are] just focusing on what we can do. We are very pleased with 90% of the results and performances that we have.”

This was hardly a vintage performance from the clinical home side after a testing week but it did not need to be against opponents who offered precious little in attack, even if they defended for their lives at times.

Having gone six matches without defeat to start the season, a second in succession will only add to Everton’s concerns after confirmation that the club’s American owners want out.

“It was always going to be hard after conceding the early goal,” said Moyes, whose solitary victory at the Emirates was as West Ham’s manager in 2023. “I want us to challenge the top teams but it’s difficult when you see the strength of their bench.”

Everton’s record at this stadium is almost as bad as their manager’s. They arrived in north London having won twice in 35 matches here and had to do without Jarrad Branthwaite and Jack Grealish, who was ruled out with illness. It did not bode well for them when Arsenal took the lead in the seventh minute with a third corner in succession.

View image in fullscreen Ezri Konsa (No 15) squeezes the ball home for Arsenal’s early first goal against Everton. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Gabriel made the crucial first contact at the near post and Jordan Pickford tipped the ball on to the crossbar, only for Vitaliy Mykolenko’s failed clearance under pressure from Viktor Gyökeres to allow Konsa to ram home from close range. After a record-breaking 25 goals from set pieces last season, it was their first of this campaign.

It was a measure of Arsenal’s exertions against Bayern Munich on Wednesday that Arteta rotated his side more than usual for a Premier League match, making five changes.

Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke spurned good opportunities to extend the lead in front of the watching England head coach, Thomas Tuchel. The latter was left out of the last squad, but could well benefit from Bukayo Saka’s expected long absence due to a thigh injury. He was inches away with an instinctive effort with his right foot from the edge of the area on the half-hour mark and was consistently Arsenal’s most dangerous threat.

Everton must have feared the worst as yet another Arsenal corner – 10 during the first half – was launched into the area. Yet the defence just about stood firm.

A moment’s lapse of concentration from Ben White just before half-time almost gave Everton an equaliser but Thierno Barry could not get enough on his attempt to flick the ball past David Raya in their clearest opening.

Gyökeres looked determined to make an impression on his first Premier League start of the season but the Sweden striker, who has yet to score for his club this term, looked laboured.

Quick Guide Arsenal 2-0 Everton key facts Show • With both Arsenal and Manchester City doing so this season, this is just the third top-flight campaign to have two teams win at least seven of their opening eight matches after 1892-93 (Preston and Sunderland) and 1913-14 (Blackburn and Manchester United). • This was David Moyes’s 400th defeat across all competitions in his managerial career with all clubs. 31 of these have come against Arsenal, more than against any other opponent. • The opener from Ezri Konsa (pictured celebrating) was Arsenal’s first set piece goal (excluding penalties) since May against Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one. Opta Photograph: Adam Davy/PA Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

He could not believe it when Tony Harrington penalised him for a foul on James Tarkowski and a sheepish Arteta earned himself a booking for protesting. Unsurprisingly, Gyökeres’ number was up soon after as Arsenal turned to their bench.

It took less than 60 seconds for Gabriel to head in at the back post as White offered Tuchel a timely reminder of his qualities with a brilliant cross.

Moyes’ frustration meant he joined Arteta in the referee’s notebook. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall could have made things interesting but his header fizzed just wide of a post.

Arsenal are now breathing down City’s necks, although whether this title race lasts the course remains unknown.

Sports.title: Fulham climb out of drop zone after Oscar Bobb’s late show sinks Coventry
Sports.content:
Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a win against Coventry that lifted Álvaro Arbeloa’s side clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to score in the 80th minute, twisting his way into the area and bending a shot into the far corner. It was his second goal for the club since his £27m move from Manchester City in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by beating Hull 1-0.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s team second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon that bought the Coventry fans back down to earth after their 4-1 win against Newcastle in their previous home match.

“I think we are improving as a team,” Arbeloa said. “We are competing for 90 minutes. I talked to the players. It’s not about if we play well for 60 minutes or 30 minutes, we need to understand that you need to compete for 90 minutes.

“Understand the game, understand what you have to do. Sometimes you need to defend your box, sometimes you will control the game.

“Sometimes you need to win because of the quality of your players. I think it was a good game as a team but at the end the quality of Oscar in one moment decides the game.”

Quality was in short supply between two teams who started the day in the bottom three. King should have broken the deadlock in the 18th minute when afforded too much space in the box, but his powerful shot rebounded off the top of the upright before Alex Iwobi sent a wild follow-up effort high and wide.

At the other end, Bobby Thomas met Jack Rudoni’s free-kick but got his angles all wrong as he headed well wide, before Brandon Thomas-Asante missed from Jay Dasilva’s cross after a good run forward from Rudoni.

A mis-hit back pass from Antonee Robinson offered Thomas-Asante another chance but his shot lacked power as Leno easily gathered.

View image in fullscreen Ephron Mason-Clark is denied by the Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno. Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock

While Coventry were piling up half-chances Fulham were the ones bossing possession but, in keeping with their season so far, struggling to turn that dominance into goals. The Coventry defender Milan van Ewijk almost helped them out, deflecting Robinson’s low cross dangerously close to his own goal as it found the side-netting.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Just before the break Calvin Bassey went down in the box claiming a shirt-pull from Thomas-Asante, but the referee Adam Herczeg waved play on with replays suggesting they each had a hold of the other.

The video assistant referee had taken a look, and was involved again early in the second half when Rudoni’s free-kick from the right struck Iwobi on the arm before he cleared, but the Nigerian’s arms were by his side and play was waved on.

Coventry then suffered a major blow when the in-form Thomas, praised by Lampard in midweek, hobbled off just before the hour, replaced by the teenage Manchester City loanee Stephen Mfuni.

The hosts were starting to build some momentum after a series of substitutions but it swiftly ended as Bobb struck with 10 minutes to go.

Coventry tried to respond but a powerful strike from Matt Grimes was blocked and a late penalty appeal for handball against Shea Charles was waved away with the midfielder having had his arm tucked in.

“If it ends 0-0, I think both say fair play,” Lampard said. “Fulham are a good team, they’ve been creating a lot of chances – you can see why. They didn’t give us massive problems around our box but they found a moment of quality that we couldn’t find.

“We didn’t have any real zip at the top end of the pitch, so that’s disappointing. Sometimes it can happen. This is the Premier League. They’re trying to stop you and if you want more it’s not always there. We’ve got to keep pushing on.”

Sports.title: Relief for Slegers as Russo rescues Arsenal against Tottenham in WSL
Sports.content:
Alessia Russo’s contentious second-half penalty delivered relief, a reprieve and a chance for a reset as Arsenal came from a goal down to earn their second win of the WSL season in the north London derby.

At a rain-lashed Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Gunners were again their own worst enemy, forced to come from behind after Cathinka Tandberg’s headed opener. Georgia Stanway levelled and Russo powered in the penalty that gave them the lead they protected defiantly.

The Tottenham manager, Martin Ho, queried the penalty decision, with the ball hitting the raised arm of substitute Ella Morris from the clearance of one of her teammates. “My interpretation of the rule is if your teammate hits it and it hits your player, if you’re one yard away, the time and distance is taken into account, so there’s no penalty,” he said. “That’s my understanding of it, from when we were told to start the season. I want to understand what they’re saying, because then I can accept the decision.

“I don’t want the game to be about that, but when it decides a game it’s frustrating because it’s not within the law of the game.”

Arsenal’s manager, Renée Slegers, said she was glad to give the fans a win. “They sing us and fight us through the game,” she said. “At the end it’s scrappy, it’s game management and it’s scenarios, and they’re all with us.”

With the pressure building on her and her players after five games without a win, at times it felt like they were trying to disprove the phrase “you can’t dig yourself out of a hole”.

Quick Guide Brighton cruise to victory against West Ham Show Maisie Symonds’ first-half stunner sent Brighton on their way to a 3-0 win against West Ham at the Amex Stadium. The midfielder Symonds’ thunderbolt gave the Seagulls a half-time lead before Fran Kirby and Kiko Seike struck quickfire goals midway through the second period. It was a first clean sheet this season for Arturo Ruiz’s side and lifts them up to eighth in the table, two points above West Ham, who slipped to 12th after their fifth league defeat of the campaign. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Arsenal had looked a little shaky in the opening few minutes but they settled, built possession and started to pose a threat. A failure to carve out clearcut chances and capitalise on any period of dominance has been the running theme of their season. They lacked fight and there was sloppiness too, with too many overhit passes putting the ball out of play or giving away possession.

That the opener came from a Tottenham corner was unsurprising. Victoria Pelova swung the ball in and Tandberg rose above her two markers, Stanway and Emily Fox, who failed to even to jump and challenge, and headed home.

Spurs’ joy was short lived as Stanway made up for her marking error four minutes later by arriving to meet Russo’s cut back and powered the ball in off the crossbar.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Georgia Stanway equalises for Arsenal in the 17th minute. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

After the break there was concern for Tottenham when Alice Sombath’s leg seemed to twist awkwardly as she stretched for the ball. The club’s record signing left on a stretcher to be replaced by Morris, who made her return from an anterior cruciate ligament injury towards the end of last season.

After the lengthy stoppage, Russo forced a huge save from Lize Kop as she attempted to turn in Caitlin Foord’s cross from close range, the forward putting her hands to her head and screaming in frustration at the missed opportunity.

It did not take long for that frustration to transform into elation. The resulting corner from Kyra Cooney-Cross was headed on by Leah Williamson at the near post and Lisa Baum’s effort came back off the post. Spurs’ clearance bounced off the raised arm of Morris and the referee pointed to the spot. Russo sent Kop the wrong way and drove the ball low into the corner.

Arsenal were clinging on as the final whistle loomed but they had “found their fight,” said Slegers. “We had a run of games where results haven’t been good enough. It was frustrating for everyone. I’m so happy we got to win on this occasion, in the north London derby, away from home in the rain and we showed that character in the team.

“This will definitely energise us. We need to back this up in the next couple of games.”

Sports.title: Maresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless start
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season.

Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend.

“No, I’m not worried about Marc at all,” Maresca said. “I know that he’s played every minute since the season started with us, with the international team, so it’s not easy. But again, the change was also because he was on a yellow card and in the way we want to be aggressive, sometimes to have one yellow card can be dangerous, but I’m not worried at all.”

City had 15 shots to Villa’s eight as they dropped points for the first time this season. Zion Suzuki made a number of important saves to keep City at bay in the second half, and Villa scored with their only two shots on target.

“I think we deserved more from the game, for the amount of chances that we created and for the chances that we conceded,” Maresca said. “We lost because probably we have not been clinical enough in their box and sometimes when you concede the first goal because of the mistake, the second goal again comes from transition in 45 minutes. It’s difficult to avoid that every time, but we learn from the game and we try to move on and to improve.”

View image in fullscreen Nicolas Jackson scores Aston Villa’s first goal past Gianluigi Donnarumma. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

Jackson’s double takes him to seven goals since his move from Chelsea. He was a constant threat to the City centre-backs, who were unable to cope with his speed, physical presence and clinical finishing. Unai Emery said of his forward: “He’s very demanding of himself to improve things. Today he scored two goals, in the last matches he scored goals – but at the beginning of the season, what happened to us was more difficult and he was shooting a lot of balls over the corner.

“Now, he’s getting better at shooting. He’s working fantastically tactically, he’s understanding as well where we need him. Today, he scored two goals, but the most important thing is how he did his work, his task.”

His fellow summer signing Suzuki challenged Jackson for the player of the match award and is starting to show why Villa were so keen to acquire him as Emiliano Martínez’s replacement. Matty Cash told TNT Sport: “He’s brilliant, his first session when he came in, in the possession drill I thought we’d signed a midfielder. His vision is unbelievable, he catches crosses really well which as a full-back is a dream.”

Sports.title: European football: Lazio beat Parma to top Serie A; Dortmund lead Bundesliga
Sports.content:
Lazio climbed to the top of Serie A with a 2-1 home win ⁠over Parma ⁠as Roma ​twice came from behind to secure a 3-3 draw with Napoli in a pulsating clash in Naples.

Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this ⁠season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor ⁠struck his first of the season, before Parma’s Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying ​to cut out a cross. The visitors scored a ‌late consolation through Simone Lontani.

Third-placed Roma ‌trailed 2-0 and then 3-2 late on, so will be pleased with a point in Naples as they preserved ‌their 15-game unbeaten league run that dates back to April. Frank Anguissa’s spectacular overhead kick gave Napoli the lead and Scott McTominay doubled the advantage.

At that stage they were cruising, but two goals in four minutes from Matías Soulé and Leonardo Balerdi drew Roma level. When McTominay added his second in the closing stages the momentum swung back in Napoli’s favour, but Balerdi headed an equaliser for Roma with a minute remaining.

“We maintained ‌roles, positions and our way of playing,” said the Roma coach, Gian Piero Gasperini. “The goals were of quality. We are fine [with the result], with high morale. Balerdi knows football, has extraordinary ​energy and has been a great signing for us.”

Como backed up their Champions League victory over Manchester United as Anastasios Douvikas scored twice in 11 minutes for a 2-0 win against Sassuolo. They climbed to fourth in the table.

In Germany, Maximilian Beier scored in the 80th minute to send Borussia Dortmund top of the Bundesliga table after a hard-fought 1-0 home win over Eintracht Frankfurt.

In a game lacking clear chances, Jobe Bellingham came off the bench and threaded a clever pass for his fellow substitute Beier to score less than a minute later. The narrow victory was Dortmund’s first in the league since mid-September and took Niko Kovac’s side three points clear at the top.

Bayern Munich can return to the top with a win at Freiburg on Sunday but will be without their coach, Vincent Kompany, who is being treated in hospital for a mystery virus after collapsing at training on Friday.

Niclas Füllkrug scored for the sixth straight Bundesliga match as Werder Bremen won 3-2 at Mainz. Füllkrug, who returned to Bremen on loan from West Ham in the summer, converted two penalties inside the opening 25 minutes. Ludovit Reis grabbed Bremen’s other goal, while Anthony Caci and Lee Jae-sung scored for the hosts.

View image in fullscreen Niclas Füllkrug (third left) celebrates after scoring his side’s second against Mainz. Photograph: Florian Wiegand/DPA/AP

RB Leipzig completed a comfortable 4-0 home win over promoted Elversberg. Romulo scored twice while Tidiam Gomis and Christoph Baumgartner also got on the scoresheet. Paderborn’s Rayan Philippe scored in the 88th minute against Hamburg, his parent club, to grab the promoted side a 1-0 victory. Augsburg drew 1-1 with Union Berlin as both sides finished with 10 men. Cologne and Schalke played out a scoreless draw in a match marred by a head clash between the visitor’s Robin Gosens and Soufiane El-Faouzi, who left the field after a first-half collision.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In La Liga, Atlético Madrid kept up the pressure at the top with a 1-0 win over Deportivo A Coruña at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano. Julián Alvarez struck three minutes into the second half as Diego Simeone’s side extended their unbeaten run to eight matches in all competitions and moved within two points of leaders Barcelona ahead of El Clasico on Sunday.

Georges Mikautadze, meanwhile, snatched a late 2-1 win for Villarreal in their derby against Valencia, who had Harvey Elliott sent off as both sides finished with 10 men. The visitors came from behind to triumph, leaving Javier Aguirre’s side 19th.

View image in fullscreen Harvey Elliott, on loan at Valencia from Liverpool, was sent off in the 89th minute against Villarreal. Photograph: Maria Jose Segovia/DeFodi Images/Shutterstock

Pepelu put Valencia ahead from the penalty spot in the first half before the American defender Alex Freeman headed the visitors level after 69 minutes. Iñigo Pérez’s Villarreal had Pape Gueye sent off when the Senegal international hit José Gayà in the face with his elbow.

However, Elliott, who is on loan from Liverpool, was soon dismissed for two quick yellow cards for apparent dissent. Mikautadze broke through in stoppage time, racing through and finishing with aplomb to claim the three points.

In France, Lens came from behind to beat Paris FC 2-1 ⁠with Thorgan Hazard’s 83rd-minute winner taking them to within a point of the Ligue 1 leaders. Lens, who ⁠were runners-up last season, ⁠made ​a slow start to the season and fired coach Dino Toppmöller after six matches in charge, but under ⁠Yannick Cahuzac they have won successive French league games to advance to 13 points from eight matches. They are one ⁠point behind five clubs who share the lead on 14, including Paris ​FC.

Sports.title: Burnley sack Nicky Hayen after Lincoln rout leaves them in bottom three
Sports.content:
Burnley have sacked Nicky Hayen after only 14 games in charge, in the wake of a 4-1 defeat at Lincoln that left the Clarets in the Championship’s relegation zone.

The Belgian was appointed in the summer as the permanent successor to Scott Parker, who left in April with relegation from the Premier League inevitable. He leaves having won just one match, a 4-0 league victory at Watford on 10 October.

Burnley edged past Notts County on penalties in the Carabao Cup in his first match in charge and recovered in the last seven minutes from 2-0 down to draw at home to West Ham in their opening game of the Championship season. However, they then lost badly at West Brom and Norwich, sandwiching a shootout exit from the Carabao Cup at Bradford, and the pattern was set.

Burnley were fancied to push for promotion, which was achieved in their past two Championship seasons, but are now at risk of relegation. Wolves’ come-from-behind win at Turf Moor last weekend left Hayen on the brink and now the club have acted.

A terse, two-sentence statement on the club website said: “Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect. The board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season.”

Hayen had earlier said in his post-match press conference, before news of his dismissal emerged: “It’s frustrating for everyone, especially the fans. I want to apologise to them, but I know it doesn’t matter because it’s another hard defeat for them and I can understand their criticism.

“We haven’t got the results. I will keep on working hard as long as I have the chance. But there will be a day if it carries on like this that it stops. I know it’s a really tough defeat and something to think about for the board.”

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Kelsy fires Rangers to emphatic win; Dundee United pip Aberdeen
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 Premiership win at Ibrox. After dropping two points at Dundee last Saturday, the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from the Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy.

Saints started the second half brightly but goals from the Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. The Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on the midfielder Nico Raskin, before the substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining.

McInnes said: “It’s quite ironic in the sense that we were so good and so brilliant at times in the first half and create so many opportunities, that we were only a goal to the good at half-time. And obviously, we don’t want to let the frustration of those missed opportunities and dominance filter into the second half.

“I think half-time came at a bad time for us because, despite the conditions, some of the play was really good. I asked the players to be brilliant today, not just win the game, can we really commit to being the best we can be, as good as we can be? And I thought we were in the first half. Everything was brilliant except the result at half-time because we should have been more in in front.”

Celtic can restore their four-point advantage over Rangers at the top when they travel to Hibernian, the bottom side, at noon GMT on Sunday.

Dundee United won a rollercoaster game 3-2 against Aberdeen at Tannadice. Zidane Iqbal scored for the hosts before the visitors equalised through Nesta Guinness-Walker – both players scoring their first goals for their clubs.

United took the lead once more thanks to a Dylan Tait strike, with Connor Ronan drawing Aberdeen level after the break. Zac Sapsford secured all three points for his side, with the win moving United up to fourth – one point behind Hearts, who are at Motherwell on Sunday – while Aberdeen dropped to ninth.

Two own goals helped Falkirk climb to seventh with a 3-0 victory over Kilmarnock. Centre-backs Cathal McCarthy and George Stanger scored past their own goalkeeper either side of a Jacob Murrell header. St Mirren ended their losing streak with a 2-1 victory over Dundee with goals from Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule before Bradley Fink pulled one back for the visitors.

Sports.title: Kimi Antonelli secures pole in Austin to boost chances of becoming world champion at US Grand Prix amid F1 calendar chaos
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli secures pole in Austin to boost chances of becoming world champion at US Grand Prix amid F1 calendar chaos

Pole for Kimi Antonelli under the Texan sun. And so there is a decent chance this breezy, curly-haired kid could become world champion today, the youngest ever at 20, without anyone knowing it’s a fact for sure.

The Mercedes man’s elevation to the top step in only his second season appears the strongest of possibilities – but with a strange caveat attached.

For the timing of his honour is complicated because it is unclear how many rounds remain on the calendar. Owing to conflict in the Middle East doubts surround the viability of the two intended concluding grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

So, should they fall off the roster, with only Imola lined up as a single replacement, Antonelli’s current 102-point lead over crestfallen team-mate George Russell, who qualified sixth, if maintained or extended here, would be insurmountable in a reduced schedule of four rounds.

Antonelli would be two points beyond reach whatever anyone else can muster over the next few weeks. In other words, he would be champion, yet awaiting his official coronation.

Everything is falling his way and the Italian is capitalising with clinical precision. His pole by 0.179sec over Red Bull’s Max Verstappen demonstrated his gifts again. Isaak Hadjar will start third, Charles Leclerc fourth and Lewis Hamilton fifth – a bad afternoon for Ferrari given their major upgrade package and big hopes of taking a leap forward.

Kimi Antonelli (centre) was fastest in qualifying ahead of Max Verstappen (left) and Isack Hadjar (right) in Austin

My own hunch, for what it is worth, is that the Middle Eastern races will be called off, that Formula One’s insistence that they will be on is fanciful, that they are placating their friendly and well-heeled friends in the region for now, and that, lo and behold, Imola will host what will turn into a late November/early December party to celebrate Italy’s first world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

What better script could there be for the local boy born in Bologna, 20 miles up the road? Just don’t let on for now.

Antonelli, rightly, is doing his calculations according to the syllabus before him. If the last two races are on, the arithmetic reads like this: having won eight out of 17 races, he has two theoretical ‘rivals’, Russell and Hamilton, a huge 111 points back.

If Antonelli leaves Austin 125 points ahead of them both today he will clinch the honours regardless of the scheduling permutations. For that to happen, he needs to win and Russell to finish ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower at the Circuit of the Americas, this great, undulating track 15 miles southeast of Downtown Austin, with its music scene and packed bars.

‘It’s crazy if you think about the championship, and that’s why I won’t think about it,’ said Antonelli, whose potential success would eclipse Sebastian Vettel as the sport’s youngest title-holder. The then precocious German was aged 23 years and 134 days, back in 2010, at Red Bull.

‘Something catastrophic needs to happen to others for me to become champion this weekend.

‘We had a meeting with ‘Bono’ (race engineer Peter Bonnington, who has enjoyed his role as mentor to the young Antonelli) this morning and we said: “Just have fun.”’

Antonelli took over the seat of the world’s ‘most winningest’ driver – as they say this side of the Pond – namely Hamilton’s when he moved to Ferrari last season.

Antonelli could become world champion at the US Grand Prix on Sunday

The pair get on well, as role-model and apprentice, and Hamilton paid this tribute to the man-child he knows will follow him into sporting history, having nurtured his progress since Antonelli joined Mercedes on the Silver Arrows’ young driver programme aged 11.

‘He doesn’t need any advice,’ said the seven-time world champion. ‘He’s shown this year and also last year, but particularly this year, just his talent and his ability, his calmness in approach.

‘I’m so proud of the way he’s carried himself, how he interacts with the drivers, even with the media. If it’s not my team winning, I’d always say I want to see my old team do well.’

The final word to Antonelli and his dreams on the eve of a significant Sunday in his nascent career.

‘I have wanted to win the title since I was little,’ he admitted, for once throwing off his pragmatic blinkers. ‘But there’s still a bit to go.’

How far is anyone’s guess. It could all be over today, bizarrely, without us or him knowing it.

Sports.title: Inside Trent Alexander-Arnold's Real Madrid struggles: How injury setbacks and Jose Mourinho's indifference - despite flashes of 'awesome' brilliance and Kylian Mbappe's backing - have left fallen star at a career crossroads
Sports.content:
Inside Trent Alexander-Arnold's Real Madrid struggles: How injury setbacks and Jose Mourinho's indifference - despite flashes of 'awesome' brilliance and Kylian Mbappe's backing - have left fallen star at a career crossroads

One of the cruellest realities as to the debate around Trent Alexander-Arnold and his lost genius is that, in Madrid, no such debate exists. While we search for answers, those in Spain have little interest in the question.

That is where the 28-year-old finds himself heading into Sunday’s El Clasico, a match that monopolises every column inch and conversation in the Spanish media. This week, that coverage has not bothered much with Alexander-Arnold. He is Real Madrid’s third-choice right back. He is not a Galactico.

Yet, we continue to wonder what has happened, and what will happen, to our fallen star. It was six years ago when I spoke to Cafu about Brazil and World Cups. He wanted to talk about Alexander-Arnold.

'He can take the position of right back to another level,’ said the greatest right back in the history of the game.

‘I think we've started changing the narrative (because of Alexander-Arnold), with the way people view full backs. It's not just the goalscorer who should be the best player in the world. It is totally wrong that some great players never won the Ballon d'Or because of their position. Nowadays, full backs should be seen as the main protagonists in the game.’

And, for a while after, Alexander-Arnold was exactly that. He was spoken about as a Ballon d’Or contender. In 2022, he was voted in the top 25 players. Even in the summer of 2025, when he joined Real from Liverpool, there was hope, at least here, that his undeniable gifts would flourish once more.

Trent Alexander-Arnold's career is at a crossroads despite his high-profile move to Madrid

He joined the Spanish club to much fanfare but is an indifferent figure among fans

Such enthusiasm, however, has never really been shared in the Spanish capital. Jose Mourinho’s indifference towards the Scouser has echoes of Thomas Tuchel with England, and Alexander-Arnold’s managers, it would appear, see more of the flaws as opposed to the brilliance that once blinded us to the former. Mourinho is his third boss at the Bernabeu.

Terry Gibson, formerly of Wimbledon and Manchester United, has covered Spanish football for two decades and will be commentating on Sunday’s game for La Liga TV. Like him, he expects Alexander-Arnold to be on the sidelines.

‘He has never been regarded as a major, superstar signing,’ Gibson told me this week. ‘Even when he joined, the hope was that Dani Carvajal would be fit and play ahead of him. Then, when Carvajal left this summer, they signed Denzel Dumfries. But the bigger problem now is that Mourinho has moved Federico Valverde, a midfielder, to right back.

‘I had to smile last Sunday night. Valverde started and then Mourinho put Eder Militao at right back late on. The camera cut to Dumfries and Alexander-Arnold on the bench and they looked at each other as if to say, “I thought this was our competition”.’

They are still in competition, but only for the role of back up to Valverde.

‘In my opinion, Jose is fudging it a little bit in order to get his captain in the team,’ says Gibson. ‘But that’s the reality of it for Alexander-Arnold now. The supporters are kind of indifferent to him. They’re nonplussed about whether he stays, goes, plays or whatever. That’s sad. It’s also a crying shame that of all the top coaches he’s worked with, none of them have been able to improve him defensively. He’s 28 now, so that’s not going to change.

‘At times, some of the stuff he’s done here has been awesome. His last match against Villarreal (October 10) I thought was one of his best performances for Real. His set-pieces were brilliant, his cross-field balls. Then, just after half-time, Mourinho took him off when there was no need and we haven’t seen him since. He’ll play against the lesser teams at home, maybe, but we shouldn’t expect to see much of him in the bigger games.’

In Alexander-Arnold’s defence - and, as ever, this is an argument about his attacking merits - sources in Spain say that Kylian Mbappe loves playing with him. There was one trademark cross during a 4-0 home win over Malaga in August that laid on a goal for the France striker, and they had also swapped passes in the build-up. But this speaks to Gibson’s observation - trialled in the smaller ones, not trusted in the bigger ones.

Jose Mourinho prefers Federico Valverde at right back, with Alexander-Arnold third choice

The Englishman is 28 and has a decision to make over his footballing future

There was one headline in Spain this month, on the day of his birthday, that read: ‘Trent turns 28 without Mourinho's confidence.’ History tells us, Mourinho’s support is not easy to regain.

A week earlier, during the international break and following Alexander-Arnold’s surprise recall by Tuchel, Madrid newspaper AS observed: ‘England reveals the best of Trent.’ Again, though, this was at home to Czech Republic in a routine 3-0 win. He did not feature against Spain.

Indeed, some cynics suspected that, at least in part, Tuchel’s motivation in selecting Alexander-Arnold in the squad was to divert conversation from the continued fallout of England’s World Cup exit and the head coach's part in that. His playing time with England, you suspect, will be just as limited as in Madrid.

Injuries have not helped in Spain, and data shows he missed 23 Real fixtures last season.

‘He missed a real opportunity,’ says Gibson. ‘Because if he’d stayed fit, that position was there for the taking. So he’s not guilty of doing anything wrong, really. He's never received too much criticism. He's never received too much praise.’

That conversation with Cafu seems like a long time ago now. But as for the next six years, Alexander-Arnold has a decision to make. Because those who make the decisions in Madrid have probably decided he is not for them.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer 'lost his head' in Chelsea's defeat by Spurs: Gary Neville hits out at Blues star after sending off and claims Morgan Rogers should also have seen red
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer 'lost his head' in Chelsea's defeat by Spurs: Gary Neville hits out at Blues star after sending off and claims Morgan Rogers should also have seen red

Gary Neville has claimed Cole Palmer 'lost his head' after the Chelsea star was sent off for two quick yellow cards in the defeat by Spurs on Saturday.

Palmer was booked after shoving Mateus Fernandes to the ground before being given his marching orders for what Neville called a 'very naughty' challenge on Conor Gallagher just minutes later.

His dismissal came after Chelsea had fallen behind when Mike Penders inadvertently punched the ball into his own net from a corner.

Ten-man Chelsea's misery was compounded as Mathys Tel doubled Spurs' lead late on as Roberto De Zerbi's side became only the second Tottenham team to win at Stamford Bridge in 36 years.

Speaking on Sky Sports during the game, Neville said: 'Cole Palmer has lost his head. To do that five minutes after the challenge on Fernandes is just silly.

'He sticks his studs in on him, he knows exactly what he's doing. It's not a good challenge. It is naughty, very naughty. He's experienced enough to know.'

Cole Palmer was sent off for two quick yellow cards in Chelsea's defeat by Spurs on Saturday

Neville said Palmer was fortunate not to see red for the push on Fernandes with the Blues forward furious at the midfielder's deliberate handball.

'Why has Palmer done that? I'm not sure why he reacts,' Neville said.

'Fernandes has handballed it and it's a clear yellow card. Palmer's reaction looks silly. He's asking for trouble.'

A frustrated Morgan Rogers was then booked in the dying moments for kicking Gallagher, a challenge Neville felt should have seen Chelsea reduced to nine.

'I think that's a red. I do,' Neville said.

'He's absolutely wellied him with no intent. That's ludicrous from Rogers. They have lost it. Xabi Alonso needs to get them off.'

Palmer will be available for Chelsea's next league game, at home to Manchester United on Saturday, despite the red card as he will serve his suspension when Alonso's men travel to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday.

Sports.title: 76ers fans brutally boo halftime performer for underwhelming act at LeBron James' first home game
Sports.content:
LeBron James got the full Philadelphia experience in his 'home' debut for the 76ers on Thursday night.

Not only did his new fans shower the Sixers with boos as they fell behind the Cleveland Cavaliers by 27 points in the second quarter, but the jeers continued after the horn as spectators turned on the halftime entertainment.

Known as 'Light Man,' the performer wore an LED costume while balancing glowing objects on his hands as a small array of luminous drones floated around him.

Perhaps it was the routine, or maybe it was the 24-point halftime deficit, but the locals did not hide their displeasure.

'When the Sixers are down 24, this talented, creative gentleman got booed for a big portion of his act,' ESPN's Mike Breen said over highlights of the halftime show.

'They're just not in a frame of mind,' color commentator Richard Jefferson responded.

Known as 'Light Man,' the performer wore an LED costume while balancing glowing objects on his hands as a small array of luminous drones floated around him. Fans were not impressed

James and Tyrese Maxey (left) celebrate as the Sixers come back from 27 down vs Cavaliers

It’s unclear if he was booing, but 76ers legend Allen Iverson (sunglasses) was on hand and appeared to be sitting just a few seats down from James’ young daughter, Zhuri (far left)

'He'll get another chance,' Breen said, adding: 'Hopefully.'

Fans online were equally dismissive.

'Yeah, no patience for a guy with drones spinning a box when they're down 29,' one Sixers fan later wrote on X before dropping the name of a more popular halftime performer. 'He's no Red Panda.'

Others remarked on Philadelphians' commitment to booing.

'Philly booing the Sixers AND the halftime performer in the same night is wild,' one commenter noted on X. 'You came to watch the show and you booed the whole show.'

But things would improve in the second half as the Cavs went cold from the perimeter while the Sixers frontcourt of James, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid began dominating the paint.

In the end, Philadelphia came away with 114-106 win to improve to 2-0 in the James era.

Obviously, Light Man is in some good company when it comes to being booed by Philadelphians. Most famously, the city booed Santa Claus during an Eagles game at Franklin Field in 1968.

It’s unclear if he was booing, but 76ers legend Allen Iverson was on hand Thursday and appeared to be sitting just a few seats down from James’ young daughter, Zhuri.

James, meanwhile, was scratched from Saturday's game against Milwaukee to rest up ahead of Sunday's matchup with the visiting Detroit Pistons.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick reveals private chats with Sir Alex Ferguson and Ole Gunner Solskjaer as under-pressure Man United boss tells fans they will see a 'different team' against Bournemouth after Como capitulation
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is in regular contact with Sir Alex Ferguson and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer as he fights to survive Manchester United’s disastrous start to the season.

Carrick is under huge pressure going into Sunday’s game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford after a run of seven games without a win.

United have made their worst start to a league season in 40 years since Ferguson was brought in to replace Ron Atkinson, and Carrick apologised to fans in Como in midweek after the club’s heaviest defeat in Europe since 1994.

The 45-year-old gave an impassioned speech before his press conference at Carrington on Friday, in which he summoned the spirit of Ferguson by calling on everyone at United to put the club first, and later revealed that he has been speaking regularly to the legendary Old Trafford boss.

Carrick, who was first-team coach under Solskjaer and beat him to the job of head coach in January, has also been in close contact with the Norwegian.

Michael Carrick says he is spoken with Ole Gunner Solskjaer (left) and Sir Alex Ferguson (not pictured) as he fights to save his job

Carrick needs a win against Bournemouth on Sunday after a terrible start to the season

‘I speak to both of them quite regularly, to be honest,’ said Carrick. ‘There's nothing in particular from that. I'm close to both of them and we do have regular conversations. It's nothing different this week.’

There have been concerns over dressing-room unrest after captain Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez gave interviews criticising Carrick and director of football Jason Wilcox, but the United boss denied the club have become ‘unmanageable’ and backed his players to come good.

‘I definitely trust them. One hundred per cent I trust them,’ added Carrick. ‘It wasn't a very good night (in Como) at all for so many reasons, we all know that. I think that's pretty obvious. We'll be a different team on Sunday. We have to be a different team on Sunday.’

Carrick was asked why he gave a five-minute monologue before his weekly press conference on Friday, and replied: ‘Because I understand the situation, and I understand my position and I know what this football club means to so, so many people.

‘The history doesn't give you the right to keep winning. Teams that win earn the right to win. So it's important that we draw inspiration from history and the past of what's gone on.

‘But our responsibility is to carry that forward, and it's so important to me that we do that.’

Sports.title: Chelsea 0-2 Spurs PLAYER RATINGS: Which Blues star endured a nightmare outing? Who was an 'absolute nuisance' for the visitors? And how did Cole Palmer rate after red card?
Sports.content:
Tottenham beat Chelsea at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in 36 years on an evening to remember for Roberto De Zerbi's men. A dreadful error from Blues goalkeeper Mike Penders gave Spurs the lead 13 minutes from time as he punched a corner into his own net. It went from bad to worse for Chelsea shortly after as Cole Palmer was sent off for two yellow cards in quick succession. Mathys Tel then sealed the three points for Spurs as he beat Penders from distance to cap a perfect outing for the visitors and leave Xabi Alonso with questions to answer. Daily Mail Sport's KIERAN GILL and BOBBY MANZI were there to run the rule over both sides. Roberto De Zerbi's men secured a famous victory at Stamford Bridge on Saturday night CHELSEA (3-4-2-1) Mike Penders – 3 Is there a worse way to mark your full debut in the Premier League than this? He tried to punch clear a Tottenham corner, but only sent the ball backwards for an own goal. He was then beaten from 20 yards by Mathys Tel to cap an unfortunate afternoon for the 21-year-old understudy. Josh Acheampong – 5 Tottenham seemed to target this 20-year-old academy graduate’s side, especially in the first half. Acheampong had his hands full with Tel, who got away from him to score Spurs’ second, while James Maddison was also drifting into his area. Maxence Lacroix – 5 Performed an acrobatic clearance in a bid to try to save Penders from his humiliation, but the ball had crossed the line. Among those Chelsea players who took turns fouling Maddison before he exited injured. Levi Colwill – 5 Had an easier time of it defending-wise than Acheampong. Super ball in behind from deep nearly left Pedro Neto one-on-one. But this was a substandard afternoon for all those associated with Chelsea. A dreadful error from Mike Penders gifted Spurs the lead 13 minutes from time as he punched into his own net Pedro Neto – 6 Wing back. Winger. Call him what you want. Neto works hard. Tel tried to buy a penalty out of him, but he won the ball fairly. Tested Antonin Kinsky several times – just couldn’t score. Moises Caicedo – 5 If you were in his way, he’d barge into you, as Maddison discovered here on the odd occasion. Maddison was allowed too much space throughout. Captained Chelsea to a derby defeat. Jordan Henderson – 5 Almost scored in what was his fourth successive start in the Premier League. Kinsky managed to stop his 18-yard crack after some – rare – nice one-touch football from Chelsea. Jorrel Hato – 5 When Spurs had the ball – as they often did – he was expected to be a left back. When Chelsea had it, he was supposed to get forward to help the attack. Cole Palmer – 3 He flirted with a second yellow last week at Everton and got away with it then. But he did not here. He earned his two bookings. He barged into Mateus Fernandes to be cautioned for dissent after 71 minutes. Then stood on Conor Gallagher’s foot after 80. Both were acts of idiocy from Palmer. Cole Palmer was sent off for two yellow cards in quick succession after a moment of madness Morgan Rogers also struggled in a different role as the Blues rued the absence of Joao Pedro Geovany Quenda – 5 First start for Chelsea, replacing the injured Joao Pedro, but hardly contributed to the attack. Tried swapping wings with Neto for a while. Huge roar for Estevao when the Brazilian replaced him. Morgan Rogers – 5 Chelsea missed the hold-up play of a striker. Rogers largely filled in as a false nine, though the set-up was rather fluid as players moved around positions. Showed his frustration towards the end when he was on the pitch without his mates, the red-carded Palmer and the injured Joao Pedro. SUBS USED Marco Palestra (for Hato, 65 minutes) – 5 Came on at 0-0. Chelsea lost 2-0. But hardly his fault. The Blues were not competitive enough throughout this match and Spurs left saying they outplayed their opponents. Estevao (for Quenda, 73 minutes) – 5 You do not hear many roars this loud for a substitution as Estevao was introduced before the 80th minute for the first time this season. But he could not deliver that big moment. Danny Welbeck (for Neto, 88 minutes) – N/A SUBS NOT USED Teddy Shawman-Lowe Wesley Fofana Valentin Barco Malo Gusto Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli Romeo Lavia MANAGER Xabi Alonso – 4 This was not a performance worthy of Chelsea when Tottenham come to town. They are supposed to try to take control, but they were weak here, and deserved to lose. TOTTENHAM Antonin Kinsky - 7 Slightly questionable with his feet but brilliant otherwise. Made a fantastic save to deny Palmer, tipping over the bar. A few good stops from Neto chances, too. Archie Gray - 6 Played both left-back and right-back, neither fazed him. Managed Palmer and Quenda well. Didn’t offer bundles going forward, though. Jan Paul van Hecke - 7 Pressured Penders into a mistake as he punched into his own net, giving Spurs their first win at Stamford Bridge in eight years. Spurs fans won’t care how it was scored, van Hecke will go down as their hero. Was a rock at the back. Sandro Tonali helped Spurs run the midfield in a dominant display as they claimed a 2-0 win Micky van de Ven - 7 Strong. A misfiring Chelsea front line could not get past him. Formed a fine partnership with his compatriot at centre-back. Andy Robertson - 6 Combined well with Tel, particularly in the first half. Played an exquisite cross into Marmoush’s feet and was robbed of an assist by poor finishing. Mateus Fernandes - 7 Was up for it and pivotal to Spurs’ midfield control. Expertly broke up play and acted as the anchor between defence and attack. Solid. Sandro Tonali - 7 Covered the most ground of any player. Offered a durable platform with his defensive work. Dominated midfield alongside Fernandes and that was vital. Mohammed Kudus - 7 Missed narrowly inside the area, bending wide of the post from a tight angle. Got on the ball plenty and showed his dribbling quality. Tonali's midfield partner Mateus Fernandes put in his best performance since joining Spurs James Maddison - 8 Ran the show on his second start of the season until he was forced off injured minutes into the second half. He just cannot stay fit. Kept it ticking in midfield; Moises Caicedo could not get near him. Was the main creative outlet while on the field, with the most touches in the opposition box. Found Tel in space on the left with a wonderful outside-of-the-boot pass. Their link-up was effective. Mathys Tel - 8 Absolute nuisance down the left. Chelsea could not handle him at all. Topped it off with an exceptional drilled finish from outside of the box in the dying minutes, guaranteeing a rare Spurs win over Chelsea. Omar Marmoush - 5 Should have given Spurs the lead after he was found free in the six-yard box but hit his effort straight at Penders. Anywhere else, it was 1-0 Spurs. Disappointing. SUBS Conor Gallagher (51’ for Maddison) - 6 Was fouled as Cole Palmer was sent off for a second yellow card. Viscerally booed by the home fans on return to his former employers. Didn’t do much. Dominic Solanke (65’ for Marmoush) - 5 Didn’t manage a shot in his 25-minute cameo. It was a good job those around him took the initiative. Pedro Porro (65’ for Robertson) - 6 Active up and down the touchline. Helped keep Spurs’ energy high. Ben Davies (89’ for Kudus) - N/A Dejan Kulusevski (89’ for Tel) - N/A Now give your ratings...
