Sports.title: Alberto Puello Falls Short Against Dalton Smith
Sports.content:
Dalton “Thunder” Smith (20-0, 14 KOs) retained his WBC light welterweight title with a split decision over former champion Alberto “La Avispa” Puello (25-2, 11 KOs) on Saturday at a sold-out Utilita Arena in Sheffield, England.

Two judges scored the fight 115-113 for Smith, while the third had Puello ahead 115-112. Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Boxing promoted the event, which aired on DAZN.

The opening six rounds were closely contested, with this writer’s unofficial card even after Puello took the fifth and sixth.

Smith responded well in the seventh and eighth, edging the action as swelling appeared beneath Puello’s left eye. Puello answered with stronger work in the ninth and tenth before Smith took the 11th.

In the final round, a left hand from Puello opened a small cut on Smith’s right cheek. Smith began celebrating during the final 30 seconds, although the divided scorecards showed how close the contest had been.

Lee Every refereed.

Giorgio Visioli Edges Maxi Hughes

Unbeaten southpaw Giorgio “The Italian Job” Visioli (12-0, 6 KOs) defeated veteran Maxi “Maximus” Hughes (29-10-2, 6 KOs) by majority decision over ten rounds to win the vacant WBC International Silver lightweight title.

Two judges scored it 96-94 for Visioli, with the third returning a 95-95 draw.

Visioli’s effective jab helped him through much of the first seven rounds. Hughes opened a cut over Visioli’s left eyebrow with a right jab in the eighth, but Visioli responded and finished strongly enough to secure the decision. Kieran McCann refereed.

Shannon Ryan Stops Emma Dolan In Rematch

Shannon “Kaos” Ryan (12-1, 3 KOs) avenged her previous defeat to Emma Dolan (9-2, 1 KO) with a first-round stoppage in their scheduled ten-round super flyweight rematch.

Around 20 seconds into the fight, Ryan dropped Dolan with a right hand to the side of the face. Dolan rose, but another right followed by a left sent her down again.

Referee Howard Foster stopped the contest at 40 seconds after Dolan regained her feet.

Edward Hardy Outpoints Diego Ruiz

Edward Hardy (9-0, 3 KOs) remained unbeaten with an eight-round points victory over Diego “El Profeta” Ruiz (28-16-1, 14 KOs).

Referee Jamie Kirkpatrick scored it 79-73 for Hardy, who controlled most of the action from the second round onward.

Both fighters maintained a high work rate during an active final round, but Hardy finished with a clear points win.

Joe Hayden Defeats Will Harrison

Joe Hayden (25-0, 4 KOs) handed Will “The Thrill” Harrison (8-1-2, 0 KOs) his first professional defeat in their eight-round welterweight bout.

Referee Jamie Kirkpatrick scored it 79-72 for Hayden.

Leo Atang Scores Three Knockdowns In First-Round Stoppage

Nineteen-year-old heavyweight Leo Atang (9-0, 8 KOs) dropped Jonathan “Chicito” Vergara (9-5, 5 KOs) three times before stopping him in the opening round of their scheduled six-round contest.

A right hand dropped Vergara within the first minute. Atang scored another knockdown with a right to the side of the head with approximately 30 seconds remaining.

A third right hand sent Vergara down again in the closing seconds. Referee Jamie Kirkpatrick waved off the fight after Vergara rose, just before the bell.

Chris Mulunda Shuts Out Harley Collison

Chris “Mulla” Mulunda (5-0, 0 KOs) defeated Harley Collison (3-9-2, 0 KOs) by points over six rounds.

Referee Michael Alexander scored every round for Mulunda, returning a 60-54 verdict.

Divine Omojor Wins Professional Debut

Cruiserweight Divine Omojor (1-0, 1 KO) began his professional career with a second-round stoppage of Goran Kozul (8-13, 2 KOs).

Referee Michael Alexander stopped the scheduled four-round bout at 1:52 of the second.

David Diamante served as ring announcer.

Sports.title: Emanuel ‘Vaquero’ Navarrete Loses to O’Shaquie ‘Ice Water’ Foster!
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie “Ice Water” Foster defeated Emanuel “Vaquero” Navarrete by unanimous decision Saturday night at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas, adding the WBO and IBF super featherweight titles to his WBC championship.

Foster scored two knockdowns in the final round and won by scores of 118-108, 118-108, and 115-111. The Top Rank event aired on DAZN.

Foster improved to 26-3 with 12 knockouts, while Navarrete fell to 40-3-1 with 33 knockouts.

Navarrete spent the opening round following Foster without consistently cutting off the ring, allowing Foster to land counters and move away. The second round became scrappier, with Foster tying Navarrete up when he closed the distance.

Navarrete had success with pressure in the third, but Foster’s movement and counterpunching helped him control much of the action over the following rounds. Foster hurt Navarrete during the seventh, forcing him to hold.

Both landed well in the tenth, with Navarrete producing some of his better offensive work. Navarrete also hurt Foster with a heavy shot late in the 11th, giving him encouragement entering the final round.

Foster responded with two knockdowns in the 12th. A counter right sent Navarrete to one knee, and referee Mark Nelson administered the count. Another counter right dropped Navarrete again in the final minute.

Navarrete rose both times and reached the bell, but Foster’s strong finish secured the victory.

Albert Gonzalez Knocks Out Edward Vazquez

NABF featherweight champion Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez improved to 19-0 with 12 knockouts by stopping Edward “Kid” Vazquez at 1:04 of the second round of their scheduled ten-round bout.

Vazquez, of Fort Worth, Texas, fell to 20-4 with six knockouts.

Gonzalez overwhelmed Vazquez with a prolonged attack in the second round, then followed him to another corner. Heavy punches to the body sent Vazquez to one knee, where referee Laurence Cole counted him out.

Frank Martin Stops Tarik Zaina

Southpaw Frank “The Ghost” Martin stopped Tarik “El Camello” Zaina at 2:38 of the seventh round to win the vacant NABO light welterweight title.

Martin improved to 20-1-1 with 14 knockouts, while Zaina dropped to 18-4-1 with 12 knockouts.

Martin had success early, but Zaina’s lead right hands helped keep the middle rounds competitive.

In the final minute of the seventh, Martin landed a combination beginning with a left to the chin that dropped Zaina. Zaina beat referee Angel Mendez’s count, but Martin immediately followed with a flurry that forced Mendez to stop the fight.

Deric Davis Shuts Out Joaquin Silva Faccio

Deric “Scooter” Davis defeated Joaquin Silva Faccio by unanimous decision in their eight-round lightweight bout, winning 80-72 on all three scorecards.

Davis improved to 13-0 with ten knockouts, while Faccio fell to 10-2 with four knockouts.

Davis consistently attacked the body and controlled the action. He hurt Faccio with a body shot late in the seventh, but the Uruguayan remained on his feet.

Faccio fought back in an active final round, though Davis completed the shutout. Laurence Cole refereed.

Samuel Contreras Outpoints Oscar Pedroza Padilla

Samuel Contreras remained unbeaten with a six-round unanimous decision over Oscar “El Perro” Pedroza Padilla in their lightweight contest.

All three judges scored it 60-54 for Contreras, who improved to 9-0 with three knockouts. Pedroza Padilla dropped to 8-3-1 with three knockouts.

Contreras hurt Pedroza Padilla with a flurry midway through the second round, leaving him with a bloody nose. Pedroza Padilla answered with an overhand right that rocked Contreras during a competitive fourth.

Contreras finished strongly, landing the cleaner punches over the closing rounds to secure the decision. Angel Mendez refereed.

Daniel Cortez Edges Joshua Montoya

Daniel III Cortez won a six-round split decision over Joshua “Spotlight” Montoya in their super bantamweight bout.

Two judges scored it 58-56 for Cortez, while the third had Montoya ahead by the same score.

Cortez improved to 14-1 with nine knockouts, while Montoya fell to 8-6-2 with one knockout.

Cortez’s work rate helped him through several close rounds, but Montoya stayed competitive and finished well in the sixth. His late effort wasn’t enough to secure the verdict. Laurence Cole refereed.

Joseph Almajdi Defeats Miqal Dolphus

Joseph Almajdi defeated Miqal Dolphus by unanimous decision in their six-round super welterweight opener, winning 60-54 on all three cards.

Almajdi improved to 6-1 with three knockouts, while Dolphus suffered his first professional defeat and fell to 6-1-1 with four knockouts.

A right hand from Almajdi buzzed Dolphus near the end of the third round. Almajdi also landed a left hook late in the fifth that drove Dolphus backward, helping him complete a clear points victory.

Angel Mendez refereed. Ralph Velez Jr. handled the preliminary ring introductions, with Jimmy Lennon Jr. announcing the main card.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Targets O’Shaquie Foster After Undisputed Run
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson called for a future fight with O’Shaquie Foster after watching him defeat Emanuel Navarrete, describing the newly unified super featherweight champion as an opponent who would motivate him to return to the ring.

Shakur left the timing open, indicating he would wait until Foster finishes pursuing undisputed status at 130 pounds. His challenge came after Foster collected Navarrete’s WBO and IBF belts to go with his WBC championship Saturday night.

“Helluva fighter he will never give me my credit but I’ll be real tonight he showed his level,” Shakur wrote on X. “That’s a challenge that would get me out of bed. Let’s do it whenever he’s ready.” He added: “I’ll be here after his undisputed run!”

Shakur’s challenge initially sounded immediate, but waiting until Foster becomes undisputed suggests he wants the fight to marinate before committing.

Foster earned the attention with a performance built on accurate counters, movement, and a strong finish. He dropped Navarrete twice in the 12th round and won by scores of 118-108, 118-108, and 115-111.

That was the kind of opponent Shakur could appreciate: a boxer who made an aggressive, awkward champion miss and repeatedly punished him for reaching. Foster also recovered from being hurt late in the 11th to deliver his most decisive round.

There was a competitive edge beneath Shakur’s praise. His claim that Foster would never give him credit made the message more than a congratulatory post, although he still recognized what Foster had accomplished.

The practical questions remain unanswered. Shakur did not name a weight, propose a date, or suggest negotiations had begun. Foster has just secured three belts at super featherweight, while Shakur holds the WBO light welterweight title.

A meeting would therefore require decisions about weight as well as timing. For now, Shakur has identified Foster as a challenge worth pursuing, while giving him room to chase the remaining championship at 130 before discussing a fight.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Drops Emanuel Navarrete Twice To Unify
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster knocked Emanuel Navarrete down twice in the final round to complete a unanimous decision victory and unify three super featherweight titles Saturday night at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas.

The judges scored it 118-108, 118-108, and 115-111 for Foster, who retained his WBC belt and took Navarrete’s WBO and IBF championships. He also claimed the vacant Ring Magazine title in the DAZN main event.

Foster’s accuracy and movement frustrated Navarrete through much of the contest. He landed leaping left hooks early, followed with straight punches, and stepped away before Navarrete could bring his heavier attacks into play. Navarrete kept advancing but frequently found himself reaching and missing.

The third round offered Navarrete a route back into the fight. He caught Foster near the ropes, landed to the body, and threw a prolonged combination that forced the American onto defense. His pressure was more effective when he closed the distance before letting his hands go.

Foster adjusted in the fourth, taking the initiative with body jabs and counters. Over the middle rounds, he repeatedly beat Navarrete to the punch, landing straight shots and a sharp counter uppercut while using movement and clinches to interrupt the return attacks.

Navarrete remained dangerous despite struggling to sustain his offense. He landed some of his cleanest punches during a competitive tenth round, then hurt Foster with a heavy shot near the end of the 11th. That moment gave the closing stages an uncertainty the earlier rounds had often lacked.

Foster removed it in the 12th. With Navarrete chasing a knockout, Foster landed counter right hands that produced two knockdowns. Navarrete rose both times, but he couldn’t turn the fight around.

The finish strengthened a performance built on cleaner punching and better control of distance. Navarrete’s persistence kept him threatening late, but Foster made him pay for the risks he took and left with three world titles at 130 pounds.

Sports.title: Emanuel Navarrete vs. O’Shaquie Foster Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster defeated Emanuel Navarrete by unanimous decision, scoring two knockdowns in the final round to unify the WBC, WBO, and IBF super featherweight titles. The judges scored it 118-108, 118-108, and 115-111 for Foster, who also claimed the vacant Ring Magazine belt.

Foster controlled much of the fight with accurate counters, body punching, and movement that repeatedly left Navarrete swinging at empty space. Navarrete had success when he trapped Foster near the ropes, and a heavy shot late in the 11th briefly hurt the American.

Foster answered decisively in the 12th, dropping Navarrete twice with counter right hands as the Mexican chased a knockout. Navarrete rose both times and reached the final bell, but Foster’s cleaner boxing and strong finish secured the three-belt victory.

Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez (19-0, 12 KOs) knocked out Edward Vazquez (20-4, 6 KOs) with a second-round body attack to retain his NABF featherweight title. Gonzalez had a quiet opening round before increasing his aggression sharply in the second.

He hurt Vazquez early in the round and followed with short, compact combinations that left the challenger struggling to recover. Gonzalez kept attacking downstairs, landing heavy body punches, including a left hook, before Vazquez went to the canvas. Vazquez couldn’t beat the count, with referee Laurence Cole counting him out.

The unbeaten Gonzalez needed fewer than two rounds to defeat a former world title challenger in the scheduled ten-round co-main event. The knockout ended Vazquez’s three-fight winning streak and gave Gonzalez another early finish following his second-round victory over Aaron Alameda in July.

Frank “The Ghost” Martin (20-1-1, 14 KOs) stopped Tarik Zaina (18-4-1, 12 KOs) in the seventh round to win the vacant NABO light welterweight title. Martin started cautiously, allowing the taller Zaina to keep the early rounds competitive with his reach and awkward style.

Zaina landed a couple of solid power shots in the third, giving Martin more to consider as he searched for openings. Through five rounds, Martin had yet to take firm control, with his opponent continuing to find occasional success at long range.

That changed in the seventh when Martin stepped back and dropped Zaina with a hard left hand. Zaina beat the count, but Martin immediately attacked with follow-up punches that forced the referee to stop the fight.

The finish handed Zaina his first stoppage defeat and gave Martin a needed victory after his February draw with Nahir Albright.

Deric “Scooter” Davis (13-0, 10 KOs) swept all eight rounds against Joaquin Silva Faccio (10-2, 4 KOs), winning a unanimous decision in their lightweight bout. All three judges scored it 80-72 for Davis, who controlled the action from the opening round.

Faccio came forward aggressively, but Davis picked him off with straight punches and used defensive movement to avoid much of the return fire. Davis continued landing the cleaner shots as Faccio’s awkward footwork did little to disrupt his accuracy.

In the sixth, Davis attacked the body with hard punches that left Faccio trying unsuccessfully to match his work. Faccio absorbed considerable punishment but kept fighting back through an active finish. There were no knockdowns, with Davis having to settle for a wide points victory against an opponent tough enough to last the distance.

Super bantamweight Daniel III Cortez (14-1, 9 KOs) edged Joshua “Spotlight” Montoya (8-6-2, 1 KO) by split decision. Two judges scored it 58-56 for Cortez, while the third favored Montoya by the same score. Cortez entered as the favorite but had to work for the victory against an opponent who kept the contest close.

Cortez’s busier work helped him in the third round, although Montoya came on toward the end of it. Neither fighter scored a knockdown, leaving the judges to separate them after six competitive rounds.

Montoya made a strong case for the decision, with ringside observer Francisco Salazar scoring the fight 58-56 in his favor. Cortez ultimately secured his 14th professional victory, but the divided scorecards reflected how little separated the two fighters.

Lightweight Samuel “Sammy” Contreras (9-0, 3 KOs) remained unbeaten with a six-round unanimous decision over Oscar Pedroza Padilla (8-3-1, 3 KOs). All three judges scored it 60-54 for Contreras, who controlled most of the action.

Contreras punished Pedroza Padilla through the first three rounds, leaving the Mexican fighter struggling to find an answer. Pedroza Padilla rallied in the fourth, getting inside and landing enough shots to draw a response from the crowd. Contreras regained control in the fifth, delivering more punishment and stopping his opponent from building on that success.

The fight went the distance without a knockdown, giving Contreras his ninth professional victory.

Joseph Almajdi (6-1, 3 KOs) handed Miqal Dolphus (6-1-1, 4 KOs) his first professional defeat, winning a six-round unanimous decision in their junior middleweight bout. All three judges scored the opening preliminary contest 60-54 for Almajdi.

Using his height and reach, Almajdi established distance with his jab and followed with straight right hands. Dolphus pressed forward and attacked the body, trying to get inside the taller fighter’s reach.

The middle rounds brought lively action, with Dolphus finding some success but Almajdi producing the cleaner work. Almajdi’s footwork and timing helped him control the distance often enough to sweep the scorecards.

Neither fighter scored a knockdown, with Almajdi earning his sixth professional victory and Dolphus going the distance despite struggling to impose his pressure.

Sports.title: Albert Gonzalez Knocks Out Edward Vazquez In Two
Sports.content:
Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez broke through Edward Vazquez’s defenses with a punishing body attack, scoring a second-round knockout to retain his NABF featherweight title Saturday night at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas.

The unbeaten Gonzalez improved to 19-0 with 12 knockouts in the scheduled ten-round co-main event on the Emanuel Navarrete–O’Shaquie Foster card on DAZN. Vazquez dropped to 20-4 with six knockouts, losing his three-fight winning streak.

Gonzalez gave little away about the approaching finish during a quiet opening round. The 24-year-old allowed Vazquez to be the more active fighter while taking time to find his distance. There was no sustained attack from Gonzalez, and the veteran challenger had an opportunity to get started without immediately being forced into survival mode.

That changed quickly in the second.

Gonzalez hurt Vazquez early and moved straight into his finishing work, throwing short combinations rather than giving the challenger time to recover. His punches downstairs did the most damage, with a left hook to the body among the blows that sent Vazquez to the canvas.

Referee Laurence Cole completed the ten-count with Vazquez unable to rise in time. Once Gonzalez increased his output, the fight went from a cautious start to a one-sided finish.

The result followed Gonzalez’s second-round body-shot knockout of Aaron Alameda in July, when he won the vacant NABF belt. Trained by Robert Garcia, Gonzalez again showed how quickly his compact punches can become decisive when an opponent remains within range.

Vazquez brought experience against Joe Cordina and Rafael Espinoza, along with recent winning form, but neither helped him absorb Gonzalez’s body attack. He had entered after three consecutive victories, including a decision over Daniel Lugo.

Gonzalez still needs tougher tests before his championship potential can be judged fully. This performance, however, gives his team reason to seek a higher-level opponent: Vazquez never had time to make his experience count once Gonzalez began landing heavily.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia vs Teofimo Lopez Targets February 6
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are targeting February 6 for their next fight, with negotiations continuing despite uncertainty over Lopez’s WBA title and Garcia’s pursuit of Floyd Mayweather Jr.

Mike Coppinger reports that neither the WBA’s decision nor the possibility of a Mayweather fight is expected to interfere with those discussions. That puts Garcia–Lopez ahead of the Mayweather matchup, which has generated plenty of talk without producing an agreement.

“Would be surprised if Garcia-Teofimo didn’t take place next,” Coppinger wrote on X. “Feb. 6 is the targeted date right now as talks continue.”

The date is still a target. There is no confirmed fight announcement, but the report gives Garcia’s next move a clearer direction after his attorney and adviser, Guadalupe Valencia, promoted the financial potential of facing Mayweather.

Valencia’s comments left the timetable dependent on Mayweather becoming available. Coppinger’s reporting places that possibility further down the road, with Teofimo first.

A Garcia–Lopez fight would give Ryan an opponent whose threat comes from what he can do today. Mayweather’s name would sell the event, but Teofimo offers a competitive fight between two active stars with something to lose.

The WBA situation remains a separate question. Jack Catterall has been pursuing his ordered fight with Lopez, while Teofimo has sought permission to pursue Garcia instead. Coppinger’s report indicates negotiations can continue regardless of the ruling; it does not establish whether Lopez will retain his championship.

That affects how the fight can eventually be promoted. Garcia–Lopez has an appeal with or without two belts, but calling it a confirmed unification would be premature until Lopez’s title position is settled.

Garcia also has reason to keep his attention on the opponent closest to becoming a reality. Selling a Mayweather fight before reaching terms with Teofimo risks making the more competitive matchup sound like a preliminary step.

For now, February 6 is the date to watch. Mayweather remains a possible later payday, while Garcia and Lopez work toward the fight Coppinger expects to happen next.

Sports.title: Emanuel Navarrete vs. O’Shaquie Foster: Strategic Analysis
Sports.content:
Tonight, at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas, is the coronation for the best super featherweight boxer in the world. The winner of the unification match between Emanuel “El Vaquero” Navarrete and O’Shaquie “Ice Water” Foster will capture the vacant Ring magazine

super featherweight title along with the respective belts held by each champion the WBO, IBF, and WBC titles.

The winner may also potentially be recognized as the fighter of the year, as both fighters’ accomplishments thus far merit contention; a victory tonight would only reaffirm the designation as this year’s best.

A fight where potentially both can win but must overcome stylistic challenges to capture the victory. For Navarrete (40-2-1, 33 KOs) it’s contending with Foster’s (25-3, 12 KOs) superior technical boxing ability. O’Shaquie’s agility and elusiveness is what Emanuel will most struggle with.

Trainer Pedro Navarrete knows of the challenges saying, “I think every training camp is different because you have to prepare for the opponent in front of you. I think this will be one of the more difficult camps because of Foster’s style, but we’re putting in the work. We have elusive sparring partners helping us prepare for that style so we can go into the fight as well prepared as possible.”

If El Vaquero can close the distance and stay within range of Foster, he’ll be able to attempt and connect one of his most deadliest, the gazelle hook. This punch is difficult to defend because he leaps and lunges into the punch throwing it when the opponent is within range.

It is Emanuel’s awkwardness and unpredictable fighting style that makes him so dangerous to defend against. He must use this to his advantage and use his volume to throw from unconventional and awkward angles to connect against O’Shaquie.

Navarrete may be the strongest puncher Foster has faced in his career and his average output rate of 60 punches per round will present its own difficulties. El Vaquero is most effective offensively utilizing his power punches, he connects at a respectable rate of 34.7 percent (Compubox).

How effective O’Shaquie is in defending Navarrete’s power punches will determine the winner of the match. When asked about Emanuel’s power, Foster said, “I wouldn’t be able to tell until I get in there with him. I faced power punchers…several power punchers. I had Jon Fernandez, Edward…Rocky Hernandez. I faced power punchers man and I’ve always dealt with it great. So, he’s just going to be another guy, he’s just a little more chaotic with it but you know I just gotta stay focused, you can’t trust him. He going to throw from different angles, but…but we’re going to freeze him, though.”

Foster holds the overall edge in this match due to his overall boxing ability and skill but it’s Navarrete’s power and chaotic style that make him so difficult to defend, he will be the bigger stronger fighter come fight night but O’Shaquie will be the faster, more agile boxer who will attempt to outpoint El Vaquero by limiting the exchanges by being precise with his punches.

Navarrete’smethod of victory will be to attempt to time Foster coming in. He’s fought boxers with movement in the past but nothing to the level of O’Shaquie. He had his struggles against Liam Wilson but was ultimately able to connect and score the knockout victory.

Against Denys Berinchyk, he struggled with weight and style, losing by split decision. Foster is on another level in terms of boxing ability and has looked much improved since his controversial loss to Robson Conceicao. As long as he doesn’t get caught sleeping, this is O’Shaquie’s fight to lose and prove he’s on the elite level.

Ghana News.title: GES, stakeholders call for stronger action against child marriage in Eastern Region
Ghana News.content:
The Eastern Regional Directorate of the Ghana Education Service (GES) has marked the International Day of the Girl with a call for increased investment in girls’ rights and efforts to end child marriage.

The celebration was held at Oyoko Methodist Senior High School on the theme: “End Child Marriage and Invest in Girls’ Rights.”

It brought together students and stakeholders to promote girls’ education, protection and empowerment, while encouraging boys to play an active role in addressing teenage pregnancy and gender-based violence.

Madam Patricia Birago Gyamfi, Eastern Regional Girls’ Education Officer, said the participation of boys was essential to efforts to protect and empower girls.

She stressed that no girl under 18 years should be forced into marriage, adding that every child deserved the opportunity to learn, develop and make informed decisions about her future.

She called on parents to keep their daughters in school and urged teachers, community leaders and other stakeholders to create safe learning environments and support programmes that promoted girls’ education, health, safety and leadership.

Mr Kwasi Owusu Obeng, Eastern Regional Population Officer of the National Population Council (NPC), said teenage pregnancy and early sexual activity posed serious threats to girls’ education and prospects.

He said the Eastern Region had a teenage pregnancy rate of about 14 per cent, describing it as a concern that required stronger interventions.

Mr Obeng said reproductive health education often focused on girls, despite the role boys played in teenage pregnancies, and called for greater attention to educating boys on abstinence and responsible sexual behaviour.

He said involving boys in reproductive health programmes would help reduce teenage pregnancies and promote shared responsibility among young people.

Dr Moses Barima Djimatey, Eastern Regional Deputy Director of Public Health, said addressing teenage pregnancy required the active involvement of both boys and girls.

He disclosed that more than 4,000 girls aged between 10 and 19 became pregnant between January and June, describing the situation as a concern with health, social and economic implications.

Dr Djimatey called for stronger collaboration among district assemblies, religious and traditional leaders, schools, the police and health workers to guide young people and protect their future.

Assistant Superintendent of Police Lydia Wemegah, Eastern Regional Coordinator of the Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU), highlighted the need to intensify efforts to end child marriage and protect girls from abuse.

She called for stronger enforcement of laws against child marriage, community sensitisation and support for victims, noting that poverty, cultural practices and limited education contributed to the persistence of the practice.

As part of the celebration, students were divided into nine groups and assigned mentors to share their life experiences and discuss decisions that could shape their future.

Madam Diana Mintah, Headmistress of Ghana Senior High School (GHANASS), called for regular mentorship programmes for students, saying they would equip them with the knowledge and values needed to become responsible leaders and positive role models for future generations.

Ghana News.title: NDC to investigate vote-buying allegations in constituency elections if evidence is provided
Ghana News.content:
Dr. Sofo Tanko Rashid Computer, Deputy National Director of Elections and IT for NDC

The National Democratic Congress (NDC) says it is prepared to investigate allegations of vote-buying in its ongoing constituency elections if credible evidence is brought before the party’s national executives.

The party’s Deputy Director of Elections, Rashid Tanko-Computer, said the NDC would not condone conduct that compromises the integrity of its internal electoral processes.

He cited the party’s response to a previous incident involving Ayawaso as an indication that it was willing to act when concerns about electoral conduct were brought to its attention.

Mr Tanko-Computer, however, said the party had not recorded any incidents of vote-buying in the constituencies where voting had taken place, describing the elections overall as largely peaceful and successful.

He acknowledged that the exercise had encountered difficulties in some areas, including Odododiodioo, where counting was suspended following violence but resumed after party officials intervened. He also disclosed that voting in some constituencies in the Ashanti and Eastern regions had been postponed until the following day to allow outstanding issues to be resolved.

Speaking on Channel One TV, Mr Tanko-Computer said: “If somebody has any evidence of that and it’s brought to the notice of the national executives, why not? We’ll take notice of it.”

Ghana News.title: Transport Minister calls for efficient, competitive ports to boost regional trade
Ghana News.content:
c

Mr Nikpe said achieving the ambition required sustained collaboration among the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA), the government, private-sector operators, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders across the transport and logistics value chain.

He made the call in a keynote address at the GPHA’s 40th Anniversary Dinner and Industry Awards, where he highlighted six priorities for building a more efficient, competitive, and sustainable port system.

The priorities include improving cargo handling and evacuation, reducing avoidable delays, strengthening coordination among port operators and regulatory agencies, and making port services faster, more reliable and cost-effective.

The Minister said port competitiveness depended not only on infrastructure but also on the quality and efficiency of services delivered to businesses and customers.

He also called for the adoption of integrated digital systems, automation, and data-driven operations to improve transparency, simplify procedures, and enhance customer experience.

On transport connectivity, he said stronger links among ports, roads, railways, inland terminals and logistics centres were essential to easing congestion, facilitating cargo movement, and improving access to regional markets.

Mr Nikpe urged stakeholders to prioritise environmental sustainability, energy efficiency, workplace safety and operational resilience as the country modernised its port infrastructure and services.

He said workforce development was equally important, calling for investment in professional training, digital skills, technical expertise and leadership development to prepare workers for the changing demands of the maritime and logistics industry.

On regional trade, the Minister said Ghana had an opportunity to strengthen its position as a preferred gateway for landlocked neighbouring countries and a leading logistics hub for West Africa.

He said realising that potential required reliable services, competitive costs, efficient transit procedures and deeper collaboration with regional partners.

The Minister said the six priorities reinforced the anniversary theme of service, partnership and progress, stressing that no single institution could achieve the objectives independently.

He encouraged stakeholders to sustain cooperation to improve the competitiveness and efficiency of Ghana’s transport sector.

The event also recognised individuals and organisations whose dedication, professionalism and contributions had advanced GPHA and the country’s maritime industry.

The Minister congratulated the award recipients and urged stakeholders to uphold high standards of service, integrity, and innovation.

As GPHA looked towards its next 40 years, he called for continued investment in digital transformation, transport connectivity and workforce development to expand Ghana’s contribution to regional trade.

He said the ambition to build West Africa’s premier trade and logistics hub must be reflected in service quality, strong partnerships and tangible results for businesses, communities and the country.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod begins stakeholder consultations ahead of 2027 small-scale mining support programme
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) has begun engaging industry stakeholders on a proposed programme to formalise artisanal and small-scale mining and provide financial support to eligible operators ahead of its planned launch in 2027.

The initiative, known as the Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining (ASM) Formalisation and Financing Support Programme, is expected to bring eligible informal miners into a regulated system while improving their access to financing and strengthening oversight of their activities.

GoldBod said the consultations involve relevant government agencies, small-scale miners’ associations, civil society organisations and other industry stakeholders. The engagements are intended to gather input to ensure the programme reflects industry needs and can be implemented sustainably.

The Board is developing the programme in collaboration with the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, the University of Mines and Technology (UMaT) and the Mineral Income Investment Fund (MIIF), with technical support from South Africa’s Rand Refinery.

According to GoldBod, the initiative is expected to increase gold production and mineral revenues, create jobs, reduce operational costs and limit environmental degradation associated with mining activities.

The programme also forms part of efforts to tackle illegal mining by ensuring that eligible operators are licensed, monitored and held accountable for their environmental and operational practices.

GoldBod has stressed that the objective is not to legitimise galamsey, but to help eligible informal miners transition into lawful operations and comply with the country’s mining regulations.

In a statement issued by its Media Relations Unit, the Board said it had “commenced stakeholder engagements with key industry stakeholders, including relevant government agencies, small-scale miners’ associations, civil society organizations, among others, on the proposed ASM FFSP”.

The consultations come amid public debate over comments by GoldBod Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi on the formalisation of unlicensed small-scale miners. GoldBod has rejected allegations that he endorsed illegal mining, arguing that a video of his remarks was selectively edited and omitted important context.

Ghana News.title: Almost 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
Ghana News.content:
Nearly 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands of people took part in another day of protests across France which were followed by some clashes late on Saturday, officials have said.

After a day of largely peaceful demonstrations, police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in a number of cities including Paris, while barricades were set alight in Marseille and people ripped boards from a shop in Bordeaux.

But officials have so far managed to avoid rioting and looting on the scale seen last weekend, which resulted in some of the worst scenes of disorder in France's modern history.

The interior ministry said an estimated 410,000 people protested on Saturday, while the unions put the number at about 800,000.

Some 70,000 police officers were deployed and restrictions imposed in several cities to prevent the latest protests over the cost of living and poor school conditions from descending into the kind of chaos which saw officers outnumbered, hundreds of businesses looted and buildings torched.

President Emmanuel Macron had decreed earlier this week that only demonstrations organised by a recognised trade unions would be permitted. Hundreds of people have been jailed for vandalism, arson and looting after fast-track court hearings in recent days.

Clashes between protesters and riot police in Paris erupted at the end of a peaceful march from the city's Porte d'Italie towards Porte de Vincennes on Saturday, where the police operation included an elite unit that usually deals with organised crime and counter-terrorism.

Some protesters were seen erecting makeshift barricades and pelting officers with projectiles, while police baton-charged groups of masked youths who were smashing the windows of a car dealership.

French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that "several thousand radical activists gathered at the rear of the march, including around 500 individuals identified as rioters", the AFP news agency reported.

In the southern port of Marseille, rubbish bins were set ablaze and metal sheets used to block streets. A law enforcement vehicle was seen driving through a burning barricade in France's second-largest city.

Meanwhile, some protesters in dark clothing and face coverings were seen taking boards off a building to build a street barricade in the southern city of Bordeaux.

In Lyon, police used tear gas grenades to disperse a crowd which had reportedly gathered in an area deemed off-limits by the local prefecture.

"There were around 150 of us, mostly secondary school and university students. Then the tear gas came almost immediately. You could barely see anything in the street," said one protester in France's third-largest city.

Nuñez said late in the day that nearly 1,000 people had been arrested, a number he said would increase.

The minister also said two people had been "seriously injured": one in the south-western city of Toulouse, and another one in Clermont-Ferrand, central France.

Earlier, a peaceful protester in Paris who gave her name as Zelie told the BBC people had taken to the streets because they were "really frustrated" and had been "suffering a lot" since Macron came to office.

"They keep us quiet. They take our money, they tax us a lot and we can't say anything. Today we are in the streets because it's been too long, it's been too much," the 26-year-old said.

Two masked teenage protesters, who did not want to give their names, also said their generation was in despair and felt abandoned by the government.

"I think looting is really not good," one of the demonstrators said of last Saturday's disorder. "But it's because of poverty and the violence of the police."

He added that the protests would end "when we have a response to our demands. We really want a change in France".

Meanwhile, some 13,000 people joined a rally against the hard-right National Rally party in the north-central city of Orléans which proceeded peacefully.

Mass protests triggered by similar issues as in France also rocked several other European cities on Saturday.

In Albania's capital Tirana, riot police fired tear gas to disperse thousands of anti-government demonstrators, while clashes were also reported in Belgium's capital Brussels.

In Milan, northern Italy, a major security operation including hundreds of soldiers alongside police prevented protesters gathering in the city. Many had feared a repeat of violent scenes last week when some started fires, smashed windows and looted shops.

Ghana News.title: Tinubu blames opposition for hunger, poverty in Nigeria; Atiku kicks, says president delusional
Ghana News.content:
President Bola Tinubu has accused opposition politicians of causing the hunger and poverty Nigerians are experiencing, insisting that his administration is working to address the problems as he formally launched his 2027 presidential campaign in Kaduna on Saturday.

Mr Tinubu made the remarks at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign flag-off at Ranchers Bees Stadium (also known as Kaduna Township Stadium), ahead of the 2027 general elections.

I have heard the opposition talking about hunger and poverty. Who caused them? They did! They caused hunger and poverty. We are trying to eliminate them,” the president said.

He also urged his supporters to be wary of statements from the opposition, particularly criticism of his decision to remove the petrol subsidy, insisting that the country would not return to the previous system.

“Be careful; watch them. Don’t let them lie to you. What is past is in the past.

“Fuel subsidy is in our past: no more corruption, no more falsification of invoices, no more lies, no more smuggling of fuel,” Mr Tinubu told supporters at the rally.

The president’s remarks come amid persistent public concerns over high food prices, inflation and declining purchasing power, issues expected to feature prominently in political debates ahead of the 2027 elections.

In a swift reaction to the president’s remarks, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, described President Tinubu’s claim “as a delusional, shameless attempt to dodge responsibility for the misery his own government has inflicted on Nigerians.”

He said a president cannot light the fire of hardship with his own policies, then blame the neighbours for the smoke.

Tinubu defends petrol subsidy removal

Since assuming office in May 2023, the Tinubu administration has implemented major economic reforms, including the removal of the petrol subsidy and changes to the foreign exchange regime.

The government has defended the measures as necessary to reduce public expenditure, tackle alleged corruption associated with the subsidy system and establish the foundations for sustainable economic growth.

While Mr Tinubu insists that the removal of the subsidy is irreversible, critics continue to demand evidence that the savings and additional revenue generated by the reforms are translating into improved living conditions for ordinary Nigerians.

At the rally, the president also said salaries were being paid on time and praised APC governors for their development projects.

Tinubu thanks Kaduna residents

At the rally, Mr Tinubu thanked the people of Kaduna State for supporting him in the 2023 presidential election, saying their backing contributed to his victory.

“You gave me the joy of remembering the victory you gave me to become president. I have returned to thank you once again,” he said.

He urged Nigerians to give him another opportunity in 2027, promising to continue pursuing his agenda of prosperity, development and national growth.

Tinubu has a long history of supporting the North – VP Shettima

Vice President Kashim Shettima defended Mr Tinubu’s political relationship with northern Nigeria, saying the president had supported politicians from the region for years, including those who contested the presidency in previous elections.

Mr Shettima cited Mr Tinubu’s political relationships with former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and the late President Muhammadu Buhari to argue that the president had consistently supported northern political figures.

“President Bola Tinubu is one person who has fiercely identified with the North over the years. It is pertinent to mention that when former Vice President Atiku Abubakar was harassed and chased off the PDP with his tail between his legs, he ran to the Lion of Bourdillon, who gave him political succour, support and a platform to contest for the presidency of this country in 2007.

“In 2011, Asiwaju supported another northerner, Nuhu Ribadu, and in 2015 and 2019, he supported our late President Muhammadu Buhari,” Mr Shettima said.

The expression, “Lion of Bourdillon,” refers to Mr Tinubu, whose residence on Bourdillon Road in Lagos has become associated with his political influence.

Atiku contested the presidency under the Action Congress (AC) in 2007 after leaving the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), with support from Mr Tinubu and other party leaders.

In 2011, Mr Ribadu contested the presidency under the Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN), a party led by Mr Tinubu. In 2015 and 2019, Mr Tinubu supported Mr Buhari’s presidential bids under the APC.

However, Mr Tinubu and Atiku subsequently became political opponents, particularly during the 2019 and 2023 presidential elections, when the former vice president contested under the PDP while Mr Tinubu was in the APC.

Mr Shettima’s remarks were part of the APC’s effort to highlight Mr Tinubu’s history of political alliances and support for politicians from Northern Nigeria as the party seeks another presidential term for him in 2027.

Top government officials attend the rally

The event attracted senior federal government officials, APC governors and party leaders from different parts of the country.

Those in attendance included Vice President Kashim Shettima and Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani, who received Mr Tinubu upon his arrival in the state.

Secretary to the Government of the Federation George Akume was also among the senior officials at the event. Other attendees included ministers, senators, members of the House of Representatives, APC governors and prominent party figures.

APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda and Abdulaziz Yari, director-general of the party’s presidential campaign council, were among the party leaders involved in preparations for the rally and efforts to mobilise support for Mr Tinubu’s re-election.

The event marked the official launch of the APC’s presidential campaign, as the party seeks to consolidate its support base ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Ghana News.title: Obama attacks Trump as he campaigns for Democrats ahead of midterm elections
Ghana News.content:
Former President Barack Obama has attacked the Trump administration over the Iran war and high consumer prices as he hit the campaign trail for Democrats ahead of the US midterm elections.

"This election is our last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration," Obama told crowds in Ohio on Saturday.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump touted his administration's immigration and tariff policies at a rally in Georgia, telling supporters "we're in the golden age of America".

The midterm elections on 3 November will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump's term, and therefore how easy it is for the president to carry out his plans.

Early voting has already begun and Trump cast his ballot on Saturday in Florida alongside his wife First Lady Melania Trump.

Speaking on Saturday in Ohio and Michigan, Obama targeted Trump and his cabinet members, at one point mocking the president's attempt to redecorate the White House.

"After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, 'enough is enough,'" the former president said in Cleveland.

Obama said he sympathised with voters who rejected Democrats in 2024 over economic and inflation concerns following the Covid pandemic. But he said Trump had only himself to blame for the current state of the economy.

"If you thought everything was too expensive before 'you know who'," he said, referring to Trump without using his name, "everything is more expensive now".

Trump, meanwhile, acknowledged that oil prices were "temporarily high" but said "our country is getting stronger and stronger all the time, and those pump prices are going to come down".

The Republican president has faced significant pressure to lower fuel prices, which have jumped due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

Talking up the economy, Trump told the crowd in Perry "we're taking in massive amounts of money through tariffs", and repeated his pledge to offer every adult American a $5,000 (£3,700) payout if Republicans win both chambers of Congress.

He also took aim at the Democrats, telling the crowd they would "loot your wealth" and "annihilate your borders".

Using derogatory language, he accused the Democrats of trying to open up immigration from Libya, Yemen, Haiti and Somalia - countries which he described as "terror-infested".

Describing a previous meeting with several senators, he recalled: "I said, 'Why do we always have to take people from shithouse countries? Why can't we take people from, like, well... Norway, Sweden? Why not Denmark?'"

Ghana News.title: Luv FM journalists sweep top honours at GJA Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards
Ghana News.content:
Journalists from Luv FM, a subsidiary of the Multimedia Group Limited, have won multiple awards at the 2025 Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards.

Four journalists from the Kumasi-based station received honours across several categories, with Emmanuel Bright Quaicoe taking the night's top prize as Ashanti Regional Journalist of the Year.

Mr Quaicoe also won Best Feature Production, Best Agriculture Reporter, and placed second in Best Entertainment Journalism.

Emmanuel Bright Quaicoe

Clinton Yeboah secured first place in both Best Health Journalism and Best Business and Economy Journalism.

Clinton Yeboah

Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom won first place in Best Community Impact Journalism, placed second in Best Health Journalism and finished third in Best Environment, Science and Climate Journalism.

Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom

Mahmud Mohammed-Nurudeen also swept awards, including Best Science, Climate and Environment Reporter, and placed third in the Best Feature Production Category

The awards recognise journalistic work across different beats, including health, business, entertainment, environmental reporting and community impact.

Mr Quaicoe’s overall regional award, alongside the category wins secured by his colleagues, highlights the range of reporting represented by the Luv FM team.

The GJA Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards celebrate journalists whose work contributes to public understanding of issues affecting communities across the region.

Luv FM, based in Kumasi, is part of the Multimedia Group’s network of radio and television stations in Ghana.

The regional winners are expected to feature in the broader national awards calendar, although their participation and final standings at the national level will depend on the applicable GJA arrangements.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Serbia votes in election pitting longtime leader against student movement
World.content:
Polls show populist leader Aleksandar Vucic in a tight race against the anticorruption and anti-authoritarian movement.

Serbians are voting in parliamentary elections amid a mass student protest ⁠movement that seeks to oust longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vucic, who has held power as prime minister and then president for more than a decade.

The snap elections, called by Vucic in September, follow almost two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption ⁠and creeping authoritarianism, triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the city of Novi Sad in 2024.

The students have since gained widespread support.

A loss for Vucic ⁠would mark a profound political shift in the Balkan country of some 6 million people, reminiscent of the defeat of Hungary’s Viktor Orban in April.

But Vucic, who resigned as president in September to run again for prime minister, is a strong incumbent. Many voters thank him for pulling Serbia out of economic obscurity and ‌orchestrating a period of sustained modernisation.

“The Serbian election ⁠is shaping up to be a watershed moment for the country as the Student List mounts the biggest challenge against Vucic yet,” Mario Bikarski, senior Europe analyst at risk consultancy Verisk Maplecroft, told the Reuters news agency.

During the campaign, Vucic has promised higher pensions and public sector salaries, investment in state healthcare, and subsidies for young couples. He has balanced closer ties with China, a major investor, and Russia, Serbia’s traditional ally and principal supplier of natural gas, while leaving the door open to joining the European Union.



But relations with the EU have frayed under his leadership, with the bloc growing increasingly frustrated over a lack of reforms addressing the judiciary, the rule of law and corruption.

The Student List movement’s agenda focuses on rooting out corruption and improving schooling, while saying little about their international ambitions.

Their roster of 250 largely unfamiliar candidates, including university professors, actors and farmers, is led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic.

Opinion polls are predicting a tight race.

An Ipsos poll published on Thursday gives Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party 47 percent ⁠of the vote to the students’ 40 percent, though other polls have put the students ahead.

Rights groups and activists say repression has worsened since the deadly train station canopy collapse, which was widely blamed on government corruption and sparked the student demonstrations.

About 150,000 supporters of the student movement rallied in central Belgrade on Thursday.

Vucic and his party have repeatedly denied accusations of repression, corruption and spying on their opponents.

The former president claims the students are funded by foreign agents in Croatia and Montenegro, a charge the students deny.

World.title: Obama joins El-Sayed in Michigan rally cry before key midterms
World.content:
NewsFeed Obama joins El-Sayed in Michigan rally cry before key midterms

Former US President Barack Obama joined Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed at a Detroit rally ahead of key midterms. With Black residents making up about 75% of Detroit’s population, Obama denounced attempts to portray candidates as un-American over their faith or background.

World.title: New York Archdiocese agrees to pay $800m to 1,300 sexual abuse survivors
World.content:
The settlement is the second-largest after an $880m ​deal reached by the Archdiocese of Los ​Angeles in 2024.

The Archdiocese of New York has agreed to pay more than $800m to settle the legal claims of about 1,300 survivors of sexual abuse by clergy.

New York Archbishop Ronald Hicks said on Saturday that the settlement will be formally signed on November 6 after an agreement with the plaintiffs and their lawyers.

“We are on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors,” he wrote in an email sent to his priests and shared by the archdiocese’s news outlet.

“This agreement will also allow the archdiocese to turn its full attention once again to its mission of preaching the Gospel, healing the sick, caring for the poor and needy, welcoming the stranger, and educating our children,” he added.

According to The New York Times, which broke the story, each of the approximately 1,300 survivors will receive at least $250,000 from the Archdiocese of New York and potentially more depending on the severity of the abuse suffered.

The settlement is the second-largest of its kind after an $880m deal reached by the Archdiocese of Los Angeles in 2024.

“The unanimous agreement of survivors who filed claims against the Archdiocese of New York marks a powerful moment in the pursuit of justice,” Jeff Anderson, a lawyer representing people who filed more than 1,000 claims against the Catholic Church in New York state, said in a statement.

“Through their courage, sacrifice, and determination, survivors have helped bring about a reckoning and a meaningful step toward accountability.”



Scandals and settlements

The agreement marks the end of years of negotiations with lawyers representing the plaintiffs, as the Catholic Church in the United States has been mired in sexual abuse scandals since the early 2000s.

In the 2000s, media investigations revealed that Catholic priests in the US had committed sexual abuse against thousands of children over several decades, and that church leaders had often covered up these cases or transferred the offending priests instead of reporting them to civil authorities.

Dioceses across the country have had to pay hundreds of millions of dollars in damages, and programmes have been created to compensate survivors without going to trial.

In June, the Archdiocese of San Francisco announced it had reached an agreement to pay $395m to about 530 survivors of sexual abuse committed by its clergy to settle their lawsuits.

World.title: Thousands rally in Turkiye over journalist arrests, media shutdowns
