NewsFeed Thousands rally in Turkiye over journalist arrests, media shutdowns

Thousands have protested across Turkiye against the arrests of journalists and restrictions on independent media. Authorities have jailed reporters, seized control of opposition broadcaster Halk TV and blocked news websites. The government denies targeting journalists for their work.

World.title: El Clasico awaits a Yamal vs Mbappe showdown on Mourinho’s return to La Liga
World.content:
Barcelona vs Real Madrid will see the return of Spanish football’s fiercest rivalry between two star-studded teams.

Share ‘A match like no other’: El Clasico awaits a Yamal vs Mbappe showdown on social media

Barcelona, Spain – It has been 15 years since Jose Mourinho was first thrown into the ring of fire at Camp Nou and the famously polarising manager’s Real Madrid side was handed a La Liga battering by Barcelona.

The home team’s supporters have not forgotten that cold November night from 2010, when Pep Guardiola’s men stamped their authority with a 5-0 win.

It became an enduring image of a rivalry that spilled from the pitch onto the touchline, sparking heated confrontations among players and bitter exchanges between managers for years to come.

Now, Barcelona – the city and the club – are ready to “welcome back” Mourinho on his second stint as the manager of their fiercest rival.

“I remember the 5-0 [scoreline] but also the tension,” recalls Aleix Soler, a Barcelona fan.

“You’d spend the whole week arguing about the game even before a ball was kicked,” he tells Al Jazeera at a Barcelona fan zone.

The 35-year-old culer – as Barcelona’s supporters are known – will watch the match, having also attended games during Mourinho’s first Madrid spell.

“Beating Madrid is always special, but against Mourinho, you’re still smiling on Monday morning.”

Points, pride and bragging rights

As Mourinho returns to the fixture after 13 years on Sunday, he will face another Barcelona side that has set a punishing pace in the league.

The spotlight will be on Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe – with their growing rivalry adding another dramatic layer to the plot.

The two forwards meet a day before the Ballon d’Or award ceremony in London, bringing individual ambition to a contest that isn’t shorn of consequences for either club.



Barcelona have won all nine of their league games, scoring 39 goals, and lead Madrid by six points.

Victory would stretch that gap to nine. A Madrid win would not only reduce it to three points, but also inject new belief in Mourinho’s side.

Mourinho acknowledged the significance of the occasion after his team’s Champions League victory over RB Leipzig on Wednesday.

“It’s another league match, but it’s not a match like the others,” he told local broadcaster Movistar.

Madrid are third in La Liga standings, behind Atletico Madrid, and have lost six of their past seven Clasicos. Mourinho must find a way to interrupt that pattern before the title chase intensifies.

Contrasting forms, identical headaches

While Hansi Flick has made this fixture a source of strength for Barcelona in his two years as manager, the hosts approach it with their own questions after a 4-2 defeat at Paris Saint-Germain, their first loss of the season, on Tuesday.

Barcelona scored freely against Getafe, Galatasaray and Real Betis before travelling to France. In Paris, their attacking threat remained but defensive absences and the spaces opened up to PSG made the evening uncomfortable.

Barcelona defenders Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde were out injured, leaving Flick with Xavi Espart and Joao Cancelo as full-back options on either side of Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin.

Kounde remained absent from training on Friday, while midfielder Dani Olmo’s adductor injury further narrowed the coach’s options.

Madrid enjoyed a more encouraging European evening, beating Leipzig 4-1 with goals from Bernardo Silva, Arda Guler, Mbappe and Yan Diomande.

Their three wins from three Champions League games offer a foundation, even if domestic consistency has proved harder to establish.

However, they will face Barcelona without the suspended Vinicius Junior, removing one of their most dangerous runners and leaving Mourinho with another decision to make about Mbappe.

Yan Diomande offers an alternative on the left, while Guler’s passing and Jude Bellingham’s movement could be essential to getting Madrid’s leading scorer into dangerous positions.

The task begins with escaping Barcelona’s pressure. If Madrid can move the ball beyond the first challenge and find a passer facing forward, Mbappe can attack the space behind Flick’s defensive line.

For Barcelona, maintaining pressure on that passer will be as important as tracking the run. Retreat too readily, and they risk losing the compact shape that allows them to recover possession and keep attacks coming.



Federico Valverde’s recent deployment at right-back gives Madrid another route forward, with his overlapping runs complementing teammates who move inside.

Whether Mourinho keeps him there will help determine the balance between creativity and defensive cover in midfield.

Yamal vs Mbappe: Battle of the forwards

Madrid must decide how much attention they can afford to give Yamal.

The young sensation’s dribbling can draw a second defender towards Barcelona’s right wing, but that help comes at a cost elsewhere as Pedri can redirect possession towards the space left open.

Meanwhile, Raphinha’s movement threatens opponents concentrating on the ball, and his 12 league goals underline the danger of treating Barcelona as a one-man attack.

Stopping Yamal from beating his marker will achieve little success if the supporting defensive movements leave another player free.

For Real Madrid fans, one glorious night at Camp Nou could be seen as a turning point.

“Winning there would make me believe we can win the league, especially if we play with courage”, says Lucia Martin, a Madrid supporter.

The 26-year-old is travelling to Barcelona with her father to attend the game, and much of her hope rests on Mbappe, although she wants the team to share the responsibility.

“When he gets the ball, I always think something can happen, but we can’t spend 90 minutes waiting for him to rescue us.”

Despite leading all conversations around the match, Yamal and Mbappe will rarely confront each other directly; their influence will be measured in the problems they create for everyone else.

Yamal has eight goals and six assists in nine league appearances. Mbappe has nine goals and two assists across the same number of games.

One can pull defenders towards the ball before releasing a teammate, the other can force them backwards with the threat of a run.

Both are nominees for the upcoming Ballon d’Or and although the match falls outside the assessment period for this year’s award, it will serve as the perfect build-up to one of the most hotly-contested awards in recent years.

Before football celebrates its outstanding performers in London, two of its strongest claimants to the title of world’s best will share a stage where reputations are tested under exceptional pressure and strengthen their claim as the world’s best.

On the eve of the Ballon d’Or, Yamal has a chance to extend Barcelona’s perfect start and deepen Madrid’s frustration.

For Mbappe, there is the opportunity to bring his team back into the race at their rival’s expense.

World.title: Bulgarians vote for president in shadow of Russia’s war in Ukraine
World.content:
The two leading candidates condemn recent deadly Black Sea drone strikes but differ on the Ukraine war more broadly.

Share Bulgarians vote for president in shadow of Russia’s war in Ukraine on social media

Bulgarians are voting in a presidential election amid the spread of Russia’s war on Ukraine to the waters off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast.

Ahead of Sunday’s vote, President Iliana Iotova, 61, and ex-caretaker Prime ⁠Minister Andrey Gyurov, 50, were leading a field of 27 candidates in the polls.

⁠The presidency is a largely ceremonial post in Bulgaria. While major policies must be approved by Parliament, direct election gives the president greater political authority. The president leads the armed forces and can veto legislation, sign international treaties and appoint ambassadors.

The election has also gained attention after a series of drone attacks on merchant ships off Bulgaria’s coast that likely killed some two dozen international seafarers.

The drone strikes ‌sparked international condemnation and concerns about the growing reach of the war in Ukraine, prompting Bulgaria to seek allied assistance to bolster its maritime security.

The Bulgarian government has stopped short of explicitly blaming Russia for the attacks, but Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the outcome of the strikes “benefits the Russian Federation”.

Relations with Russia, West at stake

The two leading candidates for president have both condemned the strikes, but they differ on the broader war in Ukraine.

Gyurov, who served as caretaker prime minister this year, is backed by ⁠pro-Western, reformist parties and has long expressed support for Ukraine. He ⁠signed a security cooperation agreement with Kyiv during his time as premier.



“I want Bulgaria to have a voice of its own in Europe, a reliable NATO ally that defends its interests through preparedness, strong diplomacy and ⁠a clear position,” he said at a rally on Thursday.

Iotova, a former vice president, became acting president in January after Radev resigned to ⁠enter the parliamentary race, which he won on what many ⁠political analysts considered a Kremlin-friendly ticket.

Radev supports Iotova, and they both call for a diplomatic end to the war.

“My opponents argue that there must be ‌a war of attrition,” Iotova told a rally on Thursday. “The truth is, we are all the ones who are most exhausted.”

While there is a broad consensus among the parties in Parliament on the country’s pro-Western path, widespread pro-Russian sentiments based on traditional historical and cultural ties with Russia have divided society, particularly since the start of Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Dobromir Zhivkov, managing director of the Market Links polling agency, said Iotova is among those who advocate that Bulgaria take a more neutral position.

“They call for an end to aid for Ukraine and a halt to arms deliveries to Ukraine; we often hear them use Kremlin rhetoric and terminology borrowed directly from Kremlin propaganda,” he told The Associated Press news agency earlier this week.

Run-off vote expected

Candidates are also addressing public fears about the steep rise in energy prices and surging inflation, with many Bulgarians in rural areas struggling to make ends meet.

Polls by Alpha Research give Iotova 41 percent of the vote and ‌Gyurov ‌28 percent.

Voting starts at 7am (05:00 GMT), and polls close at 8pm (18:00 GMT).

Analysts expect none of the 27 candidates to secure the outright majority needed to win in the first round, however.

Turnout must also be above 50 percent of the 6.6 million registered voters, and Sunday’s turnout is expected to be less than 40 percent, which means a likely run-off on November 1.

World.title: Mass rally against Netanyahu ahead of pivotal Israeli election
World.content:
NewsFeed Mass rally against Netanyahu ahead of pivotal Israeli election

World.title: Obama slams Trump’s ‘cruelty and corruption’ as he rallies Democrats
World.content:
Former US president says Trump ‘chose to make a series of bad decisions’, highlighting the US-Israel war on Iran.

Share Obama slams Trump’s ‘cruelty and corruption’ as he rallies Democrats on social media

Barack Obama has criticised the “cruelty and corruption” during US President Donald Trump’s second term, as the former president campaigned for Democratic candidates in two Midwestern states.

Obama delivered scathing criticism of Trump on Saturday at a midterm election campaign rally in Ohio, slamming his successor’s foreign policies.

“The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions,” the 65-year-old Democrat said in Cleveland. “Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for,” he added, referring to the US-Israel war on Iran.

Obama urged Ohioans to vote against the Republican administration, saying: “After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘Enough is enough’.”

Later on Saturday evening, Obama headed to Michigan to campaign for Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Democratic gubernatorial candidate Jocelyn Benson.

At the Detroit rally, he framed the November 3 vote as a “circuit breaker” to “at least rein in some of the foolishness” of Trump’s presidency. “We have never seen a president excel in straight-up grifting, ⁠on your dime, like this,” Obama said.

“Never seen a president so intent ⁠on selling favours like this,” he also said, adding that the Republican Party “seems to stand for corrupt government, or inept government, or no government”.



Obama ridiculed the Trump ⁠administration’s claims of victory against Iran. He argued that the war has given Iran more economic leverage because its threats to attack shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have unsettled oil exporters.

“Iran now has veto power over the Strait of Hormuz, ‌where oil goes through to get to the world,” Obama said.

Criticising Ramaswamy ad

The former president also addressed the recent controversy in Ohio’s gubernatorial race surrounding an attack  by Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy against Democrat Amy Acton.

“In recent days, we’ve seen there is no line he will not cross, no low he will not sink to,” Obama said of Ramaswamy. “I don’t know what’s happened where the standards of behaviour are so low that somebody could run an ad like that.”

In the , Donna Arthur, Acton’s mother, disputes her daughter’s account of a childhood involving homelessness and ⁠⁠⁠⁠sexual abuse by her stepfather, urging Ohioans not to vote for her.

Acton says she has not seen her mother since 1978. Acton’s brother has supported her account of being sexually abused by her stepfather when she was a child. The stepfather, who died in 2004, was charged with rape.

Obama backed Acton, saying that she has “spoken movingly about her painful childhood and all she’s experienced: abuse, neglect and homelessness”.

The former president shared the rally stage with Acton and Ohio’s former Democratic senator, Sherrod Brown.

Trump defended the Ramaswamy  on Saturday, when he cast his ballot early in Florida.

Defending El-Sayed

Obama also condemned critics of El-Sayed, suggesting they are using the 41-year-old politician’s name and Muslim faith to tear him down.

“We have seen this movie before. I starred in it,” Obama told a rally in Detroit. “I’ve got a long-form birth certificate to prove it.”

He added, “Abdul is as Michigan as it gets.”

The former president pushed back against those who call El-Sayed a “radical”, declaring that “Abdul shares my values”.

Obama remains the Democratic Party’s best motivator nearly a decade after leaving the White House. And he is taking his star power on the road in the final days of the midterm elections, which will help determine the balance of power in US politics on November 3.

Obama will headline a Democratic Party rally in Georgia next week with Senator Jon Ossoff and gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms.

Trump spoke in Georgia on Saturday.

World.title: Almost 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
World.content:
Nearly 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands of people took part in another day of protests across France which were followed by some clashes late on Saturday, officials have said.

After a day of largely peaceful demonstrations, police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in a number of cities including Paris, while barricades were set alight in Marseille and people ripped boards from a shop in Bordeaux.

But officials have so far managed to avoid rioting and looting on the scale seen last weekend, which resulted in some of the worst scenes of disorder in France's modern history.

The interior ministry said an estimated 410,000 people protested on Saturday, while the unions put the number at about 800,000.

World.title: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
World.content:
Ukraine now has a "stable connection" to Starlink, its defence minister has said, after its military suffered days of restricted connectivity on the satellite internet network.

Kyiv relies on the Starlink and its military-grade counterpart Starshield for piloting drones and operations within Ukraine, but last week accused US President Donald Trump of telling owner Elon Musk to place limits on it.

This meant drones would lose connection when travelling at 161km/h (100mph) or more, it said. Trump denied doing so before saying Musk had "put it back".

Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said that speeds of more than 400km/h were now possible on the network, indicating that full capability had been restored.

"This result is above all important for our front, for our soldiers, for the operation of drones, for logistics and for communications," he said in a statement on Saturday.

Ukraine's military uses the network of 10,000 low Earth orbit satellites extensively for military operations, particularly in remote areas on the battlefield.

Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, which Musk said was controlled by the US military when he suggested the Pentagon could be behind the recent issues.

Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, so when Ukraine sends long-range missiles or drones deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work.

The debacle over Starlink began last week, and emerged during a broader diplomatic row between Trump and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.

Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move criticised by Ukraine and its European allies.

World.title: Palestinian families displaced as Israeli forces demolish Hebron homes
World.content:
The Israeli military has launched a sweeping crackdown in the occupied West Bank, demolishing homes and businesses in the city of Hebron and displacing hundreds of families, according to local officials.

Footage shared online showed destruction caused by Israeli bulldozers, with at least one whole street appearing to have been flattened. The military has also cordoned off the city, heavily restricting the movement of its 200,000 residents.

The operation was announced by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday, in response to the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen in an attack on a checkpoint. Three other Israeli soldiers were injured, and the gunmen were also killed.

Netanyahu said on Friday that buildings around the site of the attack and the neighbourhoods that the two gunmen were from would be "destroyed".

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said about 2,000 residents had been displaced by the operation, which centred on the Ein Deir Baha and Farsh al-Hawa neighbourhoods, and targeted homes, businesses, industrial sites and infrastructure.

He said dozens of families had been forced to spend the night outside, with some told to leave without taking their vehicles, while homes were marked for demolition with spray paint.

He added that he believed the military planned to displace a total of 2,500 people from about 0.35 sq km of urban land. The city's governor and deputy mayor meanwhile said at least 200 families had been displaced.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) did not respond immediately to the BBC's request for comment. It said in a statement on social media that it had dozens of targets across the West Bank and that its operations would last for several days.

World.title: Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
World.content:
Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a 33-year-old German man during a fire at Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat, the Kehlsteinhaus, also known as the Eagle's Nest.

Dispatchers in Traunstein received a fire alarm from the building at 21:15 local time (19:15 GMT) on Friday and firefighters found it engulfed in flames.

Some 200 emergency personnel were deployed to the scene where the blaze was still burning early on Saturday, as police said difficult terrain hindered efforts to bring the fire under control.

Police said they apprehended the man riding a motorcycle near the scene, German media reported. A criminal investigation has been launched.

There is currently nothing to suggest the involvement of further suspects, police official Gerhart Holzinger told a press conference on Saturday afternoon.

Public prosecutor Rainer Vietze said a psychiatric report had concluded the 33-year-old man showed signs of possible mental illness and diminished responsibility might therefore be assumed.

Vietze said a possible political motive was also being considered, but stressed the investigation was in its early stages.

The residence, above the town of Berchtesgaden, was one of several buildings in the area used by the Nazi dictator and his entourage during World War Two.

Hitler and top Nazi officials used his nearby Berghof residence to plan the invasion of the USSR in 1941 and the whole complex was considered one of his headquarters.

He also used the area as a backdrop for propaganda films portraying him as a lover of animals and nature.

Local media reported that site had been "largely destroyed" and the public was urged to avoid the area.

Bavaria's Interior Minister Joachim Herrmann told reporters that the site would "under no circumstances remain a ruin", broadcaster BR24 reported. "It is important that we continue our work of remembrance," he added.

World.title: Father who killed Oregon school gunman describes anguish over children he couldn't save
World.content:
A father who fatally shot a gunman at his daughters' school in the US state of Oregon has described his anguish over being unable to save more pupils after "hearing children pleading for their lives".

Three students and a teacher were killed by a 16-year-old former student at Silver Rail Elementary School earlier this month. The attacker was then killed by Kaylub Giamanco.

"I want to apologise for not saving their babies," Giamanco, who has been hailed as a hero, said of his thoughts for the parents of the children killed, in an interview with Oregon Public Broadcasting (OPB) that aired on Friday.

"The gratitude for saving people's children is awesome, but there were ones that I didn't save."

Giamanco, 36, said he wanted to meet the victims' families and "cry with them and hold them".

He credited a teacher who fought the attacker with giving him the chance to intervene without losing his own life.

"I would love to give her a hug because that's a real true hero," he said.

The students who were killed were all boys, aged five, eight and 11. They were among six people in total who were shot in a classroom at the school, police said. Alongside the teacher who was killed, another child and a teacher were wounded.

Giamanco told OPB that the day of the attack began with breakfast and making packed lunches. He and his wife had spent extra time getting their daughters ready because it was school picture day.

The carpenter had taken lunch to work but decided to go home to eat with his wife instead. That decision brought him past the school as the attack began.

He initially wondered whether someone carrying a long gun was playing a prank. Then he saw him fire at a pickup truck and head towards the school.

Giamanco retrieved a handgun from his vehicle and called emergency services.

"I said, 'I'm sorry, I have to go in. People are going to die'," he told the broadcaster.

He followed the attacker, who shot through the school's locked glass doors. Hearing children pleading for their lives and more gunfire, Giamanco crawled towards the building.

"I told myself this is probably the last thing that I'm ever going to do," he said.

World.title: British woman dies after trying to rescue sons swept away at sea in the Bahamas
World.content:
"She was the purest, most amazing wife, mother and friend to have ever walked this Earth," her husband said in a Facebook post.

"I will never get over this, she was my soulmate, my childhood sweetheart, my one and only. The foundation of my entire family and the strength that held us all together.

"My boys had to witness something nobody should ever have to see of any age, but they know Mum died an absolute hero."

Gregory said he had also set up a fundraising page "for my sons and security after the tragic loss".

In the post on that page he described how his wife, who he had been with for 22 years, had held on to their son until he was rescued "but didn't have the energy to save herself".

He added: "I just have to be thankful for the hero she was in life and in death, and totally grateful for the fact my boys got out safely."

World.title: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
World.content:
Vanessa Trump, the former wife of Donald Trump Jr, has announced that she is cancer-free following her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year.

Trump, 48, who has five children with President Donald Trump's eldest son, shared in a short video on her 19-year-old daughter Kai's Instagram account that her recent tests results "came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free".

Following the Instagram post on Friday, Vanessa and Kai Trump released a longer video on Saturday, in which they discussed breast cancer awareness, early detection and prevention.

Vanessa Trump separated from Trump Jr in 2018 and announced last year that she had begun dating US pro golfer Tiger Woods.

"October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to raise awareness about early detection, education, and support for those affected by breast cancer," Kai Trump wrote on Instagram.

"I sat down with my mom and Dr. Nicole Saphier to talk about my mom's journey with breast cancer and learn more about prevention and early detection," she continued.

Kai's post received over 20,000 likes and hundreds of comments from people offering support and well wishes, including from American singer and media personality Mary Millben.

Vanessa Trump explained in the YouTube video that she experienced arm pain for several months before discovering a pea-sized lump in her breast, which testing confirmed was a cancerous tumour.

"It's a process you have to deal with," she said of the days spent waiting for her test results.

"You have to be mentally strong for yourself because you're going to need the strength to fight whatever challenge it is that's coming towards you."

Trump said she was first diagnosed with breast cancer in April. She publicly announced the diagnosis in May, saying in a social media post that she had undergone surgery and was working on a treatment plan with her medical team.

She eventually had a lumpectomy and radiation treatments, she said.

According to the American Cancer Society, the average risk of a woman in the US developing breast cancer is about 1 in 8, or 13%. The disease also accounts for 30% of all new female cancers every year, according to the group.

Surgery cures most breast cancers, but if some disease remains, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and endocrine therapy can reduce the long-term risk.

Treatments have been advancing, including more targeted therapies for early breast cancer, new types of hormonal therapies, and more precise and effective radiotherapy.

World.title: Three released without charge after fatal arson attack in Ireland
World.content:
Three people, who were arrested in connection with a suspected arson attack which killed four family members in the Republic of Ireland, have been released, gardaÃ­ (Irish police) have said.

Philip and Kim English and two of their children - nine-year-old Jayden and 12-year-old Callum - died after their home in Birch Avenue, on the outskirts of Waterford was set on fire earlier this month.

A man aged in his 20s and a woman in her 30s were previously charged in connection with the attack.

On Saturday, gardaÃ­ said three people - two women in their 30s and a man in his 50s - who were arrested on Tuesday have been released without charge.

A fourth person, a man in his 20s who was arrested on Thursday, remains in custody.

World.title: Poison for profit: Why fake drinks are killing Nigerians and what must change now, By Chukwuemerie Uduchukwu
World.content:
The war against fake and counterfeit products cannot be left to NAFDAC alone. Manufacturers must invest in secure packaging and rapid verification tools. Traders must refuse to stock goods of doubtful origin. Consumers must demand proof of authenticity and report irregularities. Lawmakers must pass the necessary statutes, and enforcement agencies must receive the resources to sustain operations beyond individual raids. Only a coordinated effort across these groups can shrink the space in which counterfeiters operate and restore confidence in the everyday items that sustain households.

The recent surge in counterfeit and fake drinks and consumables across Nigeria has reached alarming proportions, as confirmed by successive enforcement operations that uncovered vast networks of the illicit production and distribution of these goods in major commercial hubs in the country. In Lagos, officials of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) discovered more than twenty illegal stores hidden within the International Trade Fair Complex, where operators blended and repackaged popular alcoholic brands, revalidated expired and unsafe beverages, and stockpiled banned imports on a massive scale. The haul exceeded ₦2 billion in value, with two suspects arrested amid equipment including drums, filters, heating devices, labels, corks, and bottles of whisky, wine, and energy drinks.

Parallel actions in Aba targeted five shops at Old Court Road Market, seizing counterfeit labels, corks, packs, and outer packaging materials worth hundreds of millions of naira that bore the names of well-known brands such as Jameson, Glenfiddich, Four Cousins, Lord’s Dry Gin, and Imperial Blue. A separate facility at Omenazu Street revealed an unhygienic setup for manufacturing spirits and herbal liqueurs, complete with a 200-litre drum of liquid ethanol stored in large containers, dirty sieves, sealing machines, tree barks, and bottles already marked with established labels. These discoveries form part of a broader weekly haul exceeding ₦5.3 billion in seized and destroyed counterfeit products spanning drinks, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, and food items. The pattern is clear: organised syndicates treat the health of the public as a commodity to be diluted, adulterated, or poisoned outright for profit, thereby flooding markets with products that can cause organ failure, chronic illness, or sudden death.

What drives individuals to pursue this murderous trade remains difficult to comprehend. The same people who mix industrial alcohol with flavourings, or who repackage expired stock under fresh labels, live in the same communities where their products circulate. They shop in the same markets, attend the same gatherings, and share the same water and food chains. Nothing shields them or their relatives from the very toxins they unleash. A child who drinks a counterfeit soft drink, a relative who takes a falsified medicine, or a friend who consumes adulterated spirits can die from the very enterprise that was meant to enrich the perpetrator. Greed appears to override even basic self-preservation. The calculation seems to rest on the assumption that the victims will always be strangers, the enforcement will always be temporary, and the profits will always outweigh the risk of detection. Yet, the raids demonstrate that the risk is real and growing. Traders who resisted evacuation of seized materials in Aba only underscored how deeply the trade has embedded itself, turning ordinary markets into nodes of organised harm.

Capital punishment for those who knowingly manufacture, package, or distribute fake drinks, foods, or medicines would signal that the state places the lives of citizens above the profits of syndicates. Such legislation would also equip investigators with stronger tools for asset forfeiture and for prosecuting financiers who never touch the products themselves but bankroll the operations.

The National Assembly must respond with laws that treat the counterfeiting of consumables as a capital offence. Existing penalties have proven insufficient to deter large-scale operators who calculate that fines or short prison terms are merely a cost of doing business. When the product itself can kill, the law should recognise the act as equivalent to premeditated harm against the public. Capital punishment for those who knowingly manufacture, package, or distribute fake drinks, foods, or medicines would signal that the state places the lives of citizens above the profits of syndicates. Such legislation would also equip investigators with stronger tools for asset forfeiture and for prosecuting financiers who never touch the products themselves but bankroll the operations. Delay only allows the networks to reorganise after each raid, relocating equipment and recruiting new fronts, while the public continues to bear the cost in hospital admissions and premature deaths.

The same legislative urgency applies to product authentication. The National Assembly should enact laws requiring NAFDAC to adopt systems already used by sister agencies in other countries. Every manufacturer selling products in Nigeria must include a barcode or pin code concealed beneath a scratch-off panel on the packaging. Consumers should be able to verify authenticity freely through both the manufacturer’s website and the NAFDAC portal, receiving immediate confirmation that the item is genuine and within its approved shelf life. Some pharmaceutical companies have already introduced comparable technology, proving that the infrastructure is feasible and that consumers respond when given a simple means of self-protection. The majority of companies marketing drinks, foods, cosmetics, and other consumables have not followed suit. This gap leaves the market open to counterfeiters who simply copy packaging without any corresponding digital trail. The present moment offers the clearest opportunity for action. Enforcement operations have exposed the scale of the problem, public awareness is rising, and the technical capacity exists. National Assembly members and the NAFDAC leadership can close the loophole by making the scratch-off code mandatory for all regulated products sold within the country, with clear timelines for compliance, and penalties for non-adherence.

The lives already lost or damaged by adulterated drinks and consumables make clear that half-measures will not suffice. The country can either tolerate a trade that treats public health as expendable or it can mobilise every available institution and citizen to end it. The choice will determine whether the next generation inherits markets filled with safe products or continues to navigate a terrain of hidden poisons.

While these measures take shape, ordinary Nigerians must protect themselves through deliberate purchasing habits. Products of any kind should be bought only from reputable stores whose ownership and supply chains can be traced. Medications, in particular, must be obtained solely from registered pharmaceutical outlets staffed by licensed professionals. Street vendors, informal markets, and unverified online sellers present the highest risk of receiving adulterated or expired goods. Checking packaging for signs of tampering, unusual pricing, or missing regulatory marks provides an additional layer of caution, yet the most reliable defence remains the choice of where to buy. Families can further reduce exposure by limiting bulk purchases from unknown sources and by reporting suspicious products or production activities directly to the relevant authorities. These steps do not replace systemic reform, but they reduce immediate harm, while stronger laws and authentication systems are put in place.

The war against fake and counterfeit products cannot be left to NAFDAC alone. Manufacturers must invest in secure packaging and rapid verification tools. Traders must refuse to stock goods of doubtful origin. Consumers must demand proof of authenticity and report irregularities. Lawmakers must pass the necessary statutes, and enforcement agencies must receive the resources to sustain operations beyond individual raids. Only a coordinated effort across these groups can shrink the space in which counterfeiters operate and restore confidence in the everyday items that sustain households. The lives already lost or damaged by adulterated drinks and consumables make clear that half-measures will not suffice. The country can either tolerate a trade that treats public health as expendable or it can mobilise every available institution and citizen to end it. The choice will determine whether the next generation inherits markets filled with safe products or continues to navigate a terrain of hidden poisons.
