World.title: #EndSARS: Cry of justice for victims louder six years after
World.content:
File image of the EndSARS protests.

By Gabriel Ewepu

As Nigerians commemorated the sixth anniversary of the #EndSARS protests on Wednesday, October 20, civil society organisations (CSOs) and lawyers said the issues that triggered the protests remain unaddressed.

They noted that while the core demands of the protesters remain largely unmet, commitments made by the government have also not been realised.

There was a consensus that sacrifices made by those affected in various ways during the protests have not translated into improved policing in the country.

Sunday Vanguard recalls that the #EndSARS protests were a series of nationwide demonstrations that erupted in Nigeria in October 2020 against police brutality, extortion, torture, unlawful arrests and extrajudicial killings allegedly committed by the Special Anti-Robbery Squad (SARS), a unit of the Nigeria Police Force established to combat armed robbery and other violent crimes.

SARS

Although concerns about alleged SARS abuses had persisted for years, the protests gained momentum following the circulation of a video in early October 2020 showing a police officer allegedly shooting a young man in Ughelli, Delta State.

Young Nigerians mobilised through social media, particularly Twitter, using the hashtag #EndSARS to demand the disbandment of the unit, justice for victims of police brutality and comprehensive police reforms. The demonstrations spread to Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Ibadan and other cities, attracting thousands of young people who also called for better governance, accountability and respect for human rights.

On October 11, 2020, the police announced the dissolution of SARS, but protesters continued their demonstrations, insisting on concrete reforms, accountability for alleged abuses and compensation for victims.

Tragic

The movement reached a tragic turning point on October 20, when soldiers opened fire on protesters gathered at the Lekki Toll Gate in Lagos, an incident that attracted international condemnation and became a defining moment in Nigeria’s recent history. Amnesty International reported that at least 12 protesters were killed at Lekki and Alausa in Lagos that day.

Widely referred to as the Lekki massacre, the incident intensified public outrage and renewed demands for justice. Although judicial panels of inquiry were established in several states to investigate allegations of police brutality, concerns over accountability and the implementation of their recommendations have persisted.

To date, the protests remain a significant expression of youth activism and the struggle for police accountability and good governance in Nigeria.

Six years after, some stakeholders, including civil society groups, told Sunday Vanguard that key recommendations by the judicial panels of inquiry were yet to be fulfilled, while the immediate and underlying issues that led to the protests persisted.

Nigerians deserve evidence of transformation — CISLAC

Speaking with Sunday Vanguard, Executive Director of the Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre (CISLAC), Auwal Rafsanjani, said Nigerians deserved evidence of transformation, not another anniversary of unfulfilled commitments.

He said: “Certainly, we cannot describe a relationship built on fear, suspicion, intimidation and widespread allegations of extortion as a healthy police-civilian relationship. Six years after #EndSARS, many Nigerians, particularly young people, still see police encounters as potential threats rather than assurances of protection.

“The reported use of tear gas against citizens commemorating #EndSARS at Lekki today raises further concerns about respect for peaceful assembly. “CISLAC maintains that the greatest tragedy of October 20, 2020, is not only the lives lost and injuries suffered, but also the continued failure to establish full accountability and restore public confidence.

“A police institution that citizens fear more than criminals has a serious legitimacy and accountability problem.

“Government must implement outstanding judicial panel recommendations, ensure justice for victims and end the culture of impunity.”

Torture

“There have been reform announcements and institutional adjustments, but Nigerians are entitled to ask: what has fundamentally changed on the streets?

“SARS was disbanded, judicial panels were established, police regulations were revised and training initiatives introduced.

“Yet allegations of unlawful detention, torture, extortion, excessive force and extrajudicial killings continue. “CISLAC insists that changing the name of a police unit without changing its conduct is not reform.

“Reform must produce measurable results: fewer abuses, independent investigations, prosecution of offending officers, compensation for victims and improved police welfare.

“Six years is more than enough time for promises to become results. “Nigerians deserve evidence of transformation, not another anniversary of unfulfilled commitments.”

Coercion

However, he noted that Nigeria had dedicated and courageous police officers, but institutional weaknesses and persistent allegations of misconduct continued to undermine public confidence.

“Poor welfare, inadequate equipment, political interference, weak supervision and insufficient accountability have complicated effective policing.

“However, none of these challenges excuses brutality or corruption. “CISLAC is particularly concerned about allegations of indiscriminate arrests, unlawful payments at checkpoints, police involvement in civil disputes and intimidation of innocent citizens.

“Policing must move from coercion to service, from intimidation to public cooperation and from impunity to accountability.

“The police must stop treating citizens as subjects to be controlled and start treating them as rights-bearing people to be protected.

“We demand independent civilian complaints oversight, stronger internal discipline, improved personnel welfare and enforceable sanctions against abuse.”

State police

Speaking on the need for state police, considering the current policing challenges in Nigeria, Rafsanjani, who is also Head of Transparency International Nigeria, said: “State police is relevant, but decentralising police powers without decentralising accountability could create 36 additional centres of political intimidation.

“Nigeria’s security challenges require more effective local intelligence, community participation and faster responses to crime.

“However, state police must never become private security organisations for governors or weapons against political opponents, journalists, protesters and vulnerable communities.

“CISLAC supports a properly regulated state policing framework with independent recruitment and oversight commissions, constitutional human rights safeguards, transparent funding and clear restrictions against political interference.

“State policing must also be subject to independent investigations and judicial accountability.

“Nigeria needs policing closer to the people, not armed institutions closer to political power.

“Without these safeguards, state police could reproduce the very abuses that triggered #EndSARS.

“Six years after #EndSARS, Nigeria must choose between accountable democratic policing and the continued misuse of security institutions.

“The sacrifices associated with #EndSARS must not be forgotten, and the 2027 elections must not become another opportunity for security agencies to violate the rights they are sworn to protect.”

2020 demands largely unmet — Global Rights

On his part, Executive Director of Global Rights, Abiodun Baiyewu, lamented that the demands of the protesters remained largely unmet.

He said: “As we commemorate the sixth anniversary of #EndSARS, we invite the Nigerian people, government, especially the Presidency, and security forces to pause and reflect on this tragic incident in which at least 135 protesters were extrajudicially killed across the country during the #EndSARS protest.

“It is worrisome that six years after this tragic event, accountability that is commensurate with the gravity of the atrocities committed is still elusive.

“The demands that brought Nigerians to the streets in 2020 remain largely unmet, and the pattern of impunity has persisted.

“In the more recent incident of the August 2024 #EndBadGovernance protests, Global Rights documented the killing of at least 31 protesters by police across several states and the arbitrary arrest of 1,135 protesters, including children as young as 13 years old.

“To date, there has been no accountability for these killings either.

“Even more worrisome is the fact that this trend is unrelenting.

“Since that incident, Global Rights has recorded at least 545 extrajudicial killings by security forces across the country.

“The repression and continued use of excessive force against protesters, the killing of citizens exercising their constitutional and fundamental human rights, and the continued brazen impunity for security personnel responsible for such violations further expose the hollowness of claims that the grievances that gave rise to #EndSARS have been adequately addressed.

ECOWAS judgment

“The #EndSARS protests were a nationwide demand for an end to police brutality, unlawful arrests, extortion, torture, and the impunity enjoyed by security personnel. “Wearied by colonial brutality against citizens and having endured decades of the savagery of military juntas, Nigerians were hopeful that under a democratically elected government, their rights would be respected and that they would be treated with dignity by the security force that is funded by their taxes to protect them.

“After two decades, realising that change was not forthcoming, they took to the streets to demand a transparent police force that respects the rights of citizens and is not a continuum of the colonial regime or military dictatorship.

“As we soberly reflect on the Lekki Toll Gate incident, we are reminded that these acts of impunity are a stark demonstration of Nigeria’s failure to value and protect the lives of its citizens.

“Nigeria’s perennial insecurity is fast eroding the bonds that bind its people together.

“Its intractable hydra-headed extremism is driven and sustained by this trust deficit.

“In order to extricate the nation from this vicious cycle, the government of Nigeria must urgently do the following: immediately implement the ECOWAS Court judgment on the Lekki massacre.

“We further demand that the Lagos State Government publicly account for its response to the Judicial Panel of Inquiry’s recommendations, specifying what has been implemented, what remains outstanding, and the steps required to give effect to the recommendations it accepted.

“Six years ago, we promised to stand with the victims and their families, however long it takes for the arc of the moral universe to bend towards justice for them, and indeed every citizen of Nigeria.

“Global Rights has not reneged on this promise.

“We remain standing in solidarity with all those who continue to demand an end to police brutality and the right of citizens to protest.

“We honour the courage of those who stood up and keep standing for their rights and reaffirm that no state institution is above the law.”

Citizens-police relationship deeply affected by mistrust — ActionAid

Reviewing the matter, Country Director of ActionAid Nigeria (AAN), Dr Andrew Mamedu, said the relationship between the police and the people remained highly unfriendly.

His words: “Six years after #EndSARS, the relationship between the Nigerian Police and citizens remains deeply challenged by mistrust, fear and unresolved questions of accountability.

“The Lekki Toll Gate incident remains a painful reminder of what happens when institutions established to protect citizens are accused of turning their weapons against them. “The reported use of tear gas against citizens commemorating the anniversary today raises further concerns about how the police respond to peaceful civic expression. “Public relations campaigns alone cannot restore trust.

“They must earn it through respect for human rights, professionalism, and accountability.

“The Nigerian Police must understand that citizens are not enemies of the state, and demanding accountability is not a crime.”

Reforms

Mamedu, however, noted that some reforms had been implemented in the police force since the #EndSARS protests.

“The police have undergone some institutional and policy reforms, including disbanding SARS, introducing new operational regulations, and efforts to strengthen police professionalism”, he said.

“However, the real question is whether these reforms have translated into meaningful changes in everyday experiences.

“Reports of extortion, arbitrary arrests, excessive use of force and other forms of police misconduct continue to raise concerns.

“We must move beyond reforms that exist only on paper.

“We must measure police reform by citizens’ safety and dignity, not by the number of policies announced.

“Six years after #EndSARS, Nigerians deserve clear evidence of accountability, justice for victims and a policing culture that prioritises human rights.

Officers

“The Nigeria Police operate under difficult conditions, including inadequate resources, operational pressures and serious security challenges.

“Many officers continue to serve professionally and make enormous sacrifices to protect communities.

“However, these challenges cannot justify misconduct or violations of citizens’ fundamental rights.

“The recurring complaints of harassment, extortion, brutality and abuse of power require urgent institutional attention.

“We need to shift from a culture of force and intimidation to one of service, community partnership, and accountability.

“A police officer should represent safety, not fear.

“The true measure of effective policing is not how much power officers exercise over citizens, but how effectively they protect their lives, rights and dignity.”

State-controlled

On the issue of state police, the AAN boss asserted: “The conversation around state police is both relevant and necessary, particularly given Nigeria’s complex security challenges and the limitations of centralised policing.

“Decentralised policing could strengthen local intelligence, improve response times and bring security institutions closer to communities. “However, there are legitimate concerns about the possibility of governors and political actors using state-controlled police formations to intimidate opponents or suppress dissent.

“The ongoing constitution amendment process presents an opportunity to address these concerns through proper institutional safeguards.

“We must not decentralise police power without decentralising accountability.

“Any state police framework must guarantee operational independence, transparent recruitment, independent oversight and strong protection against political interference. “Otherwise, we risk reproducing at the state level the same abuses Nigerians have been demanding an end to at the federal level.”

Weed out bad eggs from police — Faro

Lending his voice, human rights lawyer Idris Faro said: “There are bad eggs in every organisation.

“The police must continue to weed out the bad eggs and discipline them appropriately.

“The Nigeria Police has improved in the way they relate with the people since the violent #EndSARS protest, which led to the loss of lives on both sides.

“Evidently, there have been reforms since the nationwide protest, which turned bloody in some states.

“The police have retrained their officers to be respectful in their relations with the people and be professional while suppressing public disorder.

“The use of firearms is for self-defence and the arrest of violent armed criminals. They shouldn’t fire tear gas at peaceful protesters.

“This was reported to have happened at the toll gate at the sixth anniversary. It is wrong.

“As the elections approach, law enforcement officers must work to ensure that we have free and fair elections by providing security for all before, during and after the elections.

“They must bring the full weight of the law to bear against persons and politicians who resort to violence to further their goals. Law enforcers, as the term connotes, work for the law only.”

Six years after, we demand evaluation of policing — Odheke

Similarly, another human rights lawyer, Toluwa Odheke, called for a thorough evaluation of the Nigerian policing system six years after the #EndSARS protests.

Odheke said: “Nigeria’s policing system must be evaluated against a simple constitutional proposition: The police exist to protect the public, enforce the law and safeguard the rights of every person, not merely to maintain the authority of the state.

“The events at the Lekki Toll Gate remain a reminder of the grave consequences that may follow when the use of force, public accountability and the protection of fundamental rights become matters of institutional controversy.

“The continuing importance of that incident lies not only in the question of what happened on 20 October 2020, but also in the lessons that must be learned to prevent comparable failures in the future. “Nigeria has introduced relevant reforms, including the Police Act 2020 and the 2025–2026 police regulations.

“Nevertheless, legislation and administrative directives must be accompanied by effective implementation, independent oversight, transparent investigations and appropriate consequences for proven misconduct.”

Power

On state police, he argued:

“State police may offer advantages in local responsiveness and community engagement, but it must be designed to prevent political capture, discrimination and competing centres of unaccountable coercive power.

“Decentralisation without accountability would merely relocate existing problems.

“As the country prepares for the 2027 general elections, the responsibility of security agencies is particularly clear. “They must protect voters, candidates, electoral officials, journalists and observers impartially before, during and after polling.

“They must not intimidate citizens, obstruct lawful political activity or become instruments for manipulating electoral outcomes.

“Government should therefore make police accountability a measurable institutional priority, not simply a political commitment.

“The relevant test is whether citizens can report abuse safely, whether complaints receive impartial investigation, whether victims obtain effective remedies and whether officers who commit offences are held accountable under the law.

“The ultimate measure of police reform is not the number of policies announced, units renamed or regulations issued.

“It is the extent to which the Nigerian people can trust that the law protects them equally, that the police will respect their rights and that no person is above the law.

“That is the standard by which the legacy of #EndSARS should be assessed, state police should be designed and the conduct of security agencies during the 2027 general elections should be judged.”

Nigerians don’t trust Nigerian police — Onoja

Human rights activist Patrick Onoja asserted that six years after the #EndSARS protests, the relationship between the Nigeria Police Force and Nigerians remained strained.

He said: “Six years after the events of 20th October 2020, I would describe the relationship as one still burdened by mistrust, apprehension and an unresolved demand for appropriate sanctions for proven violations and effective remedies for victims.

“The #EndSARS protests did not emerge in a vacuum.

“They reflected years of public frustration over allegations of brutality, extortion, arbitrary arrests and abuse of police powers.

“The Lekki Toll Gate incident became a defining moment in that crisis.

“Under Chapter IV of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, as amended, citizens enjoy fundamental rights to life, dignity and personal liberty.

“The police are not above these guarantees. Their responsibility to enforce the law must be exercised within the law.

“A police institution cannot effectively protect a population that is afraid of it. Trust cannot be restored through official statements or commemorative events alone. It must be earned through consistent professional conduct, transparent investigations and accountability”.

Visible

Onoja said the Nigeria Police Force remained one of the country’s most visible and important security institutions, with officers operating in difficult circumstances and often confronting serious crimes with inadequate resources.

He said: “Nigeria Police Force remains one of the country’s most visible and important security institutions.

“Officers operate in difficult circumstances, often confronting serious crimes with inadequate resources.

“I acknowledge and commend officers who perform their duties professionally and courageously, sometimes at considerable personal risk.

“However, acknowledging their sacrifices must not prevent us from confronting institutional shortcomings in funding, training, accommodation, equipment, welfare and internal discipline.

“There are also persistent public concerns about alleged extortion and abuse of authority, which must be investigated fairly and thoroughly.

“The police-civilian relationship must be built around policing by consent, the understanding that legitimate law enforcement depends not only on legal authority but also on public confidence and cooperation.

“Years after #EndSARS, Nigeria must move beyond commemoration to addressing the institutional problems that made it a turning point.

“The loyalty of every police officer must be to the constitution and the law, not to the personal interests of any politician.

“We need a police force that is adequately equipped, professionally trained and properly supervised, and an accountability system that protects citizens from abuse.

“The enduring lesson of #EndSARS is that security without accountability threatens freedom, while accountability without effective security undermines public safety. Nigeria must pursue both.”

Vanguard News

World.title: Blaming opposition for hunger is delusional — Atiku
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike & Olayinka Ajayi

Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused President Bola Tinubu of shifting responsibility for Nigeria’s economic hardship to the opposition, insisting that the administration must account for its record ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Read Also: 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally

Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), was reacting to Tinubu’s remark at the APC campaign flag-off in Kaduna on Saturday that the opposition created hunger and poverty in the country.

In a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku described the President’s comment as “either delusion or a staggering case of political amnesia”.

“The APC governed Nigeria for eight years before you took office. You have added another three and a half years. Nigerians know who has been in power, and hardship did not begin when the opposition started talking about it. Stop insulting their intelligence and answer for your record,” he said.

Atiku accused Tinubu’s administration of worsening the hardship faced by Nigerians, arguing that the President could not dismiss concerns about the cost of living by blaming political opponents.

He also criticised Tinubu’s planned inauguration of a section of the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway, alleging that the ceremony showed how disconnected the President was from the daily realities of Nigerians.

“A road cannot be completed with a speech or a ribbon cutting ceremony,” he said.

The former Vice President challenged the administration to explain the removal of the petrol subsidy and the depreciation of the naira, which he claimed had fallen from about ₦471 to ₦1,329 to the dollar.

He also cited a World Bank estimate that 63 per cent of Nigerians would be below the national poverty line in 2026, accusing the government of presiding over rising poverty.

Atiku further questioned the extension of the 2024 budget into 2025 alongside a separate 2025 budget, as well as what he described as ₦7.13 trillion recorded under “energy security” in 2024 and ₦11.2 trillion in NNPC pipeline-related spending.

World.title: Tinubu flags-off campaign, blasts opposition, backs APC governors against Rainbow Coalition
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

President Bola Tinubu on Saturday opened the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign in Kaduna with a direct attack on his political opponents, accusing them of creating the hunger and poverty currently facing Nigerians, while asking supporters to mobilise for his re-election on January 16, 2027.

Read Also: 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally

The President described the opposition as failures and angry people who rely on heckling instead of constructive policy, saying they have nothing to offer the country.

Addressing the crowd at the campaign flag-off, Tinubu said: “I hear my opponents talking about hunger and poverty. Who created it? They did. They created the hunger. They created the poverty we are trying to eradicate.”

He defended his administration’s record, saying: “We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working. I am proud of them. They are developing.”

Tinubu told supporters that a second term would deliver “prosperity, continuity, progress and development,” adding: “To you, the children of our country, it is a promise of second-term prosperity.

You will not regret going to vote.”

He repeatedly asked the audience to confirm that they possessed their Permanent Voter Cards, saying: “Do you have your PVC? Do you have your PVC? Show your hands up.”

The President also dismissed opposition criticism as anger arising from failure. “This is not a matter of hunger; this is not a matter of anger either. Our opponents are angry because they are failures. They have nothing to offer you but heckling,” he said.

“We have prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity. I assure you,” Tinubu declared.

In apparent support of the APC governors’ position against the call by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, for a rainbow coalition, Tinubu urged voters to come out “massively” on January 16, 2027, to re-elect him and support APC candidates across the board.

“Come January 2027, January 16, you must go out massively to elect me again. APC all the way. APC for our governors. APC for our senators. APC for our honourable members of the House of Representatives and all houses of assembly,” he said.

He added: “Your prosperity is here. Your future is in your hands; the fingerprint will reflect it.”

On the pledge by former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, to bring back petrol subsidy if elected, Tinubu said the removal of fuel subsidy belonged to the past and pledged a future free of corruption and economic sabotage.

“Fuel subsidy is in our past. No more corruption. No more falsification of invoices. No more lies. No more smuggling of wealth,” he said.

He praised APC governors, saying: “Out of 36 of them, I can see the development strides they are making in their various states,” and reiterated his promise of “a better tomorrow.”

The Kaduna rally marks the formal launch of the APC’s campaign for Tinubu’s re-election ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election.

He cautioned voters to remain vigilant against lies and ensure that their choices are accurately reflected through fingerprinting.

President Tinubu acknowledged the historical significance of Kaduna State, where political leaders converged before independence.

He offered prayers for the souls of departed leaders, asking God to forgive their sins and grant them peaceful repose.

President Tinubu promised that voters would not regret supporting his re-election, under the pillars of growth, recovery and opportunity.

Key corrections

Speaking earlier, the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima said “Nigeria needs this finest servant to stand together.”

According to him: “What we have done is to fight for the survival of this nation. So, allow me, Your Excellencies, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, to reintroduce ourselves to you and show you that you do not have allies as sincere as we are.

“We were able to keep this country together and defy the predictions of those who had predicted economic failure because we worked together.

“Almost four years ago, you spoke eloquently, sincerely, boldly and decisively to elect a change-maker, His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, as President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

“We didn’t win that election because we were wise, far from it. We didn’t win that election because we were rich, and we didn’t win that election because we were educated. We didn’t win that election because we were the best speakers. We won because you saw the options before you and knew, without a doubt, that the alternative was a calamity.’’

“And for the good people of Kaduna State, we have seen why you, too, were told to renew the mandate of the APC and give His Excellency, Governor Uba Sani a mandate to redeem the fortunes of this great state.

“His wisdom has made Kaduna State a unified place, where the man from Zonkwa sees the man from Zaria as a brother, and where the dividends of our democracy are felt in Kachia as they are in metropolitan Kaduna.

“This is the legacy of the APC in Kaduna State. This is the mandate we have come to ask you to renew: a second term for the APC, from top to bottom.”

Why Kaduna?

On why Kaduna was chosen, the Vice President said: “We have the courage to come to Kaduna State today because we have kept our promise and never reneged on it.

“First and foremost, we promised to restore the glory of Kaduna State as a national centre of learning. Did we deliver on that? We have brought you the Federal University of Applied Sciences, Kachia, haven’t we? We have carried forward the transition to the Federal University of Education, Zaria, haven’t we?

“We have established state vocational institutes in Rigachikun, Soba and Samaru Kataf, with over 4,000 graduates.

“We have committed all our education funding through NELFUND to support hundreds of thousands of students in universities, haven’t we? So, the APC is a party that delivers on its promises.

“And you can bear witness that in 2015 and 2019, President Tinubu stood solidly behind the late President Muhammadu Buhari, securing his first- and second-term victories.

“This is the reason why we have all stood with him to declare our support for Alhaji Bola Tinubu. This is a man of honour, a man of integrity and a man of honour.”

Vanguard News

World.title: Child’s safety must trump family reputation, stakeholders warn
World.content:
…as Vanguard Assistant Woman Editor launches book

By Efe Onodjae

Stakeholders in child protection have called for stronger support systems for survivors of child sexual abuse, warning that family reputation, social stigma and institutional image must not take precedence over children’s safety, dignity and recovery.

They made the call at the public presentation of Flora’s Flower, a book written by journalist and child rights advocate, Funmi Ajumobi, in Lagos, with the theme, “Beyond Justice: Strengthening Support Systems for Child Abuse Survivors.”

The Executive Secretary of the Lagos State Domestic and Sexual Violence Agency, DSVA, Mrs Titilola Vivour-Adeniyi, who reviewed the book, said the culture of silence surrounding child sexual abuse often prevented survivors from speaking out and perpetrators from being held accountable.

She warned families against concealing abuse to avoid public embarrassment, stressing that parents and guardians must create safe environments where children could disclose their experiences without fear of blame, intimidation or rejection.

Vivour-Adeniyi urged parents to take children’s disclosures seriously, report suspected abuse promptly and seek assistance from relevant authorities, healthcare facilities and trauma centres.

She also cautioned against excessive parental control that could isolate children from trusted adults capable of identifying signs of abuse and offering assistance.

The DSVA boss stressed that prosecuting offenders alone was insufficient, noting that survivors also required counselling, medical care, psychosocial support and assistance to return to school and rebuild their lives.

She recommended the use of Flora’s Flower in schools, religious institutions, parent forums and community programmes to promote child protection awareness and encourage reporting of abuse.

Similarly, Mr Olabode Olaoba, who represented the Chairman of the occasion and Special Guest of Honour, Mr Kayode Filani, said justice should extend beyond punishing offenders to protecting survivors, restoring their dignity and preventing further harm.

Olaoba said children who experienced abuse often faced stigma, intimidation, family pressure and disbelief, which could discourage them from reporting their experiences and compound their trauma.

He called for stronger family and community support systems, improved access to qualified counsellors and psychologists, effective implementation of child protection laws and better coordination among relevant institutions.

He urged law enforcement agencies, prosecutors, judicial officers, healthcare providers, teachers and social welfare personnel to adopt child-sensitive approaches that prioritised survivors’ welfare and prevented further trauma.

Olaoba also called on parents, religious leaders, traditional rulers and community stakeholders to provide safe environments where children could report abuse without fear of blame or rejection.

He urged government agencies, civil society organisations, schools, healthcare providers and the private sector to collaborate in ensuring that survivors received comprehensive and sustained support.

Commending the initiative, he called on the organisers to translate the summit’s deliberations into practical recommendations, stronger referral networks and measurable interventions.

He said the success of the initiative should be assessed by the actions taken after the event and their impact on vulnerable children.

The author, Ajumobi, described Vanguard Media Limited as a platform where destinies thrived, talents were nurtured and individuals were empowered to realise their potential.

Expressing appreciation to Vanguard’s Publisher, Mr Sam Amuka; Chairman, Mrs Omasan Dudu; Editor, Mr Eze Anaba; and the board of editors for their support, she said the organisation had provided opportunities for people to discover their voices and develop their abilities.

“For me, Vanguard is more than a newspaper organisation. Vanguard is a place where destinies are allowed to thrive. It is a place where people are given opportunities to discover their voices, develop their abilities and become more than they initially imagined,” she said.

Ajumobi also appreciated former Lagos State First Lady, Dame Abimbola Fashola, for encouraging her to rewrite the book after the first manuscript was claimed by another person.

Explaining the motivation behind Flora’s Flower, she said the book highlighted the need to support child abuse survivors beyond the arrest and prosecution of perpetrators.

She called for stronger support systems, including counselling, medical care, legal assistance and safe spaces where children could speak without fear.

Ajumobi disclosed that part of the proceeds from the book launch would support a breakfast-feeding initiative for children in Ikorodu, Lagos State, to encourage school attendance and reduce their vulnerability.

She said the book was also designed as an educational resource, containing child protection helpline information for different countries to guide survivors towards appropriate assistance.

Flora’s Flower tells the story of Flora, a 16-year-old secondary school student who suffers abuse by people she knows and trusts. It examines how poor communication, family pressure and silence can allow abuse to continue.

The book presentation attracted dignitaries and representatives of government, education, religious institutions, civil society organisations and the private sector.

Those in attendance included Fashola, Chairman of the Lagos Education and Resource Network, LEARN; Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, Mr Mobolaji Abubakre Ogunlende; Senior Special Assistant to the Lagos State Governor on Civic Engagement, Hon. Lijirin Ruth; and Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education, Mrs Abisola Dokunmu-Adegbite.

Others were Vivour-Adeniyi; the Queen of Aponmu Kingdom, Osun State, Olori Janet Afolabi; Senior Pastor, Waterbrooks Ministry International, Ikorodu, Apostle Olaniyi Aniya; and Olaoba, who represented the chairman of the occasion.

Corporate organisations and civil society groups represented included VCare Development Initiative, Child Protection Network, Nigerian Exchange Group Plc, First Adequate Benefit Insurance Broker, Kimpact Development Initiative and Damsy Foundation.

Students and representatives of King’s College, Queen’s College, The Apostolic Church Grammar School, Lyncrest Group of Schools, Ansar-Ud-Deen College, Isolo, Mylod Private School and Pearlshore Academy, Baruwa, Lagos, also attended the event.

World.title: Tinubu: I’m Working to Eradicate Inherited Hunger and Poverty
World.content:
•Shettima: President has consistently supported northern political interests

•Blaming opponents for hunger shameless attempt to dodge responsibility, Atiku replies Tinubu

• ADC mocks APC campaign flag-off over empty seats, rented crowd, recycled promises

• Tinubu’s Kaduna campaign flag-off ‘political theatre’, says Makinde

Deji Elumoye, Chuks Okocha, Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja and John Shiklam in Kaduna

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu yesterday flagged off his 2027 re-election campaign in Kaduna State, declaring that he was working to eradicate inherited hunger and poverty created by his political opponents when they were in power.

Tinubu, who spoke at the Ranchers Bees Stadium, the venue of the All Progressives Congress (APC) rally, promised that his administration would create prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity.

This comes as Vice President Kashim Shettima declared that President Tinubu has consistently supported northern political interests, citing historical instances when the president provided vital political backing to major northern figures facing political adversity.

Meanwhile, Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State has challenged opposition figures presenting themselves as northern candidates to show their track record.

Reacting to Tinubu’s claim that the opposition created hunger and poverty, African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku described it as a delusional and shameless attempt to dodge responsibility for the misery Tinubu’s government has inflicted on Nigerians.

The ADC Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has also described the APC campaign flag-off in Kaduna as a monumental disappointment, accusing the ruling party of relying on rented crowds, empty seats and recycled promises.

Similarly, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has dismissed President Tinubu’s campaign flag-off as political theatre, accusing his administration of failing the North on security, economic welfare and political inclusion.

Speaking at yesterday’s campaign rally, Tinubu accused his political opponents of creating hunger and poverty, which his administration was tackling.

Tinubu stated: “I must thank you for your participation in the past elections. You gave me joy, and I will always remember the victory you gave me to become President. I have come again to thank you and seek your mandate for a second term to fulfill our promise of prosperity, continuity, progress and development.

“I hear my opponents talking about hunger. Who created it? They did. They created hunger and poverty. We are trying to eradicate them. We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working, and I am proud of them. They are developing their states.

“To you, the children of our country, we promise prosperity in our second term. You will not regret going to the polls.

“Do you have your PVC? This is not a matter of anger either. Our opponents are angry… They have nothing to offer you but heckling. We have prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity. I assure you of that.”

The president urged voters to vote for all the ruling party’s candidates during the election.

He noted: “Your prosperity is here. Your good fortune is in your hands. Your fingerprints will reflect this. Be careful. Watch them. Do not let them lie to you.

“What is past is past. Fuel subsidy is in our past. No more corruption, no more falsification of invoices, no more lies and no more smuggling.”

Shettima: Tinubu Had Consistently Supported Northern Political Interests

Also speaking at the rally, Vice President Shettima stated that President Tinubu had consistently supported northern political interests.

“And I want us to bear in mind and go back to the past. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has fiercely identified with the North over the years. It is pertinent to mention that when former Vice President Atiku Abubakar was harassed and chased out of the PDP, with his tail between his legs, he ran to the land of the Jagaban, who gave him political succour, support, and a platform to contest the presidency in 2007.

“Again, in 2011, President Tinubu supported another Northern man, Malam Nuhu Ribadu, to contest for the presidency of this country. You can also see that in 2015 and 2019, President Tinubu stood solidly behind the late President Muhammadu Buhari, who secured his first- and second-term victories. This is why we have all stood with him. This is a mark of honour, and our faith in a man of honour.”

Shettima said Tinubu’s administration had also kept the country together despite predictions of failure and had delivered on key promises.

Shettima also cited several projects delivered by Tinubu’s administration.

Gov Sani Challenges Northern Candidates to Show Records

Kaduna State Governor Senator Sani challenged opposition figures presenting themselves as northern candidates to show their track record, stressing that Tinubu had fulfilled key campaign promises made to Kaduna State in 2022, particularly on road reconstruction and security in Birnin Gwari.

He recalled Tinubu’s visit to Birnin Gwari LGA on December 22, 2022, when the area was the epicentre of insecurity in the North-west.

Addressing the President, Sani said: “At that time, a very senior officer advised you against going to Birnin Gwari because of security concerns. You instantly rejected the advice and travelled to Birnin Gwari with 27 armoured vehicles.”

According to the governor, two promises made during that visit have been met, adding that the 123km Kaduna-Birnin Gwari Road abandoned for over 40 years was under reconstruction.

Sani said the government had released N117 billion to the contractor.

He noted: “Today you can travel to Birnin Gwari with your eyes closed without a single police escort. That is progress.”

The governor challenged opposition figures to show their track record.

“When someone came to us and said we should vote for him simply because he is a northerner, we asked him, can you show us a track record?” Sani said.

Also, the Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, said the campaign would be based on records in the economy, infrastructure, health, education and cash transfers.

“We have been engaging all and sundry, our traditional rulers, our ulama and our imams, to understand the importance of your return in 2027 for continuity, for the peace of this country.”

He added: “The opposition have now upgraded their campaign from Facebook and Twitter to AI. So, I want to call the attention of our supporters to prepare, be watchful and be vigilant.”

For his part, the National Chairman of APC, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, declared that Tinubu has earned the confidence and support of Nigerians through his courageous leadership, commitment to national development, and promise of greater prosperity for the country.

Blaming Opposition for Hunger Shameless Attempt to Dodge Responsibility, Atiku Replies Tinubu

Meanwhile, Atiku has described Tinubu’s claim that the opposition created hunger and poverty as a delusional and shameless attempt to dodge responsibility for the misery his own government has inflicted on Nigerians.

In a statement issued by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, the former Vice President argued that a President cannot light the fire of hardship with his own policies, then blame the neighbours for the smoke.

“Mr President, blaming the opposition for hunger is either delusion or a staggering case of political amnesia. The APC governed Nigeria for eight years before you took office. You have added another three and a half years. Nigerians know who has been in power, and hardship did not begin when the opposition started talking about it. Stop insulting their intelligence and answer for your record.

“The hardship your administration has brought upon Nigerians is real. You cannot deny it by blaming others.

“Your decision to commission the unfinished Abuja to Kaduna Expressway from inside a stadium shows how far removed you are from the daily reality of Nigerians. A road cannot be completed with a speech or a ribbon-cutting ceremony,” Atiku added.

ADC Mocks APC Campaign Flag-off Over Empty Seats, Rented Crowd, Recycled Promises

Reacting to the rally, the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC-PCC, Mr. Kola Ologbondiyan, said an event intended to demonstrate the APC’s political strength across the North-west had instead exposed what he described as the party’s declining public acceptance.

Ologbondiyan alleged that the APC mobilised people from the seven states of the North-west and beyond, with payments reportedly ranging from N50,000 to N100,000 per person. Yet, the stadium, which he put at a capacity of 5,000, remained sparsely occupied.

He added that the turnout, which he described as disappointing, was compounded by what he called the unenthusiastic reception given to the speeches and messages of APC leaders.

Ologbondiyan further alleged that some attendees expressed dissatisfaction with the ruling party after leaving the stadium, chanting the Hausa phrase “Ba mu yi,” which he interpreted as a rejection of the APC and its policies.

The ADC-PCC accused the APC of returning to Kaduna with promises similar to those made during the 2015, 2019 and 2023 election cycles, arguing that the ruling party had failed to account for its years in power adequately.

Tinubu’s Kaduna Campaign Flag-off ‘Political Theatre’, Says Makinde

On its part, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) said the APC campaign event would not erase what it described as broken promises, worsening hardship and declining public confidence in the ruling party.

In a statement issued by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Ihediwa, MDPCO challenged Tinubu to explain what the North had gained from his administration beyond persistent insecurity, economic difficulties and what it called marginalisation.

MDPCO alleged that at least 20,000 people had been killed in northern Nigeria since Tinubu assumed office in 2023, while millions had been displaced by insecurity. The statement did not independently verify the figures.

The organisation further alleged that the North had been marginalised in appointments to strategic federal positions, accusing the APC of treating the region primarily as a source of electoral support.

“No part of the country should be an electoral warehouse to be raided every four years and abandoned after victory,” the group said.

World.title: NDC Fixes Monday for Third NEC Meeting, Presidential Campaign Council Unveiling
World.content:
•Says 80% of candidates received free nomination forms amid economic hardship

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) will unveil its National Campaign Council on Monday as part of preparations for the 2027 general election, while presenting its financial accounts to demonstrate its commitment to transparency and accountability.

The party disclosed this in a statement issued yesterday by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, announcing that its third National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting would be held at 10 a.m. on October 26 at JD Event Centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, Maitama, Abuja.

A major highlight of the meeting, according to the party, will be the National Treasurer’s presentation of the party’s statement of account, a move it said is intended to distinguish its financial management practices from those of other political parties.

The NDC challenged other political parties, particularly the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to adopt similar measures to promote transparency in managing party finances.

The party also attributed its financial limitations partly to the economic difficulties facing Nigerians, claiming that approximately 80 per cent of its candidates could not afford the fees for expression-of-interest forms.

It said it had consequently issued the forms to the affected candidates free of charge to enable them to participate in the electoral process.

The party blamed the situation on what it described as widespread poverty, hunger and deprivation under the APC-led federal government, criticising its economic policies.

Beyond the financial disclosures, the NEC meeting will give the party an opportunity to unveil its National Campaign Council, which it said would coordinate its campaign activities across all levels of government.

According to the statement, the council will encompass the presidential, National Assembly, governorship and state Houses of Assembly campaign structures.

The party also announced plans to present certificates of return to its candidates contesting the various elective positions.

The developments come as political parties intensify preparations for the 2027 general election, with campaign structures, candidate mobilisation and party organisation expected to play important roles in the contest.

For the NDC, the planned unveiling of its campaign council and disclosure of its accounts are intended to project organisational readiness and distinguish the party’s approach to internal financial accountability.

The NDC expressed confidence in its preparations for the forthcoming elections, saying it was determined to offer Nigerians what it described as altruistic leadership.

The statement read, “The leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) wishes to announce that its 3rd National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting will hold on Monday, 26th October 2026, at JD event centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, opposite A-class park, Maitama, Abuja. The time is 10 am prompt.

“A major highlight of the meeting will be the release and presentation of the party’s Statement of Account by the National Treasurer. This reflects our avowed commitment to the principles of transparency and accountability. In this regard, we challenge other political parties, especially the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to emulate this level of openness and transparency in managing their finances.

“For the NDC, it is no longer politics as usual.

“Our finances would have been more robust. However, contrary to speculations in the public domain, and due to the level of poverty, hunger and deprivation in the country occasioned by the rudderless APC and its amorphous economic policies, about 80% of our candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms. The party had to issue forms to such candidates free of charge.

“The party will also use the opportunity of the NEC meeting to unveil its National Campaign Council (NCC).

“As a party of innovation, our NCC is all-encompassing. It covers the Presidential, National Assembly, Governorship, and State Houses of Assembly Campaign Councils.

“Our various candidates will be presented with Certificates of Return for their respective offices.

“The NDC is turbo-charged and ready to give Nigerians the altruistic leadership the nation deserves. A New Nigeria is Possible. We can do it!”

World.title: Crude Oil Price Surges Above $117 Over Fears of Fresh US Strikes on Iran
World.content:
• Oil theft slumps 82.9% to 17,600bpd in five years amid fresh uptick in losses

• Navy uncovers 132,000 litres of stolen crude oil in Bonny

Emmanuel Addeh and Linus Aleke in Abuja

Crude oil prices surged above $117 a barrel at the weekend, reaching their highest level since April, as fears of renewed US military strikes on Iran and escalating threats to energy infrastructure across the Middle East heightened concerns about global crude supplies.

This comes as oil theft and pipeline losses in Nigeria fell by 82.9 per cent in five years, from 102,900 barrels per day (bpd) in 2021 to 17,600 bpd in the first seven months of 2026, amid fresh concerns about further increases in lost volumes after years of decline.

Meanwhile, the Nigerian Navy has uncovered 132,000 litres of stolen crude oil in Allison community, Bonny Local Government Area (LGA) of Rivers State, disrupting a potential storage point in the illicit petroleum supply chain as troops of Operation Delta Sentinel intensified their clampdown on oil theft and economic saboteurs in the Niger Delta region.

Nigeria’s oil benchmark, Brent crude, climbed by about 3.5 per cent to cross $117 a barrel during trading before easing to just above $116, still up approximately 2.7 per cent.

The latest rally followed reports that Washington was considering fresh military strikes against Iran after the November 3 midterm elections, raising concerns that the conflict, now in its eighth month, could escalate further rather than move towards a diplomatic resolution.

Iran had threatened to attack oil facilities, undersea cables, data centres and artificial intelligence infrastructure across the Gulf if the United States and Israel launched a new offensive against the country.

Brent crude traded at about $72 a barrel in February, before the war began, but surged to about $126 a barrel by the end of April as the conflict intensified and concerns mounted over supply security.

Tensions rose again during the week following claims by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) that it struck four commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday.

The US ordered some diplomats and family members of American government employees to leave Saudi Arabia, which had faced continued attacks by Houthi rebels operating from Yemen.

World.title: Oil Theft Slumps 82.9% to 17,600bpd in Five Years Amid Fresh Uptick in Losses
World.content:
Meanwhile, official operational statistics published by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) showed that daily crude oil losses, which fell to a five-year low of 9,100 bpd in 2025, rose by 93.4 per cent to 17,600 bpd between January and July 2026.

The figures in the commission’s fifth anniversary publication, ‘The Upstream Gaze’, highlighted both progress in curbing crude theft and the ongoing challenge of protecting oil production and transportation infrastructure.

According to the data, daily losses declined from 102,900 bpd in 2021 to 55,000 bpd in 2022, representing a 46.5 per cent reduction. The downward trend continued in 2023 when losses dropped to 22,900 bpd, before falling further to 11,200 bpd in 2024 and 9,100 bpd in 2025.

The federal government attributed the cut in crude losses to the combined efforts of the military, local pipeline surveillance groups in the Niger Delta, and the introduction of modern crude measuring devices in the region.

The figures showed that Nigeria’s total liquid hydrocarbon production, comprising crude oil and condensate, gradually recovered from the lows recorded in recent years.

Output averaged 1.63 million bpd in the first seven months of 2026, compared with 1.62 million bpd in 2025, 1.56 million bpd in 2024, 1.47 million bpd in 2023 and 1.38 million bpd in 2022. Production stood at 1.62 million bpd in 2021, the NUPRC data highlighted.

Crude oil production alone averaged 1.46 million bpd in the period under review, up from 1.43 million bpd in 2025, 1.35 million bpd in 2024, 1.24 million bpd in 2023 and 1.14 million bpd in 2022. The figure for 2021 was 1.31 million bpd.

In contrast, blended condensate production continued its downward trend, averaging 170,000 bpd in the first seven months of 2026, compared with 190,000 bpd in 2025, 210,000 bpd in 2024, 230,000 bpd in 2023, 240,000 bpd in 2022, and 310,000 bpd in 2021.

The gradual improvement in crude production also coincided with a significant shift in how the country allocates its oil, particularly the growing share supplied to domestic refineries as Nigeria expands its local refining capacity.

Supply to domestic refineries climbed to 460,000 bpd in the first seven months of 2026, up from 280,000 bpd in 2025, 220,000 bpd in 2024, 20,000 bpd in 2023, and just 10,000 bpd in 2022. Domestic refinery supply was virtually non-existent in 2021.

At 460,000 bpd, local refineries accounted for approximately 29 per cent of the 1.61 million bpd in total crude oil lifted during the period. The allocation represented a 64.3 per cent increase over the 280,000 bpd supplied to domestic refineries in 2025, underscoring growing demand for locally processed crude.

Similarly, the shift coincided with a decline in crude available for export, as the government struggled to meet local supply. Average daily crude exports fell to 1.15 million bpd in the first seven months of 2026, from 1.33 million bpd in 2025; 1.31 million bpd in 2024; 1.47 million bpd in 2023; 1.32 million bpd in 2022 and 1.51 million bpd in 2021.

The latest export figures were down 13.5 per cent from the 2025 level and 23.8 per cent from the 2021 volume.

In the same vein, total crude lifting averaged 1.61 million bpd in the first seven months of 2026, marginally below the 1.62 million bpd recorded in 2025. The figures suggested that the growing allocation to domestic refineries has been accompanied by a reduction in export volumes, rather than a comparable increase in total crude lifted.

World.title: Navy Uncovers 132,000 litres of Stolen Crude Oil in Bonny
World.content:
Meanwhile, the Nigerian Navy has uncovered 132,000 litres of stolen crude oil in Allison community, Bonny LGA of Rivers State.

According to a statement by the Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, the Forward Operating Base Bonny discovered the stolen crude oil under Operation Delta Sentinel, following actionable intelligence.

He said the operation uncovered 10 dugout pits, adding that the site and the recovered products were handled in accordance with extant regulations.

“The operation reinforces the importance of intelligence-led action in identifying concealed petroleum stockpiles and disrupting the infrastructure that enables crude oil theft and the unauthorised movement of petroleum products.

“The Nigerian Navy will sustain efforts to locate and dismantle illegal refining infrastructure and disrupt the networks facilitating crude oil theft across the Niger Delta,” the statement said.

The Navy urged community leaders, residents, traditional institutions and other stakeholders to promptly report crude oil theft, illegal refining, suspicious petroleum storage and the unauthorised movement of petroleum products to the nearest security agency.

Timely, credible information, the statement said, could enable swift intervention and prevent illicit activities from expanding.

“Safeguarding the nation’s critical petroleum assets requires vigilance and active cooperation between security agencies and the communities they serve. The Navy therefore urges the public to remain alert and support lawful efforts to protect national resources,” Folorunsho concluded.

World.title: Amid Improved Economic Indicators, Foreign, Domestic Investors’ Transactions on NGX Hit N15.06tn
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

Foreign and domestic investors’ transactions on Nigeria’s stock market reached N15.06 trillion in the first nine months of 2026, amid key reforms and improved economic indicators.

The Nigerian Exchange Limited’s (NGX) report on domestic and foreign portfolio participation in equity trading revealed that domestic investors continued to dominate transactions, accounting for 89.74 per cent of the total. In comparison, foreign investors contributed 10.26 per cent.

Foreign investors’ share of transactions declined from 21.56 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025 to 10.26 per cent in 2026. Conversely, domestic investors, comprising retail and institutional investors, increased their share from 78.44 per cent to 89.74 per cent.

The report disclosed that domestic investors’ transactions rose to N13.52 trillion between January and September 2026, representing a 102 per cent increase over the N6.69 trillion recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.

Foreign investors, however, accounted for N1.55 trillion, representing a 16.01 per cent decline from N1.84 trillion recorded between January and September 2025.

The shift suggests that the surge in activity on Nigeria’s stock market this year has been driven largely by local capital, particularly institutional investors.

Capital market analysts attributed the growth in institutional investors’ transactions partly to the National Pension Commission’s (PenCom) decision to raise equity investment limits for pension funds in February 2026.

They said the policy had helped inject fresh liquidity into the stock market, supporting gains in the share prices of some blue-chip companies. On February 9, 2026, PenCom revised the investment limits for ordinary shares in Retirement Savings Account (RSA) Funds I, II, III and VI (Active).

The commission amended Section 9 of its investment regulations, raising equity allocation limits for RSA Fund I from 30 per cent to 35 per cent; RSA Fund II from 25 per cent to 33 per cent; RSA Fund III from 10 per cent to 15 per cent; and RSA Fund VI (Active) from 25 per cent to 33 per cent.

Institutional investors accounted for N8.36 trillion of domestic transactions between January and September 2026, compared with N5.15 trillion from retail investors. In the corresponding period of 2025, institutional and retail transactions stood at N4.09 trillion and N2.60 trillion, respectively.

The report also showed that foreign portfolio outflows rose to N913.61 billion between January and September 2026, up from N810.39 billion in the corresponding period of 2025, a 12.7 per cent increase.

Foreign portfolio inflows, however, fell to N632.35 billion, down about 38.6 per cent from N1.03 trillion in the corresponding period of 2025.

Capital market analysts said FTSE Russell’s 2023 downgrade of Nigeria contributed to foreign investors’ exit from the stock market. They described the upgrade in September 2026 as a first step towards attracting them back.

The report put foreign investor inflows in September 2026 at N925.20 billion, up 249.53 per cent from the N264.70 billion recorded in August.

Investors on the Nigerian stock market recorded strong returns in the first nine months of 2026, with market capitalisation gaining N63.73 trillion despite volatility.

Market capitalisation rose from N99.376 trillion at the beginning of the year to N163.105 trillion on September 30, 2026, representing an increase of N63.73 trillion, or 64.13 per cent.

Similarly, the NGX All-Share Index gained 95,598.64 points, or 61.43 per cent, rising from 155,613.03 points at the beginning of the year to 251,211.67 points at the end of September.

With fewer than five new listings, the NGX has recorded substantial growth in 2026, with market capitalisation reaching the N164 trillion mark amid improving macroeconomic indicators.

The report added: “Over 19 years, domestic transactions increased significantly by 160.83 per cent from N3.5560 trillion in 2007 to N9.2747 trillion in 2025, whilst foreign transactions also increased significantly by 329.87 per cent from N0.6156 trillion to N2.6475 trillion over the same period.

“Total domestic transactions accounted for about 78 per cent of the total transactions carried out in 2025, whilst foreign transactions accounted for about 22 per cent of the total transactions in the same period.

“As at 30 September 2026, year-to-date domestic transactions amounted to approximately N13.5159 trillion, representing 89.74 per cent of total market transactions, whilst foreign transactions amounted to approximately N1.5460 trillion, accounting for 10.26 per cent.”

World.title: APC Accuses Atiku, ADC of Plotting to Discredit Tinubu’s Campaign Flag-off in Kaduna With Fake News
World.content:
•Keyamo: ADC presidential candidate jittery over losing north to Tinubu

•Tinubu’s panic cannot erase APC’s terrible record, says ADC

Chuks Okocha, Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja and Chinedu Eze in Lagos

The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) has accused the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, of orchestrating a fake news campaign to discredit its presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna yesterday.

Similarly, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace development, Festus Keyamo, said Atiku was jittery over the flag-off of the presidential campaign of APC in Kaduna because he was afraid of losing the bulk votes which he was hoping to get from the north.

But is swift reaction, the ADC accused the APC of using allegations of fake news to divert attention from the economic hardship Nigerians were facing under President Bola Tinubu.

The APC-PCC in a statement issued statement by its spokesperson, Mr Dele Alake said it uncovered a “well-orchestrated, devious plan” to misinform the public through AI, deepfake videos and counterfeit documents targeted at the APC rally, President Tinubu, Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State and APC leaders.

According to the council, the plot began with the circulation of a picture of a security vehicle on routine patrol near an APC campaign billboard in Kaduna metropolis, which was twisted to claim security agents were deployed to protect APC billboards.

The council said the story was planted in a national newspaper and subsequently shared by Atiku on his social media handles.

Alake added that the second leg was the circulation online of a fake letter purportedly written by Sani to the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, on the purported release of N2.3 trillion by the Kaduna State Government to host the rally.

He added: “We are still at a loss as to how anyone can imagine and concoct this senseless and utterly baseless lie that defies logic and basic common sense.

“How much is the entire annual revenue of Kaduna State, or any state, for that matter, that a state would spend N2.3 trillion to host a rally?” Alake queried.

Alake noted that the alleged N2.3 trillion was more than Kaduna State’s annual budget for three years combined, citing the state’s budgets for 2024 at N458.271 billion, 2025 at N790.439 billion and 2026 at N985.9 billion, which he said were still less than N2.3 trillion.

The council claimed Atiku and ADC had also perfected plans to circulate old, doctored and deepfake videos during the rally to show purported resentment by the people.

Alake said: “We hereby use this opportunity to alert the general public about this malicious and ignoble plan. It is a fact that Atiku Abubakar and the ADC, his special-purpose vehicle, are incapable of winning any election.

“They will pull any strings, no matter how despicable and atrocious, to stay afloat in their desperate bid to grab power at all costs.”

The APC Campaign Council urged Nigerians to be vigilant and reject what it described as machinations of the opposition.

World.title: Keyamo: ADC Presidential Candidate Jittery over Losing North to Tinubu
World.content:
On his part, Keyamo, in a statement titled, ‘Why Atiku Abubakar is Particularly Jittery About the Kaduna Flag-off,’ posted on his verified Facebook account, alleged that the former Vice President had launched ‘blistering online attack’ against APC as the date of the launch got closer.

The minister accused Atiku of being behind the destruction of APC posters in Kaduna and other parts of the north.

“The common but cheap tactic is to position cameras in certain places, procure individuals to tear down the posters of the President, and then post the videos online. The other tactic is to disseminate disinformation claiming that any support the President is seen to receive in the North is procured only through the massive deployment of financial resources. Hence the fake letter alleging a N2.3 trillion deployment for the Kaduna rally. The intention is to generate a hoopla that will create a groundswell of public opinion that President Tinubu has been “massively rejected” in the North,” Keyamo said.

The Minister also said the reason why Atiku was allegedly doing this was because he did not want to lose the bulk votes which he was hoping to get from the north.

“The reason for this is simple: Atiku Abubakar was seriously banking on the bulk of Northern votes to see him through in 2027, knowing full well that he has no inroads at all into the South, given the mood of the country that the South deserves to complete eight years of the Presidency.

Tinubu’s Panic Cannot Erase APC’s Terrible Record, Says ADC

Meanwhile, the ADC has accused the APC of using allegations of fake news to divert attention from the economic hardship Nigerians were facing under President Tinubu.

The ADC Presidential Campaign Council said the ruling APC should focus on defending its record in government rather than accusing it and Atiku of plotting to discredit the APC’s presidential campaign flag-off.

In a statement, the council’s Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, described the APC’s allegations as an attempt to distract Nigerians from rising living costs and the administration’s economic policies.

Shaibu challenged the APC to provide evidence linking Atiku and the ADC to the alleged circulation of forged documents, manipulated images and deepfake videos ahead of the Kaduna rally.

“Until then, his ‘fake news alert’ is an empty political stunt,” Shaibu said, referring to the statement by Alake.

The ADC spokesperson argued that the economic difficulties confronting Nigerians could not be dismissed as propaganda, citing high petrol and diesel prices, food inflation and growing poverty.

He said the APC’s allegations would not change the daily struggles of households grappling with the cost of food, transportation and other essential needs.

On the security presence near an APC campaign billboard in Kaduna, Shaibu questioned the explanation that the vehicle was on routine patrol, asking why the issue had become a subject of political controversy.

He also raised concerns about reports that some APC supporters had travelled long distances to attend the rally and were left sleeping on the streets of Kaduna.

Shaibu further referred to reports of accidents involving APC supporters travelling from Sokoto and Abuja to the event. However, he acknowledged that details of the reported incidents remained unconfirmed.

The ADC spokesperson called on the APC to account for the safety of supporters travelling to the rally, arguing that political mobilisation should not come at the expense of citizens’ welfare.

“Making citizens endure long, hazardous journeys and sleep outdoors simply to create rally optics is political exploitation, not leadership,” he said.

Shaibu also questioned the scope of Tinubu’s campaign activities, alleging that the president was campaigning in only 12 states and suggesting that supporters were being moved between rallies.

He argued that the size of a rally crowd should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of widespread public support, particularly where attendees had been transported from other locations.

“You can hire buses, assemble a crowd and plaster the streets with billboards. You cannot hire consent,” he said.

World.title: Springboks’ injury list increases after brutal weekend
World.content:
This past week it was confirmed by Stormers director of rugby John Dobson that Cheslin Kolbe would miss the Springboks’ end-of-year tour as he continues his recovery from a broken jaw.

There is also an injury cloud hanging over Eben Etzebeth, while the likes of Frans Malherbe, Kwagga Smith and RG Snyman are all sidelined.

As Rassie Erasmus now considers his squad options for the end-of-year Tests, the Springbok coach would have been concerned to see hybrid player Andre Esterhuizen suffer what looked to be a serious ankle injury while in action for the Sharks on Friday, and he joins a growing injury list.



More injury worries for Springboks

On Saturday, the Stormers also picked up several injuries during a brutal battle against the Scarlets, with Deon Fourie and André-Hugo Venter picking up hamstring and elbow injuries respectively.

Fourie, in particular, was expected to tour with the Springboks as the Nations Championship concludes in November, but he is now set for a period out of action.

Meanwhile, Springbok flyhalf Handré Pollard left the field in the second half of the Bulls’ match with a hamstring injury as well.

“It’s been a while since we had so many casualties,” said Bulls coach Johan Ackermann.

Sentiments shared by Stormers boss

Speaking post-match, Dobson said the Stormers were also counting the costs of a hard-fought match.

“The mouth guards (that detect head knocks) were going like pinball. It was ping, ping!” he told the media. “I was reading through my contingency sheet. If you lose both hookers, there’s a plan, but I never thought about three.



“To lose three hookers takes away all our set-pieces. So it is a crisis.”

World.title: Duduzile Zuma-Sambudla’s trial resumes on Monday
World.content:
The trial of former president Jacob Zuma’s daughter, Duduzile Zuma-Sambudla, is set to resume at the Durban High Court on Monday, 26 October 2026.

Zuma-Sambudla faces charges under the Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act (POCDATARA) and incitement to commit violence linked to the July 2021 unrest that swept through parts of Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal following her father’s incarceration.

DUDUZILE ZUMA-SAMBUDLA FACES TERRORISM AND INCITEMENT CHARGES

As mentioned above, Zuma-Sambudla faces three charges linked to the July 2021 unrest, including incitement to commit terrorism and two counts relating to incitement to commit public violence.



The State alleges that her social media posts encouraged violence during the unrest that followed her father’s imprisonment. Zuma-Sambudla has denied the allegations.

The matter was last before the Durban High Court on 13 August 2026, when additional dates were allocated for the continuation of the trial.

The trial, which began on 10 November 2025, is scheduled to run from 26 October to 6 November 2026.



MK Party President Jacob Zuma showed solidarity with his daughter, Duduzile Zuma-Sambudla, outside the Durban Magistrate Court, addressing supporters of the @MkhontoweSizwex pic.twitter.com/4ZBQ3aOIaN — News Live SA (@newslivesa) January 30, 2025

BROADER CONTEXT

The case also tests South Africa’s ability to balance freedom of expression with national security, particularly under the contentious POCDATARA Act, which some legal analysts have criticised for its broad interpretation of terrorism-related offences.

Duduzile Zuma-Sambudla has consistently maintained her innocence and framed the charges as part of a broader campaign to silence voices critical of the state.

World.title: Green ID book countdown: 14-million upgrades in 17 Months
World.content:
Home Affairs wants the green ID book gone by March 2028. But despite recent gains, does it have the capacity to quadruple its services? Image: File

Home Affairs has announced that the green ID book stops being valid form of identification in South Africa on 31 March 2028. At the latest count that represents 14.7-million citizens and permanent residents. Over the roughly 17 months left (at time of publishing), that equates to about 855 000 upgrades per month.

Or 195 000 a week, or nearly 28 000 every calendar day. However, in the last six months, Home Affairs has only affected 1.3-million green ID book upgrades. That’s 217 000 per month. Therefore, it’s going to need South Africans to come forward four-times faster than anything achieved so far …

GREEN ID BOOK COUNTDOWN

As we know, Home Affairs business at bank branches is where all the heavy lifting is meant to occur. About 515 branches now offer walk-in replacements. Capitec alone has reportedly processed more than half-a-million applications at its 248 branches. Plus, Home Affairs says annual issuance has hit a record of four-million smart IDs in 2025.



Better still, the department announced in May 2025 that over 1.4-million naturalised citizens and lawful permanent residents could finally upgrade from the old green ID book, too. This started with applicants from visa-exempt countries. But everyone else in this group is still waiting for their invitation. Minister of Home Affairs, Leon Schreiber, has promised to enable the ‘remaining cohort’ aboard before 31 March 2028.

WHAT HAS TO HAPPEN IN GREEN ID BOOK COUNTDOWN

Banks now offer walk-in green ID book upgrades. You don’t have to prebook through eHomeAffairs. Image: File

The department’s HomeAffairs@Home scheme has no time to waste to meet its deadlines and quadruple service capacity. Bank access needs to expand quickly, with a noted target of 1 000 service points by the end of 2026. Also note that the current figure of 14.7 million excludes new first-time applications turning 16. Moreover, long-suffering naturalised citizens and permanent residents need working access to the system well before March 2028 deadline.

The deadline is firm, but Home Affairs capacity simply isn’t there yet to quadruple green ID book upgrades. And the challenge isn’t the date itself, but rather how government is going to convince millions of people to act long before the deadline comes into view …

But what do you think? Are you going to upgrade from the green ID book to a Smart ID card? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …
