Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro a 79.8% chance of winning the 25 October runoff (25 October, 12:06 a.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 80% and Kalshi at 81% (Lula: 21% and 20% ), as of 25 October, 12:20 am ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open The survey does not say how undecided voters will behave, and polls close at 5 p.m. in Brasília (4 p.m. ET).

A new poll shows Brazil’s runoff tied on the final weekend, with Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro, on 50.1% and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on 49.9% of valid votes. The Futura Inteligência survey, published on Saturday 24 October, puts the gap at 0.2 points, well inside its margin of error.

What the Futura Runoff Poll Found

Futura Inteligência interviewed 2,000 voters by telephone on 23 and 24 October, CNN Brasil reported. The survey has a margin of error of 2.2 points at a 95% confidence level and TSE registration BR-09726/2026.

How Valid Votes and Technical Ties Work

Brazilian results are reported as valid votes, which leave out blank and spoiled ballots. Pollsters publish that figure to match what the electoral court (TSE) will announce on election night.

A technical tie means the gap is smaller than the survey’s margin of error. With 2.2 points of error on each number, this poll cannot say who is ahead.

The Gap Has Narrowed Since 13 October

Futura’s survey of 13 October had Flávio at 51.8% and Lula at 48.2% of valid votes, Exame reported, and the 16 October survey had 50.8% to 49.2%, per Exame. The gap has shrunk from 3.6 points on 13 October to 0.2.

Other pollsters have shown a close race too, and you can compare them in our runoff poll tracker. One survey is a snapshot of two days of interviews, not a forecast.

What It Means for You

If you hold Brazilian stocks, bonds or US-listed shares of Brazilian companies, a race this close can bring sharp price swings once results arrive on Sunday evening. Polls close at 5 p.m. in Brasília, which is 4 p.m. ET.

If you follow US politics or trade, the winner will shape Brazil’s course with Washington for the next four years. A 0.2-point gap means neither candidate is a certain winner.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro a 79.8% chance of winning the runoff and Lula 20.5% (25 October, 12:06 a.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has drawn about US$196.7 million in total bets.

What Is Not Known

Frequently Asked Questions

Who leads Brazil’s latest runoff poll?

Flávio Bolsonaro leads Lula by 50.1% to 49.9% of valid votes in the Futura Inteligência survey published on Saturday 24 October. The 0.2-point gap is a technical tie.

What is the margin of error?

The survey has a margin of error of 2.2 percentage points at a 95% confidence level. It interviewed 2,000 voters by telephone on 23 and 24 October.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October, and polls close at 5 p.m. in Brasília (4 p.m. ET). The winner takes office as president for a four-year term.

What is a technical tie in a poll?

It means the gap between candidates is smaller than the margin of error. The survey cannot say who is truly ahead.

How did Futura’s poll change since 13 October?

On 13 October, Futura had Flávio at 51.8% and Lula at 48.2% of valid votes. The gap has narrowed from 3.6 points to 0.2.

TODAY’S PICK — ELECTION-DAY CULTURE Vote by 5pm, then let the Mostra take over Polls run 8am to 5pm across São Paulo. Check your local school or voting post, bring photo ID, and go early to avoid the lunchtime queue. After voting, the 50th Mostra Internacional de Cinema offers screenings at 57 venues until October 29. Check the official Mostra site or Veja São Paulo’s weekend list for times and tickets. For a simpler afternoon, MASP in Bela Vista is open 10am to 6pm today, R$85 entry and free on Tuesdays. Pinacoteca de São Paulo in Luz is open 10am to 6pm, R$30, and free on Saturdays. Both are indoor, weather-safe choices. The metro fare is R$5.40 exactly. Japan House São Paulo on Avenida Paulista is free to enter; check its opening hours. Good for a short, calm visit after voting.

OUTDOORS — LIGHT SUNDAY Ibirapuera stays open late and free Parque Ibirapuera opens 5am to midnight daily and is free. Sunday afternoon is ideal for a walk or a long bench session. Mercado Municipal (Mercadão) in Centro is open 6am to 4pm on Sundays with free entry. Go early for the mortadella sandwich and the stained glass.

COFFEE & WHERE TO WORK — VILA MADALENA & PINHEIROS Laptop-friendly corners before the rain week Vila Madalena and Pinheiros hold the most reliable weekend laptop spots. Coffee shops with steady WiFi and Sunday hours cluster near Rua Harmonia and Rua dos Pinheiros. Look for places open from late morning to early evening. Avoid anywhere too close to Beco do Batman if you need quiet — it gets busy by midday.

THE CONTRASTING PLAY — WINE WEEKEND FINALE A last glass at Praça Alexandre de Gusmão The 18th Wine Weekend São Paulo runs October 22–25 at Praça Alexandre de Gusmão, near Parque Trianon. Today is its final day. Take the metro to Trianon-MASP and walk a short block.

TONIGHT, AFTER 7 PM Iron Maiden at Nubank Parque Iron Maiden plays Nubank Parque tonight with Alter Bridge opening. The show is sold out — do not travel without a confirmed ticket. For a lower-key evening, the Mostra has evening screenings. Check the festival schedule for late sessions and remaining seats. Vila Madalena works for a quiet dinner after voting queues. Many bars stay open late on Sunday, though quieter than Saturday.

ALSO ON TODAY Iron Maiden with Alter Bridge — Nubank Parque — sold out, evening 50th Mostra Internacional de Cinema — 57 venues citywide — through Oct 29 Wine Weekend São Paulo final day — Praça Alexandre de Gusmão — close at evening MASP — Bela Vista — 10am-6pm, R$85 Pinacoteca de São Paulo — Luz — 10am-6pm, R$30

04

Getting Around

TRANSPORT

The Metrô and CPTM run on Sunday schedules. Rodízio does not operate on Sundays — no license-plate restriction today.

Expect heavier foot traffic near polling stations from 8am to 5pm. Ride apps may surge around voting hours; the metro fare is R$5.40.

05

Where to Eat

LUNCH & DINNER

Lunch: Mercadão’s mortadella sandwich in Centro is the classic vote-day lunch, cheap and filling. For a calmer table, try a per-kilo spot in Vila Mariana near polling stations.

Dinner: Vila Madalena’s Rua Aspicuelta has reliable dinner options without the Saturday frenzy. Pinheiros offers slightly quieter restaurants and better wine lists for a Sunday close.

06

Practical Info

GOOD TO KNOW

Carry photo ID for voting — digital ID works in most states but bring the physical one if you have it. Keep a light jacket for after sunset.

Cards and Pix cover almost everything; bring some cash for street vendors near polling stations. Book museum tickets online where possible to skip queues.

Exercise normal caution near crowded metro exits in Centro during election hours. Pickpockets work dense queues — keep your phone in a front pocket.

07

Community & Lifestyle

FOR NEWCOMERS

Election day is a natural conversation starter in expat WhatsApp and Telegram groups. Many nomads use it to compare voting systems back home.

Look for Sunday meetups in Pinheiros and Vila Madalena. Coffee-shop bulletin boards around Rua dos Pinheiros often list weekday language exchanges.

08

Game Day

THE WEEKEND ROUND

No major São Paulo club fixture dominates today — the city is in election mode. Check Corinthians, Palmeiras, São Paulo FC and Santos channels for midweek training updates.

If a big match does land near evening, two reliable watch spots are Blue Pub in Itaim Bibi and St. James Bar in Moema. Both carry Brazilian league games and have solid screens.

Verify today’s kickoff before heading out. Sunday hours can be thinner than Saturday.

09

Business & Markets

WEEK IN FIGURES

Markets are closed this weekend. On Friday the Ibovespa stock index rose 0.47% to 205,083 and the real strengthened 1.57% to 4.9654 per US dollar.

Mid-October inflation (IPCA-15) rose 0.32% in the month, below the 0.43% analysts expected and the 0.7% of the previous reading (RT economic calendar, RT). The business backdrop is dominated by Brazil’s runoff election.

Results will set the tone for Monday’s opening across currency, equities and the yield curve.

Professional expats should watch for post-election policy signals, not headline moves. The week ahead will be shaped by who accepts what and how quickly institutional transition begins.

10

Plan Ahead

THE WEEK

THE DAYS AHEAD SUN 25 — Vote 8am-5pm, then Mostra or Ibirapuera; Iron Maiden tonight MON 26 — Election aftermath — expect market moves; mild weather for a normal workday TUE 27 — Rain arrives; free MASP day if you can dodge the showers WED 28 — Wet and cooler; Mostra continues — book an evening screening THU 29 — Mostra final day; rain easing slightly

Background: What to Do in São Paulo in October 2026: BTS, Iron Maiden and the Berliner Philharmoniker.

Background: São Paulo Nightlife Tonight: Clarice Falcão, Blue Note.

11

FAQ

QUICK ANSWERS

Do I need to vote if I am a foreign resident?

No. Voting in Brazil is compulsory only for Brazilian citizens. Foreign residents cannot vote. If you hold Brazilian nationality, you must vote or justify your absence. Bring official photo ID to your designated polling place.

What is open on election Sunday?

MASP, Pinacoteca, Japan House, Ibirapuera and Mercadão are open today with the hours listed in the venue status block. Iron Maiden plays sold-out Nubank Parque tonight. The Mostra runs normal Sunday screenings across its venues.

Is the metro running today?

Metrô and CPTM run Sunday schedules; check the operators’ apps for any disruption today. The single-journey metro fare is R$5.40. Rodízio does not apply on Sundays.

Sources: AFP — Brazil election final rallies, Veja São Paulo — weekend programming, Metrópoles — Marvvila with Diogo Nogueira, Songkick — São Paulo metro area events, Shazam — event listing

World.title: Rio de Janeiro Daily Brief — Sunday, October 25, 2026
World.content:
Rio wakes to a mild Sunday ahead of a runoff vote, with the Botanical Garden open for outdoor strolls.

The headline: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and President Lula enter today’s runoff in a statistical tie: Datafolha’s final poll (23–24 October) gave Flávio 51% and Lula 49% of valid votes, within the 2-point margin of error.

Brazilian stocks rose 0.47% on Friday and the real gained 1.57% to 4.9654 per US dollar, while mid-October inflation cooled more than expected.

Your day in one line: vote if registered, then walk the Jardim Botânico’s open-air paths before a soft evening in Botafogo.

03

What to See & Do

SUNDAY IN RIO

TODAY’S PICK — GREEN ESCAPE Vote early, then let the Botanical Garden reset you The Jardim Botânico in Jardim Botânico opens its outdoor paths from 8am to 5pm on Sunday, even during the election weekend. Entry costs R$40 for residents and R$80 for foreigners. Take the Metrô to Botafogo or Antero de Quental, then a short bus or taxi to the garden’s main gate. The single-journey Metrô fare is R$7.90. Inside, the palm avenue and orchid house offer the quietest Sunday reset in the city. Pack water and wear walking shoes. The real pleasure is simple: two hours of shade, imperial palms and no agenda before lunch in Jardim Botânico.

OUTDOORS — COASTAL STRETCH A slow Ipanema-to-Leblon seafront walk If the garden feels too manicured, the seafront ciclovia from Ipanema to Leblon opens to pedestrians and bikes as it does every Sunday. The water sits near 22°C with gentle waves. Start at Praça do Arpoador, climb the rock and watch surfers before coffee in Ipanema. Keep an eye on flags: yellow appeared at some posts.

COFFEE & WHERE TO WORK — BOTAFOGO AND JARDIM BOTÂNICO Quiet corners for a laptop afternoon Botafogo has several laptop-friendly cafés near the Botafogo Metrô station. Check opening hours before you go, as Sunday hours vary. In Jardim Botânico, Coffee Five near the garden’s side entrance works for a post-walk session. Confirm weekend power outlets before settling in.

THE CONTRASTING PLAY — URBAN CULTURE Free art at CCBB and Paço Imperial, no garden needed Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil in Centro opens today from 9am to 8pm, with free entry. Walk through the rotunda galleries, then cross to Paço Imperial, also free, open 12pm to 6pm. This is the day’s indoor counterweight: cool marble, tall rooms and zero sun. Take the VLT or Metrô to Carioca.

TONIGHT, AFTER 7 PM Botafogo bars and a calm close Voting ends at 5pm BRT and results will dominate every screen in the city. Bars in Botafogo, like Bar Urca and Comuna, stay open late with stools facing the television. For a quieter night, Libreria in Jardim Botânico sits two blocks from the garden with a short wine list and no big-screen noise. Avoid driving through Centro after 7pm if first results create crowds around Cinelândia.

ALSO ON TODAY Museu do Amanhã — Praça Mauá, Centro — Thu–Tue 10am–6pm, R$40 (half R$20) Paço Imperial — Centro — Tue–Sun 12pm–6pm, free

04

Getting Around

TRANSPORT

The Metrô single-journey fare is R$7.90; check MetrôRio for Sunday service on Lines 1, 2 and 4. Expect extra passengers near voting centres and avoid rush surges around 8–10am and 4–6pm.

The VLT light rail is the easiest link between Carioca and Praça Mauá. If rain arrives, ride-app prices spike quickly from Botafogo to Zona Sul.

05

Where to Eat

LUNCH & DINNER

Lunch: Try Bráz Pizzaria in Jardim Botânico or CT Boucherie in Leblon for a weekend lunch. Book ahead and check prices on the menus.

Dinner: Bar Urca in Urca offers a harbour view, and Ferro e Farinha in Botafogo is a casual option for a Sunday supper.

06

Practical Info

GOOD TO KNOW

Carry a water bottle, sunscreen and a power bank: voting queues plus garden paths make a long day. Pix and cards work widely, but keep R$40 cash for quick snacks.

Book lunch and dinner tables before 11am — election Sunday fills Zona Sul restaurants by early afternoon.

Stay on lit main roads after dark in Centro; Praça Mauá is busy until 8pm but quieter afterwards.

07

Community & Lifestyle

FOR NEWCOMERS

Expat and nomad groups have paused formal meetups for the election weekend; check the Rio Digital Nomads WhatsApp group now for Monday evening plans.

For newcomers, the easiest plug-in is the Sunday morning run club from Arpoador at 9am — find it via the ‘Rio Runners’ Instagram, not a generic listing.

08

Game Day

ELECTION DAY, NOT MATCH DAY

Football takes a back seat to the presidential runoff in Rio today. Check the clubs’ own channels for Flamengo’s and Fluminense’s next fixtures.

Rio’s public plazas and bars become de facto watch parties from 5pm BRT, when polls close and first results hit screens.

The smarter plan: stay in your own neighbourhood to avoid long cross-town trips as counts come in.

09

Business & Markets

WEEK IN FIGURES

Brazil’s main stock index, the Ibovespa, rose 0.47% to 205,083 on Friday. The real strengthened 1.57% to 4.9654 per US dollar (RT market data).

Mid-October inflation (IPCA-15) rose 0.32% in the month, below the 0.43% analysts expected and the 0.7% of the previous reading, and 4.62% over twelve months against a forecast of 4.73% (RT economic calendar, RT). The central bank’s rate committee, Copom, meets on 3–4 November, and the election is likely to dominate trading until then.

Ahead: Monday’s opening will be the first market test of the runoff result, with investors focused on the winner’s fiscal plans.

10

Plan Ahead

THE WEEK

Background: What to Do in Rio in October 2026.

Background: Rio de Janeiro Nightlife Tonight: Piaf, Fagner, Rockarioca.

11

FAQ

QUICK ANSWERS

When do polls close in Rio today?

Voting runs from 8am to 5pm local time in Rio de Janeiro. Check your polling place and bring photo ID.

Can foreigners vote in Brazil’s runoff?

No. Voting is compulsory only for Brazilian citizens, and foreign residents cannot vote.

How did Brazilian markets close on Friday?

The Ibovespa stock index rose 0.47% to 205,083 and the real strengthened 1.57% to 4.9654 per US dollar. Markets are closed over the weekend.

Sources: Datafolha final poll (23–24 October); Banco Central do Brasil (Copom calendar); RT economic calendar (RT).

World.title: Trump Votes Early in Florida Ahead of Nov. 3
World.content:
An early voting booth at the Madison Parish Courthouse in Tallulah, Louisiana. (Photo: Ktkvtsh, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Key Facts What: Trump voted early in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Saturday, October 24.

Who: He said he voted a straight Republican ticket; Melania Trump voted too.

Polls: A New York Times/Siena poll has Democrats ahead 52% to 41% for the House.

Prediction markets: Polymarket: Democrats win the House 92%, the Senate 67% (read evening of October 24, ET).

Next: Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

This story is part of our coverage of the 2026 US midterm elections. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Obama and Trump Hold Rival Midterm Rallies

Published Saturday, October 24, 11:28 p.m. ET (Washington)

President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump voted early in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Saturday, October 24, 2026, ten days before the midterm elections. Asked whether he voted a straight Republican ticket, Trump replied “Very much so,” according to Newsweek.

The vote comes as Democrats lead in national polling and betting markets for the House. Our US midterms 2026 dossier tracks the race to November 3.

In plain English Midterms are national elections held halfway through a president’s four-year term. On November 3, Americans decide control of Congress: all 435 House seats and 35 of 100 Senate seats.

Trump Votes Early in Florida

The Trumps cast their ballots at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office in West Palm Beach, according to Newsweek. Trump then travelled to Georgia for a rally in Perry, which was moved there from Macon, with remarks at 7 p.m. ET.

Early voting is already under way in many states. Our report on the 20 million early ballots counted so far gives the wider picture.

File photo: voters queue for early voting in Metairie, Louisiana.

Where the Race Stands

A New York Times/Siena poll of likely voters, released October 21, found Democratic House candidates ahead 52% to 41%. The same poll put President Trump’s approval at 36% among likely voters.

Polls are snapshots, not forecasts, and the Senate map is harder for Democrats than the House map. Republicans start with a 53 to 47 Senate majority.

What Prediction Markets Say

House: Polymarket priced a Democratic win at 92%, with about US$21.3 million traded.

Polymarket priced a Democratic win at 92%, with about US$21.3 million traded. Senate: Polymarket priced Democratic control at 67%, with about US$9.0 million traded.

These prices are real-money bets, not polls, and they can move quickly. Kalshi, a market regulated in the US by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), also lists House contracts.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

With the final week and a half of campaigning ahead, the president’s own vote underlines how much he is staking on turnout. For readers watching tariffs, sanctions or migration policy, a Democratic House would give opposition leaders control of investigations and the federal budget process.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether Democrats will turn their polling lead into a House majority, or whether they can win the Senate. Betting prices can shift before November 3 and are not evidence that either party has won.

Frequently Asked Questions

When did Donald Trump vote in the 2026 midterms?

He voted early in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Saturday, October 24, 2026, with Melania Trump, according to Newsweek.

When is the 2026 US midterm election?

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are on the ballot.

What do prediction markets say about the midterms?

Polymarket priced a Democratic House win at 92% and Democratic Senate control at 67% on the evening of October 24. These are bets, not forecasts or results.

World.title: Mercedes Delays F1 Engine Upgrade to Brazil
World.content:
Key Facts Driver: George Russell has used his full engine allocation, so new parts would bring a grid penalty.

Circuit: Autódromo José Carlos Pace, Interlagos, São Paulo, Brazil; 4.309 km, 71 laps.

Race date: Sunday, 8 November 2026, at 14:00 Brasília time (12:00 noon ET).

Qualifying: Saturday, 7 November 2026, at 15:00 Brasília time (13:00 ET).

Status: Mercedes has not confirmed the upgrade will debut at Interlagos.

This story is part of our coverage of the São Paulo Grand Prix 2026. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Ferrari May Field Brazilian at Interlagos

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 79.8% · Lula 20.5% (US$197 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 82% · Lula 19% As of 25 October, 1:20 am ET (05:20 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them. Want prediction market reports on Brazil? Get yours free, right after you confirm →

What Happened

Mercedes did not bring its revised engine to this weekend’s United States Grand Prix at Circuit of the Americas in Austin (23–25 October 2026). Reports say it is also unlikely to be ready for the Mexican Grand Prix, which leaves the São Paulo Grand Prix 2026 as the earliest likely debut.

Mercedes has not confirmed that the upgrade will be available at Interlagos, nor that Russell will take any related grid penalty there. Reports describe the engine as not yet ready, and the team has given no new date.

The Interlagos circuit in São Paulo during the 2022 Grand Prix weekend. File photo: Governo do Estado de São Paulo, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

The circuit is Autódromo José Carlos Pace, Interlagos, São Paulo. The race is the Formula 1 MSC Cruises Grande Prêmio de São Paulo 2026, Round 20 of the championship.

Dates And Times

The official Formula 1 schedule lists Practice 1 on Friday, 6 November 2026, from 12:30 to 13:30 Brasília time, which is 10:30 to 11:30 ET. Practice 2 follows the same day from 16:00 to 17:00 Brasília time, or 14:00 to 15:00 ET.

On Saturday, 7 November, Practice 3 runs from 11:30 to 12:30 Brasília time, or 09:30 to 10:30 ET, with qualifying from 15:00 to 16:00 Brasília time, or 13:00 to 14:00 ET. The race starts Sunday, 8 November, at 14:00 Brasília time, which is 12:00 noon ET.

Strategic Context

The Mercedes upgrade is being developed under Formula 1’s Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities framework. Mercedes has not named a race for the debut.

For Russell, combining the upgrade with a planned component-related penalty could make São Paulo strategically attractive, but that remains speculation rather than a confirmed team decision. The Race reported in September that Russell’s penalty is being deferred to coincide with the upgrade.

What It Means for US Readers

For US viewers, the São Paulo Grand Prix starts at 12:00 noon Eastern Time on Sunday, 8 November 2026. Qualifying is at 13:00 ET on Saturday, 7 November, after US clocks go back on 1 November.

The race remains on the official Formula 1 calendar as Round 20 of the season. Practice 1 begins on Friday, 6 November.

What Is Not Known

Whether Mercedes will actually debut the upgraded engine at Interlagos remains unconfirmed. The team has not announced a decision on Russell’s power-unit components or any associated grid penalty.

No live prediction-market odds or named-institute poll specific to the São Paulo Grand Prix were identified in the available recent reports. The team has also not announced a date for the debut.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the 2026 São Paulo Grand Prix?

The race is Sunday, 8 November 2026, at 14:00 Brasília time, which is 12:00 noon Eastern Time. Qualifying is Saturday, 7 November, at 15:00 Brasília time, or 13:00 ET.

Will Mercedes use its upgraded engine in São Paulo?

Mercedes has not confirmed that the revised power unit will debut at Interlagos. The team did not bring the upgrade to the United States Grand Prix, and reports say Mexico is unlikely, which makes São Paulo the earliest likely but unconfirmed debut.

Could George Russell receive a grid penalty in São Paulo?

Russell has already used his permitted allocation of engine, turbo, energy store and control electronics, so any new component would bring a grid penalty. Mercedes has not confirmed whether that will happen at Interlagos.

World.title: France Detains Nearly 1,000 at Protests
World.content:
File photo: the Palais Bourbon in Paris, home of the National Assembly. (Photo: Jebulon, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Police detained nearly 1,000 people across France on Saturday, 24 October, during a second weekend of nationwide protests, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said. We follow the unrest in our Europe political crisis coverage.

The Interior Ministry counted about 410,000 marchers, while the CGT union put the number at about 800,000. For US readers, France is a NATO ally and a major economy, so a long crisis there reaches trade, security and Ukraine policy.

Key Facts Detentions: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez reported nearly 1,000 people detained in France, with the figure expected to rise.

Police: About 70,000 police and gendarmes were deployed across the country.

Turnout: The Interior Ministry counted about 410,000; the CGT union said about 800,000.

Next date: The CGT and other unions have called a strike for 5 November.

Beyond France: Italian police took 371 people in for questioning on Saturday, and Albania’s protests have left 320 injured since 13 October.

This story is part of our coverage of the europe political crisis. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Serbia Votes Sunday, Ruling List Favored

Nearly 1,000 Detained in France

Police detained nearly 1,000 people on Saturday, 24 October, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, who expected the number to rise. Police used tear gas and water cannon in Paris, and tear gas in Limoges.

About 70,000 police and gendarmes were deployed nationwide. Nuñez said most marches went well, although shops were looted in some cities.

The Interior Ministry counted about 410,000 demonstrators nationwide, including 110,000 in Paris. The CGT union said about 800,000 took part nationally and 250,000 in the capital, so the two counts remain far apart.

File photo: protest placards in Paris on 17 October 2026, a week before the latest march.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on France in Turmoil Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

A Strike Set for 5 November

The CGT union has called a strike for 5 November, and other unions have joined the call. It was announced after unions met Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on 21 October.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the left-wing party La France Insoumise, said it was time for President Emmanuel Macron to yield. He added that after that, only the exit door would remain.

The Interior Ministry counted about 550,000 marchers on the previous Saturday, 17 October, so this weekend’s count is lower. The CGT’s own figure was about 800,000 on both days.

Italy and Albania Also See Protests

In Italy, police said they made nine arrests and took 371 people in for questioning on Saturday, 110 of them minors. Marches took place in cities including Milan, Rome, Turin, Bologna and Florence.

Albania’s protests are older and separate. Its health ministry counted 320 people injured between 13 and 21 October, including 192 police officers.

Grievances differ by country, so these are separate protests, not one coordinated movement.

What It Means for US Readers

France is a NATO ally and the European Union’s second-largest economy. A long political crisis in Paris could complicate transatlantic coordination on trade, security and Ukraine.

A strike wave could also disrupt European transport and supply chains that US companies rely on. The next test is the 5 November strike.

What Is Not Known

The final French detention total is not known, because Nuñez expected it to rise. Turnout remains disputed, with the ministry and the CGT about 390,000 apart.

It is not known whether the government will make concessions or how many people will join the strike. We found no fresh national poll and no active prediction market on the French protests.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people protested in France on 24 October?

The Interior Ministry counted about 410,000 demonstrators nationwide, including 110,000 in Paris. The CGT union said about 800,000 nationally and 250,000 in Paris.

How many people were detained in France?

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said nearly 1,000 people were detained and expected the figure to rise. The final total was not known.

Is there a strike planned in France?

The CGT and other unions have called a strike for 5 November. Jean-Luc Mélenchon of La France Insoumise said it was time for President Macron to yield.

What happened in Italy and Albania?

Italian police took 371 people in for questioning on Saturday, 110 of them minors. In Albania, 320 people were injured between 13 and 21 October, according to the health ministry.

What happens next in France?

The strike called for 5 November is the next fixed date. No government concessions had been reported.
